## **18. Phase 3 — GA4 Web Analytics, Leads, ROAS/CAC**

> Section ini scope terluas: butuh GA4 property baru (belum pernah ada di SatuInbox), lead capture form baru, dan cross-collection join (ads spend × subscription revenue). Jangan mulai sebelum Phase 2 selesai — masing masing bagian di bawah independen, bisa dikerjakan paralel/terpisah.

### **18.1 Problem**

Phase 1+2 cover funnel Register→Verified→Subscription dan cost per-campaign (Spend, CPL). Belum bisa jawab:
- Berapa **visitor** yang datang ke landing page SatuInbox sebelum register? (funnel Visitor→Register→Leads)
- Berapa **Leads** (orang minta demo, belum daftar)?
- Berapa **Total/New/Active User** berbasis web traffic (GA4) — beda dari Register count?
- **ROAS** (revenue per rupiah spend) dan **CAC** (cost per paying customer) — bukan cuma cost per lead

### **18.2 Gap Ditemukan (grep FE repo)**

| Cek | Hasil |
|-----|-------|
| GA4/gtag.js terpasang di FE | ❌ **Tidak ada** — grep `gtag`, `googletagmanager`, `G-XXXXXXX` di seluruh `omnichannel-satuinbox-fe` nihil |
| Auth schema punya `lastLoginAt`/`lastActiveAt` | ❌ **Tidak ada** — schema hanya punya `createdAt`, `emailVerifiedAt` |
| Request Demo / lead capture form | ❌ **Tidak ada** — grep `RequestDemo`, `leadCapture` nihil di FE maupun BE |

Kesimpulan: Phase 3 bukan "tambah kolom dashboard" — perlu instrumentasi baru di 3 tempat berbeda.

### **18.3 Scope Phase 3 (3 sub-bagian independen)**

**A. GA4 Web Analytics**
| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Setup | Buat GA4 property baru di Google Analytics, pasang `gtag.js` di landing page SatuInbox (bukan di app dashboard — app butuh login, GA4 buat visitor publik) |
| Metrik ditarik | `totalUsers`, `newUsers`, `activeUsers` (GA4 native — definisi GA4: session dalam 5 menit terakhir), `sessions`, `engagementRate` |
| API | GA4 Data API (`analyticsdata.googleapis.com`) — Service Account credential, bukan OAuth user |
| Funnel stage terisi | **Visitor** (dari GA4 `totalUsers`/`sessions` di halaman landing sebelum register) |

**B. Leads (Request Demo)**
| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| FE | Form baru "Request Demo" di landing page (bukan bagian register flow) — field minimal: nama, email, perusahaan, phone |
| BE | Collection baru `demo_requests` — **bukan sales module** (dari koreksi user sebelumnya: sales tidak relevan). Endpoint terpisah di analytics-service atau service baru kecil |
| UTM | Sama seperti register — capture `utm_source/campaign/content` dari URL saat submit form |
| Funnel stage terisi | **Leads** (Visitor → Register → Leads, sesuai urutan yang diminta user — dicatat sebagai alternate/parallel path ke Register, bukan strictly sequential) |

**C. ROAS & CAC (cross-collection join)**
| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Prasyarat | Phase 2 selesai (`ads_performance.spend` per campaign harus ada) |
| Join | `ads_performance` (spend by campaign+date) ⋈ `auths.marketingSource` (siapa register dari campaign) ⋈ `subscriptions` (siapa bayar + `pricePerUnit`) |
| ROAS formula | `SUM(subscription revenue attributed to campaign) / SUM(ad spend campaign)` |
| CAC formula | `SUM(ad spend campaign) / COUNT(DISTINCT paying customer dari campaign itu)` |
| Limitation | Attribution model **last-touch** (keputusan Phase 1) — kalau user daftar dari Google Ads tapi upgrade subscription 3 bulan kemudian tanpa UTM baru, tetap di-attribute ke Google Ads original. Revenue jangka panjang (LTV) di luar scope. |

### **18.4 Active User — 2 Definisi Ditampilkan Terpisah**

Diputuskan tampilkan keduanya, bukan pilih salah satu — beda pertanyaan yang dijawab:

| Label di Dashboard | Sumber | Definisi |
|---|---|---|
| **Active User (Web)** | GA4 `activeUsers` | Orang yang buka website/landing page SatuInbox (visitor, belum tentu customer) |
| **Active User (Produk)** | Auth collection, field baru `lastLoginAt` | Customer yang benar-benar login ke aplikasi SatuInbox |

**FR baru:** Auth schema perlu tambah `@Prop({ type: Date }) lastLoginAt?: Date` — di-update setiap kali login sukses (auth-service login handler). Field kecil, dampak minim, tapi WAJIB untuk Active User (Produk) — tanpa ini datanya tidak ada sama sekali.

Ads Efficiency: Klik │ Impression │ CPM │ CTR │ CPR │ ROAS │ CAC │ Total Spend

User Journey:   Total User (GA4) │ New User (GA4) │ Active User Web (GA4) │ Active User Produk (Auth.lastLoginAt)
```

### **18.6 Phase 3 User Stories**

| ID | Priority | User Story | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|----------|------------|-------------------|
| US-P3-001 | P0 | As a **marketing team**, I want to see Visitor count from GA4 before Register so that I understand top-of-funnel drop-off. | 1. Given GA4 property terpasang, When dashboard load, Then funnel menampilkan Visitor → Register → Leads dengan conversion % antar step. |
| US-P3-002 | P0 | As a **marketing team**, I want a Request Demo form separate from registration so that leads who aren't ready to sign up are still captured. | 1. Given user submit form Request Demo, Then data tersimpan di `demo_requests` dengan UTM attribution. 2. Given form di-submit tanpa UTM, Then tetap tersimpan tanpa marketingSource. |
| US-P3-003 | P1 | As a **marketing team**, I want to see ROAS and CAC per campaign so that I can evaluate real revenue efficiency, not just lead cost. | 1. Given campaign punya spend dan subscription revenue terhubung, When dashboard load, Then ROAS dan CAC dihitung dan ditampilkan. 2. Given campaign belum ada subscription terhubung, Then tampilkan "—" bukan 0 atau error. |
| US-P3-004 | P1 | As a **super admin**, I want to see both web-based and product-based Active User counts so that I can distinguish site traffic from real product usage. | 1. Given GA4 dan Auth.lastLoginAt tersedia, When dashboard load, Then dua kartu terpisah ditampilkan: "Active User (Web)" dan "Active User (Produk)". |

### **18.7 Dependencies & Effort — Phase 3**

| Dependency | Owner | Catatan |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| GA4 property + gtag.js di landing page | Marketing/FE | Property baru — belum pernah ada, mulai dari nol |

### **18.8 Terminology Correction (dari referensi Lincah report)**

| Istilah user | Istilah benar/klarifikasi |

| "CPM (cost per mail)" | **Cost Per Mille** — biaya per 1.000 impression, bukan "mail". Standar istilah ads industry. |

workPackages.subject: Redash data source 5 points at decommissioned MongoDB Atlas cluster (NXDOMAIN)
workPackages.description:
Redash data source id 5 points at a decommissioned MongoDB Atlas cluster (`devcluster.s3b2jx.mongodb.net`). DNS resolution for its SRV record returns NXDOMAIN from every resolver checked (local, 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1):

```
$ nslookup -type=SRV _mongodb._tcp.devcluster.s3b2jx.mongodb.net 8.8.8.8
** server can't find _mongodb._tcp.devcluster.s3b2jx.mongodb.net: NXDOMAIN
```

This surfaced via #3644 (Analytics - Ticket KPI card not showed), where `GET /api/analytics/ticket/counts` returned HTTP 500. The BE fix in that ticket (MR !761) removes ticket analytics' dependency on Redash entirely, but **14 other exported queries still use data_source_id: 5**:

```
$ grep -l '"data_source_id": 5' redash-queries-export/*.json | wc -l
15   # (was 15 including ticket count; 14 remain after !761)
```

Those queries back conversation, member, and other analytics cards still routed through `RedashService` (`apps/analytics-service/src/app/services/redash.service.ts`) — any of them will 500 with the same `Query failed: ...` -> `GrpcInternalException` pattern whenever they execute against this dead source.

**Action needed (Redash admin, not app code):**
1. Log into the Redash UI
2. Settings -> Data Sources -> data source id 5
3. Update its connection string to point at the current MongoDB target (local dev cluster or a live Atlas replacement, whichever prod actually uses now)
4. Re-run the affected queries to confirm they resolve

**Likely root cause:** the app's own `.env` was migrated off the old Atlas cluster to a different target, but Redash's data source config (stored in Redash's own DB, not this repo) was never updated to match.

Related: #3644, MR !761 (https://gitlab.com/lolipad.id/omnichannel-satuinbox-be/-/merge_requests/761)

workPackages.subject: Duplicate accountChannel array entries + duplicate ConversationSLAMetrics rows on same conversation
workPackages.description:
**Symptom**: a single widget conversation (`_id: 6a0ad6042661fd25c7a3eb73`, channel "Pengirim 06") ended up with 14 identical-`id` entries in its `accountChannel[]` array, each differing only in `lastSyncedAt`/`channel.lastSyncedAt`, all created within ~11 seconds on 2026-05-18. The same conversation also produced a duplicate `ConversationSLAMetrics` row.

**Root causes identified (conversation-service, `omnichannel-satuinbox-be`)**

1. `ConversationRepository.addAccountChannelsToConversation` / `moveAccountChannelsToEndOfConversation` (`conversation.repository.ts`, introduced by commit `497b44ccb` on 2026-06-08) implement "replace existing entry with same id" as TWO separate, non-atomic Mongo calls (`updateOne $pull` then `findOneAndUpdate $push`). Under overlapping/concurrent invocations for the same conversationId+channelId, every call's `$pull` runs before any `$push` lands, so all calls see "nothing to remove" and all `$push` — producing N duplicates. The docstring incorrectly claims this is "atomic at the document level"; it is not.

2. Before that commit (2026-02-13, `19d6e60a4`), the same method used `$addToSet`, which only dedupes byte-for-byte identical subdocuments — not by `id`. Since `lastSyncedAt` is refreshed on every fetch, `$addToSet` never recognized repeat adds of the same channel as duplicates and always appended. This conversation's 14 duplicates (all dated 2026-05-18, before the June 8 change) are attributable to this earlier variant of the bug, not the later race — the defect class has been continuously present since Feb 13, just changing failure mode in June.

3. `ConversationSLAMetricsRepository.createMetrics` (`conversation-sla-metrics.repository.ts:133`) is a bare, unconditional insert with no existence check and no upsert — unlike the sibling `upsertMetrics` a few lines below. It's invoked by `initiateSLATracking` from 3 call sites in `conversation.service.ts` (conversation creation, `reopenConversation`, and `handleUnjunkConversation`'s in-place revert for WIDGET/WHATSAPP_API — this conversation is `isJunked: true` on a WIDGET channel, matching that third path exactly) with no guard against a metrics row already existing for the conversationId. Only the schema's `unique: true` index on `conversationId` (`conversation-sla-metrics.schema.ts:273`) stands between this and a duplicate row — if that index isn't actually enforced on the live collection, duplicates persist silently instead of throwing.

**Most likely upstream trigger for the 14 repeated adds**: `TEAM_ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_ADDED` (emitted from `people-service/team.service.ts` `dispatchAccountChannelDiffEvents`), whose diff computation (`findNewAccountChannelIds`) is itself a non-atomic read-then-decide (reads team's current channel list, diffs, then writes+emits) with no locking. If the "update team channels" call for this team+channel was invoked several times in quick, overlapping succession (double-submit on the FE settings page, a retry storm, or a provisioning loop), every overlapping call reads the same pre-update team state and independently concludes "this channel is new," each emitting its own `TEAM_ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_ADDED`. Not confirmed from static code alone — needs people-service logs around 2026-05-18T09:03–09:04Z for accountChannelId `69e8790bc893d7b36d4e0379`, or a check of the FE's channel-assignment settings component for a multi-submit bug.

**Suggested fixes**
- Collapse `addAccountChannelsToConversation`/`moveAccountChannelsToEndOfConversation` into a single atomic pipeline `updateOne` (`$filter` + `$concatArrays` in one op) instead of pull-then-push.
- Make `createMetrics` an atomic `findOneAndUpdate(..., { upsert: true })` keyed on `conversationId`, like `upsertMetrics` already does.
- Verify the `conversationId` unique index actually exists on the live `conversationslametrics` collection; backfill/rebuild if not.
- Harden `findNewAccountChannelIds`/`replaceMembersAndUpdateTeam` against overlapping calls (e.g. a conditional update keyed on a version/lastModified check, or dedupe on the emit side).
- Write a backfill script to find and clean up existing duplicate `accountChannel` entries and duplicate `ConversationSLAMetrics` rows across the DB.

No fix implemented yet — this ticket covers the investigation; a follow-up MR should implement the fixes above.

workPackages.subject: Improvement RMQ issue
workPackages.description:
USE CASE STUCK

Kenapa "stuck lagi" (memory alarm kembali)  
Dua penyumbang memori terbesar:  
1\. mnesia: 1.92GB (58.6%) — metadata banyak queue/koneksi  
2\. binary: 1.13GB (34.5%) — payload pesan + overhead koneksi  
Pemicu alarm: 264 koneksi + 409 channel + banyak queue terus menahan metadata (mnesia) di ~1.9GB. Begitu ada burst pesan, binary naik, total melewati threshold 3.26GB → alarm → publisher diblokir → memori turun → alarm clear → ulang. Flapping terus.  
Yang penting untuk kamu

*   ✅ instagram-token-refresh sudah 0 unacked — masalah IG lama sudah bersih
    
*   ❌ Broker kekurangan kapasitas memori — bukan rusak, tapi kewalahan oleh banyaknya koneksi/queue pada VM m6i.large (8GB)
    
*   Restart broker tidak akan menyelesaikan ini — memori akan naik lagi begitu traffic masuk, karena penyebabnya volume koneksi itu sendiri
    

Satu-satunya solusi permanen (bukan restart)  
1\. Naikkan batas memori container + vm\_memory\_high\_watermark (tinggal sedikit headroom — berisiko, tapi bisa)  
2\. Kurangi 264 koneksi dengan connection pooling di aplikasi (paling efektif)  
3\. Upgrade VM ke yang lebih besar RAM (m6i.xlarge 16GB) — ruang gerak paling nyaman  
4\. Pindahkan Redash (~1.4GB) ke server lain untuk membebaskan RAM host  
Restart lagi sekarang hanya akan "menang sementara" beberapa menit sebelum alarm kembali. Mau saya bahas solusi mana yang paling cocok, atau tetap restart sekarang juga?

Pola sudah jelas:

*   264 koneksi semuanya user admin
    
*   Tersebar dari banyak host berbeda (33, 31, 31 di beberapa node pertama)
    

Ini sangat khas: setiap pod Kubernetes / instance aplikasi membuka koneksi sendiri tanpa pooling, lalu saat aplikasi scale-up (banyak pod), koneksi ikut banyak. 264 koneksi untuk 119 consumer = ~2+ koneksi per consumer.  
Sekarang saya beri tahu cara nomor 2 (connection pooling) — ini perubahan di sisi aplikasi konsumen, bukan di server RabbitMQ.  
Cara nomor 2: Kurangi koneksi dengan Connection Pooling  
Konsep intinya  
Sekarang, tiap pod aplikasi buka 1 koneksi per channel per task. Yang benar: 1 koneksi dipakai bersama oleh banyak channel (AMQP channel itu murah, koneksi yang mahal).  
Karena aplikasinya Node.js (dari client properties: amqplib)  
Sebelum (boros — buat koneksi baru tiap consumer):  
async function consume(queue) {  
  const conn = await amqp.connect(URL);   // BUKA koneksi baru  
  const ch = await conn.createChannel();  
  await ch.assertQueue(queue);  
  ch.consume(queue, handler);  
}  
→ 4 queue × beberapa pod = banyak koneksi  
Sesudah (pakai 1 koneksi global + channel per consumer):  
// Satu koneksi untuk seluruh aplikasi/pod  
let conn;  
async function getConn() {  
  if (!conn) conn = await amqp.connect(URL);  
  return conn;  
}

async function consume(queue, handler) {  
  const c = await getConn();          // REUSE koneksi yang sama  
  const ch = await c.createChannel(); // channel murah, ndak masalah banyak  
  await ch.assertQueue(queue);  
  ch.consume(queue, handler);  
}  
Dengan begitu, setiap pod hanya pakai 1 koneksi (bukan 1 per queue), tambah semua consumer di dalamnya.  
Kalau ingin lebih mudah / terpusat (tanpa ubah banyak file)

*   Pakai library yang sudah handle pooling: amqp-connection-manager (Node.js) — sangat populer untuk kasus ini.
    

npm i amqp-connection-manager  
const amqp = require('amqp-connection-manager');  
const broker = amqp.connect(URL);         // satu koneksi  
const channel = broker.createChannel();   // reuse, otomatis reconnect  
Estimasi dampak

*   Dari 264 koneksi → puluhan koneksi (≈ jumlah pod × 1)
    
*   Memori mnesia + binary akan turun drastis karena tidak lagi menyimpan metadata ratusan koneksi
    
*   Alarm memory berhenti flapping
    

aanalisa ---------------

Analisa pooling-nya bener arahnya, tapi ada cacat hitungan yg bikin ekspektasi kamu ketinggian. Gw luruskan sebelum kamu janji "turun drastis" ke infra.  
Cacat #1: 264 conn ≠ penyumbang mnesia 1.92GB  
Metadata 264 koneksi di mnesia itu kecil—orde belasan MB, bukan ratusan MB apalagi GB. Turunin 264→30 koneksi ga akan bikin mnesia 1.92GB anjlok "drastis". Mnesia 1.92GB itu queue + binding + message durable, bukan conn metadata.  
Jadi klaim _"memori mnesia + binary akan turun drastis"_ = salah. Yg turun dari pooling:

*   binary turun sedikit (TCP buffer per conn: ~100-200KB × 234 conn hilang ≈ 25-45MB)
    
*   mnesia nyaris ga gerak
    

Pooling bukan solusi memory alarm. Pooling nyelesein hal lain (lihat bawah).  
Cacat #2: "264 conn / 119 consumer = 2+ conn per consumer" → salah baca  
amqplib 1 koneksi = banyak channel. 264 conn dari banyak pod itu artinya tiap pod buka koneksi baru per consumer/task, bukan 2 conn per consumer. Diagnosa kamu (no pooling per-pod) bener, cuma framing angkanya keliru. Ga ngubah kesimpulan.  
Yg sebenernya pooling selesein

Memory alarm (mnesia 1.92GB) > ❌ Nyaris nol  
Binary 1.13GB > ⚠️ Turun ~30-45MB doang  
Broker CPU/scheduler overhead (264 conn = 264 TCP loop, heartbeat, flow-control) > ✅ Ya, signifikan  
Risiko file descriptor / conn limit saat scale-up > ✅ Ya  
Kestabilan reconnect > ✅ Ya (`amqp-connection-manager`)

Pooling = higienis & benar jangka panjang, tapi bukan yg matiin alarm memory sekarang.  
Yg matiin alarm memory (root cause tetap di queue)  
mnesia 1.92GB + binary 1.13GB = message numpuk di queue. Itu 2.05GB dari total 3.28GB. Kill itu = alarm mati. Urutan bener:

*   `list_queues name messages messages_ready messages_unacked memory consumers` — cari queue gemuk (belum kamu kasih; ini penentu, bukan conn breakdown)
    
*   Set policy pagar — ini yg permanen:
    

`rabbitmqctl set_policy mem-guard "." \`  
`'{"max-length":50000,"message-ttl":3600000,"queue-mode":"lazy"}' \`  
`--apply-to queues`

`lazy` = message ke disk, ga nahan RAM. `max-length`+`ttl` = batas atas. RAM ga bisa naik tanpa batas lagi.

*   Pooling — kerjain paralel, tapi jual ke infra sebagai _"nurunin broker CPU + stabilitas scale-up"_, bukan _"nurunin memory"_. Kalau dijual sebagai fix memory, alarm balik, kamu yg kena.
    

Verdict  
Kamu udah dikasih conn breakdown, tapi belum dikasih `list_queues` per-memory. Itu satu-satunya angka yg nentuin alarm mati atau ngga. Conn breakdown penting buat pooling (masalah beda), tapi ga nyentuh alarm.

workPackages.subject: v2.8.1 regression: conversation create writes stub contactInfo ({id} only) and no createdAt
workPackages.description:
**Regression introduced by #3252** (commit `c595440c` "fix: make accountChannel replace and SLA metrics creation atomic"), shipped in **v2.8.1**. Not present in v2.8.0.3.

## Symptom

Conversations created on v2.8.1 persist a **stub `contactInfo`** — only the `id`, with every other field silently dropped:

```
contactInfo: {
  "id": { "$oid": "6a7744babf2f8f9d761ff7ce" },
  "lastSyncedAt": { "$date": "2026-09-01T01:27:07.727Z" }
}
```

Expected (and what v2.8.0.3 wrote):

```
contactInfo: {
  "id": ..., "referenceId": "628123456789@c.us", "displayName": "Jane Doe",
  "phone": "+628123456789", "phoneLast4": "6789", "email": "jane@example.com",
  "lastSyncedAt": ...
}
```

`lastSyncedAt` survives only because the subdocument schema declares `@Prop({ default: Date.now })` (`conversation.schema.ts:197`). Mongoose fills that default; nothing else is written.

## Root cause

`ConversationRepository.buildCreateConversationUpdate` (`apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/conversation.repository.ts:2869`).

#3252 replaced the `$addToSet` + `$setOnInsert` update with an **aggregation-pipeline update**. Pipeline updates cannot use `$setOnInsert`, so insert-only semantics were emulated per-field (`conversation.repository.ts:2880`):

```ts
acc[field] = { $ifNull: [`$${field}`, value] };
```

On an upsert, MongoDB **seeds the new document from the equality terms of the query filter** before running the pipeline. `buildCreateConversationQuery` (`conversation.repository.ts:2947`) filters on:

```ts
'contactInfo.id': contactInfo?.id,
status: ConversationStatusEnum.OPEN,
```

so the seed document already contains `contactInfo: { id: ... }`. `$ifNull` therefore sees `$contactInfo` as non-null and **keeps the stub**, discarding the full object built by `normalizeContact()` (`utils/formatter.util.ts:90`).

Verified with a probe — on insert, inside the pipeline, `$$ROOT` is exactly `["contactInfo", "status"]` and `$contactInfo` is already `{ id: ... }`.

The per-field `$ifNull` emulation is only equivalent to `$setOnInsert` for fields that never appear in the upsert filter. `contactInfo` and `status` both do.

## Second defect, same line: `createdAt` is never written

Pipeline updates also bypass Mongoose's insert-time timestamp handling:

```
v2.8.1     createdAt -> undefined
           keys: _id, accountChannel, companyId, contactInfo, organizationId, status, updatedAt
v2.8.0.3   createdAt -> 2026-09-01T02:10:04.894Z   (plus __v)
```

**Every conversation created on v2.8.1 has no `createdAt`.** `ConversationAggregationService.buildBaseMatch` (`services/conversation-aggregation.service.ts:547`) matches `createdAt: { $gte: dateStart, $lt: dateEnd }` — so these conversations are **invisible to every Statistic KPI card**, and equally to the #3156 drill-downs, which deliberately mirror that same match. `__v` is also absent.

## Evidence / reproduction

Reproduced against a real `mongod` (mongo:7) and again through real Mongoose 8.18.1, running both update shapes over an identical payload:

```
v2.8.0.3 ($setOnInsert):
  contactInfo -> {"id":"...","referenceId":"628123456789@c.us","displayName":"Jane Doe",
                  "phone":"+628...6789","phoneLast4":"6789","email":"jane@example.com",
                  "lastSyncedAt":"2026-09-01T01:27:07.727Z"}

v2.8.1 (pipeline + $ifNull):
  contactInfo -> {"id":"6a7744babf2f8f9d761ff7ce"}
```

Matches the production document exactly.

## Blast radius

- Both branches of the create path — `isGroup: false` (filters `accountChannel` + `contactInfo.id`) and `isGroup: true` (filters `channel.id` + `contactInfo.id`).
- `status` is likewise stubbed from the filter (benign today: the stub value equals the intended value).
- `channel` survives on the non-group path only because the filter does not key on it. On the **group** path the filter keys on `'channel.id'`, so `channel` is reduced to `{ id }` and loses `name` / `platform`.
- Downstream: contact search/filter clauses read `contactInfo.displayName` / `.phone` / `.phoneLast4` / `.email` (`conversation.repository.ts:799-803`, Atlas clauses `:892-895`); the livechat transcript subject falls back through `conversation.contactInfo?.displayName`. All degrade for affected conversations.

## Proposed fix

Gate insert-only semantics on **document** existence rather than **per-field** existence, and set timestamps explicitly since Mongoose will not:

```ts
f[k] = { $cond: [{ $gt: ['$createdAt', null] }, { $ifNull: ['$' + k, v] }, { $literal: v }] };
```

The guard must be `createdAt` — `$_id` and `$companyId` both read as ABSENT inside the pipeline on insert, so they cannot distinguish insert from match. Verified on both `isGroup` branches: full `contactInfo` is written on insert, a user-edited field on a second matching create is still not clobbered, and `accountChannel` stays deduped at exactly 1 entry (i.e. #3252's original fix is preserved).

## Backfill required

Conversations already created on v2.8.1 need repair — re-populate `contactInfo` from the contacts collection by `contactInfo.id`, and set `createdAt` from the `_id` generation timestamp. Same for `channel` on group conversations. Until that runs, affected conversations stay missing from all Statistic figures.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy v2.8.1.
2. Send an inbound message from a contact with no existing OPEN conversation (any platform; widget/WhatsApp both hit `buildCreatePayload`).
3. Inspect the created `conversations` document.
4. `contactInfo` contains only `id` + `lastSyncedAt`; `createdAt` and `__v` are absent.
5. Open any Statistic KPI card for a range covering the creation date — the conversation is not counted.

workPackages.subject: Add RLT SLA breakdown (slaRltSuccess) — full parity with FRT/TTC
workPackages.description:
RLT (Response Lead Time) has a computed value (`rltMs`) since #3226, but no SLA-success concept — unlike FRT and TTC, which each have a configurable threshold, a computed boolean (`slaFrtSuccess`/`slaTtcSuccess`), and a real-time "In SLA / Over SLA" breakdown card on the Statistic page. This ticket gives RLT full parity: a new `SLASettingMetricEnum.RESPONSE_LEAD_TIME` configurable via the existing admin Settings → SLA form, a `slaRltSuccess` boolean computed alongside `rltMs`, and a 3rd card in both the Settings "SLA Definitions" info section and the Statistic page's SLA Breakdown section.

Conversation-only (no `TICKET_RLT` SLA breakdown, no Redash query for the legacy `AGGREGATION_ENABLED=false` path — that path shows a zeroed RLT breakdown by design).

**Scope**:
- Backend: `SLASettingResolverService` fallback chain (channel override → tenant default → system default) extended with an `rlt` branch; `ConversationSLAMetrics` schema gains `rltSnapshotConfiguredMs`/`slaRltSuccess`; `handleAgentReplied` computes `slaRltSuccess`; real-time SLA breakdown pipeline (`ConversationSLABreakdownService` → `ResponsivenessAnalyticsService`) extended with `rltSla`; proto field added (`ResponsivenessSLABreakdownResponse.rltSla`, tag 3).
- Frontend: Settings → SLA admin form gets a 3rd RLT row (value/unit/reminder) and definition card; Statistic → Responsiveness → SLA Breakdown gets a 3rd RLT card per column; i18n for both locales.
- System-default RLT threshold: 5 minutes (`configuredMs: 5 * 60 * 1000`).
- Indonesian Settings-namespace label: "Waktu Tunggu Lead" (metric label + definition title).
- A `mongosh` backfill script (`tools/scripts/db/backfill-sla-rlt-success.js`) resolves and persists `slaRltSuccess`/`rltSnapshotConfiguredMs` onto existing conversations that already have `rltMs` but predate this feature, using the same resolver fallback chain as the live app (dry-run-first flow documented in the script header).

Retroactively filed — implementation was already completed against an ad-hoc plan (no ticket existed at write time):
- Backend: branch `feat/add-sla-rlt-success-backend` off `v2.8.0.1` in omnichannel-satuinbox-be.
- Frontend: branch `feat/add-sla-rlt-success-frontend` off `v2.8.0.1` in omnichannel-satuinbox-fe.

Plan/report: `.claude/PRPs/plans/completed/add-sla-rlt-success.plan.md` / `.claude/PRPs/reports/add-sla-rlt-success-report.md`.

Related to #3226 (parent RLT-to-statistic feature, which explicitly excluded RLT SLA breakdown from its scope).

Note: implementation also surfaced a pre-existing, unrelated bug in FRT's business-hours pause calculation (`handleAgentReplied` appears to use `totalPausedMs` instead of `totalFrtPausedMs`) — not fixed as part of this ticket, flagged for separate investigation.

workPackages.subject: Responsiveness team filter lets Supervisor select any team, not just their own
workPackages.description:
The team filter on Statistic → Responsiveness ignored per-user scope, letting a Supervisor select any team in the company instead of just the team(s) they belong to.

Root cause: `ResponsivenessFilterOptions.tsx` received `analyticsContext` as a prop but never forwarded it into `useResponsivenessFilterOptions(...)`, so the team fetch never passed `isMyOwnTeam` to the (already backend-supported) team-list query.

Also required gating directly on `role.code === SUPERVISOR` (matching every other team-scoping site in the codebase — `conversation.service.ts`'s `shouldScopeByTeam`, `contact-visibility-resolver.service.ts`, `contact-scope.util.ts`, both `message-authorization.service.ts` files) rather than relying solely on `useAnalyticsAccessMode`'s `accessMode === 'team'` derivation — the default seeded SUPERVISOR role carries the `statistic:*` wildcard permission, which wins over `READ_TEAM` in that hook's priority chain and would otherwise never resolve to team-scoped access. The `accessMode === 'team'` check is kept as a fallback for companies that have customized a role's permissions to `statistic:read_team` instead of the wildcard.

Fix: `apps/omnichannel/components/molecules/statistic/responsiveness/ResponsivenessFilterOptions.tsx` and `useResponsivenessFilterOptions.ts`, 2 files changed (+10/-5 lines total).

Filed retroactively — found and fixed during a separate session, no ticket existed at write time. Landed on branch `feat/add-sla-rlt-success-frontend` alongside unrelated in-progress work (RLT SLA success, #3248, and the team-filter search fix, #3243) due to a shared working-tree session collision — bundled into the same MR with user confirmation rather than split out, since all three touch the same Responsiveness filter area.

Manual browser validation still outstanding (requires a running full backend stack + seeded Supervisor/Admin/Agent test accounts, not available in the implementation session): confirm Supervisor sees only their own team(s), Admin still sees all teams (regression check), Agent still has the row hidden entirely (regression check).

workPackages.subject: Scale auto-pull cron's per-team batch limit with eligible member count instead of a flat cap
workPackages.description:
## Background
Follow-up from #3062 (auto-pull cron team-drain + slot guard). That ticket replaced the cron's old "1 conversation per team per cycle" behavior with a loop that drains a team's backlog up to a flat `AUTO_PULL_TEAM_BATCH_LIMIT = 20` per team per 15-minute cycle.

That flat cap was chosen to bound how much wall-clock time any single team can consume within one cron execution — the cron processes up to `AUTO_PULL_BATCH_LIMIT = 120` teams **sequentially, in one run, under one shared 110-second distributed lock** (`AUTO_PULL_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS`). An unbounded per-team loop risked one large/well-staffed team monopolizing that shared window.

## Problem
The flat 20 throttles **well-staffed teams** far below what they could safely absorb. Each eligible member is already independently bounded by their own `min(maxConversation − assigned, 10)` (the existing per-member rate cap from #2711) — so the *natural* per-team ceiling, with no flat cap at all, would be `sum over eligible members of min(maxConversation − assigned, 10)`:

| Eligible members with room | Natural ceiling (no flat cap) | Actual today (capped at 20) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10 | 10 (cap doesn't bind) |
| 10 | up to 100 | 20 (cap binds, wastes ~80%) |
| 200 | up to 2000 | 20 (cap binds, wastes ~99%) |

So today, any team with more than ~2 eligible members hits the flat cap well before any real constraint (`maxConversation` or the rate cap) would stop it — backlog sits queued even though online agents have room, purely because of the arbitrary 20.

## Proposed direction
Replace the flat `AUTO_PULL_TEAM_BATCH_LIMIT` with a per-team cap that scales with how many eligible members that team actually has, bounded by an absolute ceiling to preserve the original worst-case-runtime protection:

```
teamCap = min(ABSOLUTE_CEILING, eligibleMemberCount * AUTO_PULL_MAX_ASSIGNMENTS_PER_WINDOW)
```

- 1-agent team: unchanged (~10).
- 10-agent team: ~100 instead of 20.
- Very large team: still bounded by `ABSOLUTE_CEILING` (needs its own value — possibly the current 20, possibly higher; see open questions) so a single huge team still can't dominate the shared 120-team/110s-lock cron run.

## Implementation notes
- `autoPullConversationsForTeam` currently discovers eligible members lazily, one `findAvailableMemberForAutoPull` call per loop iteration (i.e., per conversation attempted) — there's no single "how many eligible members does this team have right now" count available up front.
- Computing `eligibleMemberCount` cheaply before the loop starts means either: (a) fetching+filtering the team's member list once at the top of `autoPullConversationsForTeam` (reusing the `getAllActiveMembers` + `isMemberAvailableForAutoPull` logic already inside `findAvailableMemberForAutoPull`), or (b) a lighter dedicated count-only query if one doesn't already exist. Option (a) risks an extra gRPC round trip (and per-member shift/office-hours lookups) per team per cycle — needs a cost check against 120 teams/cycle before committing to the approach.
- Once `teamCap` is known, the existing loop/lock/re-verify machinery (`assignToLeastLoadedTeamMember`, `withMemberAutoPullLock`) is unchanged — only the loop's upper bound changes from a constant to a computed value.

## Open questions (resolve before implementation)
- What should `ABSOLUTE_CEILING` be? Keep it at 20 (protects runtime, but reintroduces a version of today's throttle for very large teams — just at a higher agent count) or raise it, informed by actual cron tick duration data.
- Is the extra per-cycle "count eligible members" lookup cheap enough at 120 teams/cycle, or does it need caching/batching similar to `buildOrgCache`?
- Should this scale by *eligible* members (post office-hours/status filter, more accurate but requires the fuller lookup) or by a cheaper proxy like *active* team member count (less accurate, cheaper)?

## Suggested scope for this ticket
1. Instrument/measure actual cron tick durations and how often teams currently hit the flat 20 cap with backlog still remaining, to confirm this is worth the added complexity before changing code.
2. Design + implement the scaling formula (resolve open questions above).
3. Update `conversation.service.spec.ts` / cron tests for the new cap logic.
4. Update `docs/auto-pull-round-robin.md`'s "AUTO_PULL_TEAM_BATCH_LIMIT is a ceiling across all members" section to reflect the new scaling behavior.

## Related
- #3062 — introduced the flat `AUTO_PULL_TEAM_BATCH_LIMIT = 20` this ticket proposes to replace.
- #2711 — introduced the per-member `AUTO_PULL_MAX_ASSIGNMENTS_PER_WINDOW = 10` rate cap this ticket's formula builds on.

workPackages.subject: Exclude WhatsApp API broadcasts from spin text processing
workPackages.description:
**Problem**
Broadcast spin text was applied to all broadcast platforms, including WhatsApp API (Business Cloud API). Spin text should not apply to WhatsApp API broadcasts — only WhatsApp Web.

**Root cause**
`SpinTextMessageProcessor.resolveSpinTextOutput` in `omnichannel-satuinbox-be/apps/broadcast-service/src/app/processors/spin-text.processor.ts` only checked the organization-level `spinTextEnabled` toggle before calling the third-party spin text API. It had no check for broadcast platform, so `whatsapp_api` broadcasts (the only other platform besides `whatsapp_web` supported by `BroadcastPlatformEnum`) went through spin text transformation too.

**Fix**
- `resolveSpinTextOutput` now receives the batch's message platform and short-circuits (skipping the third-party spin text API call, falling back to `originContent` as `sendContent`) when `platform === PlatformEnum.WHATSAPP_API`.
- The emit to the spin-text queue (`handleEmitToProcessSpinText`) in `broadcast.service.ts` was intentionally left unchanged for WhatsApp API, since that queue/processor also drives send-scheduling (rate limiting, working-hours enforcement, per-sender queueing) — skipping the emit entirely would have stopped WhatsApp API broadcasts from ever being scheduled/sent.
- Added `SPIN_TEXT_SKIPPED_FOR_PLATFORM` log message in `constants/info.constant.ts` for visibility.

**Files changed**
- `apps/broadcast-service/src/app/processors/spin-text.processor.ts`
- `apps/broadcast-service/src/app/constants/info.constant.ts`

Ticket filed retroactively after implementing the fix.

workPackages.subject: FIX - RMQ export job
workPackages.description:
Incident Report: RabbitMQ / Message Delivery Delay  
Ringkasan  
\- \*\*Tanggal insiden\*\*: 24 Juli 2026  
\- \*\*Sistem terdampak\*\*: RabbitMQ pada host \`sirabbit\` (container \`rabbitmq\`)  
\- \*\*Gejala utama\*\*: pesan terindikasi tidak terkirim / tertahan pada antrian tertentu  
\- \*\*Status saat ini\*\*: \*\*terpulihkan sebagian\*\* (broker sehat, namun masih ada indikasi masalah di sisi  
consumer untuk queue tertentu)  
Dampak  
\- Potensi keterlambatan pemrosesan pada workflow tertentu, terutama queue:  
\- \`export-report-delayed\`  
\- \`instagram-token-refresh\`  
\- \`broadcast-retry\`  
\- Outbound queue utama (\`outbound-\*\`) saat pengecekan terakhir dalam kondisi normal (tidak backlog).  
Kronologi Singkat  
1\. Dilakukan pengecekan service RabbitMQ di \`sirabbit\`.  
2\. Ditemukan RabbitMQ berjalan sebagai \*\*Docker container\*\* (\`rabbitmq\`), bukan service systemd.  
3\. Container sempat dalam kondisi exited sebelumnya, lalu dilakukan restart:  
\- \`docker restart rabbitmq\`  
4\. Verifikasi pasca-restart:  
\- Container up  
\- Port AMQP/management aktif  
\- \`rabbitmq-diagnostics\` menunjukkan node sehat, tanpa alarm.  
5\. Investigasi queue menunjukkan:  
\- Outbound queue utama: tidak ada \`messages\_ready\`/\`messages\_unacknowledged\` signifikan.  
\- Terdapat backlog \`messages\_unacknowledged\` pada queue tertentu (terutama \`export-report-  
delayed\`).  
6\. Log RabbitMQ menunjukkan error berulang:  
\- \`precondition\_failed: unknown delivery tag ...\`  
\- indikasi masalah ack/channel di sisi consumer.  
Temuan Teknis  
Kondisi Broker  
\- RabbitMQ \*\*sehat\*\* (no alarm, memory/disk aman).  
\- Tidak ada indikasi broker crash berulang setelah restart.  
Kondisi Queue  
\- Queue outbound umum (\`outbound-email\`, \`outbound-whatsapp-api\`, \`outbound-whatsapp-web\`, dll)  
normal.  
\- Queue dengan unacked tinggi:  
\- \`export-report-delayed\` (tertinggi saat observasi)  
\- \`instagram-token-refresh\`  
\- \`broadcast-retry\`  
Indikasi Akar Masalah (Probable Root Cause)  
Kemungkinan besar masalah ada di \*\*worker/consumer\*\*, bukan broker RabbitMQ:  
\- Ack dilakukan pada delivery tag/channel yang tidak valid atau sudah berubah.  
\- Potensi race/reconnect handling pada library consumer.  
\- Efeknya: message masuk status unacked lebih lama, memicu delay pemrosesan.  
Aksi yang Sudah Dilakukan  
1\. Restart RabbitMQ container di \`sirabbit\`.  
2\. Health check broker + queue + log untuk validasi kondisi aktual.  
3\. Dibuat tooling monitoring dan auto-heal:

\- Script: \`/home/ubuntu/mq-autoheal.sh\`  
\- Rule: \`/home/ubuntu/mq-autoheal.rules\`  
\- README: \`/home/ubuntu/MQ\_AUTOHEAL\_README.md\`  
4\. Dijadwalkan periodic check via cron (setiap 5 menit).  
5\. Mode awal diset \*\*alert-first\*\* (aman): rule tanpa restart command agar tidak restart liar.  
Solusi  
Solusi Jangka Pendek (Operasional)  
1\. \*\*Lanjutkan monitoring otomatis\*\* via \`mq-autoheal.sh\`.  
2\. Isi \`restart\_command\` pada rule queue bermasalah untuk restart worker spesifik (bukan restart broker  
global).  
3\. Terapkan cooldown restart (sudah didukung) agar tidak terjadi loop restart.  
4\. Jalankan dry-run sebelum aktivasi penuh:  
\- \`~/mq-autoheal.sh --dry-run\`  
Solusi Jangka Menengah (Perbaikan Aplikasi)  
1\. Audit logic consumer untuk ack:  
\- pastikan ack dilakukan \*\*sekali\*\* per delivery,  
\- tidak ack setelah channel ditutup/recreated,  
\- validasi penanganan reconnect.  
2\. Set prefetch yang sesuai per worker.  
3\. Pastikan retry + DLQ policy konsisten untuk queue kritikal.  
4\. Tambahkan observability per worker (metric ack/nack/retry/error by queue).  
Solusi Jangka Panjang (Reliability)  
1\. Definisikan SLO queue processing (latency + backlog threshold).  
2\. Alerting berbasis:  
\- \`messages\_ready\` tinggi,  
\- \`messages\_unacknowledged\` tinggi,  
\- consumer count = 0,  
\- error pattern \`unknown delivery tag\`.  
3\. Buat runbook insiden resmi + ownership queue per tim/service.  
4\. Lakukan uji chaos/reconnect untuk memastikan consumer robust saat koneksi putus-sambung.  
Rencana Tindak Lanjut (Action Items)  
1\. \[ \] Mapping queue -> worker/service owner  
2\. \[ \] Isi \`restart\_command\` pada \`mq-autoheal.rules\`  
3\. \[ \] Aktifkan auto-restart bertahap per queue kritikal  
4\. \[ \] Patch bug ack handling pada worker terkait  
5\. \[ \] Tambah dashboard backlog + unacked + error rate  
6\. \[ \] Review hasil 24-48 jam setelah auto-heal aktif  
Lampiran  
\- README operasional: \`/home/ubuntu/MQ\_AUTOHEAL\_README.md\`  
\- Script auto-heal: \`/home/ubuntu/mq-autoheal.sh\`  
\- Rules auto-heal: \`/home/ubuntu/mq-autoheal.rules\`  
\- Log auto-heal: \`/home/ubuntu/.mq-autoheal/autoheal.log\`  
\- Log cron: \`/home/ubuntu/.mq-autoheal/cron.log\`

workPackages.subject: Maximum call stack in inbound prod
workPackages.description:
WhatsApp group messages fail to process in conversation-service (v2.7.0) when the sender's  
 phone number matches one of the conversation's account channels (e.g., another company CS  
 number posting in the same group). The inbound processor crashes with RangeError: Maximum   
 call stack size exceeded, the RabbitMQ message retries and fails repeatedly, and the  
 affected message never reaches the UI (no socket emit, no ticket sync) — the conversation  
 appears frozen.

 Root cause:

 handleSenderInfo() in inbound-message.processor.ts passed a live Mongoose subdocument (from  
 conversation.accountChannel.find(...)) into mapMongoToProto(). Live Mongoose structures  
 contain circular internal parent back-pointers, so the recursive mapper never terminates.  
 Surfaced in v2.7.0 because validateAccountChannel now lets group messages on inactive  
 channels through to this code path.

 Fix:

 1. Extract only the four fields sender info needs (id, name, email, phoneNumber) instead of  
 recursively mapping the live subdocument.  
 2. Add recursion-path tracking (WeakSet) to toProtoValue/mapMongoToProto in libs/common —  
 circular input now throws a typed GrpcInternalException (internalCode 5000) instead of  
 crashing the process.

 Branch: fix/2531-map-mongo-to-proto-circular-reference (targets v2.8.0)

workPackages.subject: Instagram: Reconnect Expired Channel Instead of Delete + Re-create
workPackages.description:
**Date**: 2026-07-06
**Repo**: both
**Scope**: `apps/instagram`, `apps/channel-service` (BE); Instagram add-on settings UI (FE)

## Problem

When an Instagram account's token expires, the only way to restore the channel today is to delete the account channel and reconnect from scratch. This loses configuration and is a confusing user flow — users don't understand why a working channel suddenly requires full re-setup.

## Investigation findings

- `POST /instagram/exchange-code` (api-gateway → `apps/instagram`) already supports reconnecting in place: `checkInstagramAccountExist` in `apps/instagram/src/app/services/app.service.ts` (~line 1088) allows re-running OAuth for an already-connected account instead of erroring, and `upsertAccountChannel` resets `connectionStatus` back to `ACTIVE` on the *same* `accountChannelId`. **No new backend endpoint is required for the reconnect action itself.**
- The frontend already has a partially-built affordance: `InstagramTableColumn.tsx` (`omnichannel-satuinbox-fe/apps/omnichannel/components/molecules/settings/add-ons/instagram/InstagramTableColumn.tsx`, ~line 31-39) renders a "Connect" button whenever `connectionStatus !== 'active'`, but it has **no `onClick` handler** — it's currently dead.
- The real gap is that nothing ever flags a channel as disconnected when its token actually expires, so the reconnect button never has a reason to appear:
  - `apps/instagram/src/app/services/token-refresh.service.ts` line ~145 has a TODO comment (`// TODO: Consider updating account status to disconnected and notifying user`) instead of actually updating status on refresh failure.
  - `apps/instagram/src/app/services/webhook.service.ts` only handles Graph API error code 230 (consent required); it does not handle code 190 (invalid/expired token) to flag disconnects from webhook delivery failures.
  - The only code path that currently reacts to loss of access is `handleDeauthorization` (`app.service.ts` ~line 1117), which hard-deletes the Instagram account and soft-deletes the channel — i.e. it destroys the connection rather than flagging it as reconnectable.

## Proposed scope

1. **Backend** — detect and flag disconnects instead of silently doing nothing:
   - On token refresh failure in `token-refresh.service.ts`, update `connectionStatus` to `inactive` via the channel-service `updateAccountChannel` gRPC call (replace the existing TODO).
   - Handle Graph API error code 190 in `webhook.service.ts` the same way code 230 is handled today, flagging the channel as disconnected.
2. **Frontend** — wire up the existing dead button instead of adding a new one:
   - Pass a reconnect handler from `InstagramPlatformContent.tsx` into `InstagramTableColumn.tsx`, reusing the existing OAuth popup flow (`hooks/instagram/use-instagram-oauth.ts` → `exchange-code`).
   - On success, invalidate `FETCH_ACCOUNT_CHANNEL` (already done today for the "Connect account" button) so the badge flips back to active.
3. **Guardrail** — since reconnect matches on Instagram `userId`, add a check/warning if the account used to reconnect doesn't match the originally connected `userId`, so users don't accidentally attach a different Instagram account to an existing channel.

## Note

Deleting a channel does not cascade-delete conversations or contacts today (no delete event is emitted/consumed), so historical data is not at risk either way — but reconnect-in-place avoids losing the account channel config and is a much simpler UX.

## Files likely touched

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `omnichannel-satuinbox-be/apps/instagram/src/app/services/token-refresh.service.ts` | Replace TODO (~line 145) with actual disconnect flagging on refresh failure |
| `omnichannel-satuinbox-be/apps/instagram/src/app/services/webhook.service.ts` | Add handling for Graph error code 190 alongside existing 230 handling |
| `omnichannel-satuinbox-fe/apps/omnichannel/components/molecules/settings/add-ons/instagram/InstagramTableColumn.tsx` | Wire the existing non-active "Connect" button to a reconnect handler |
| `omnichannel-satuinbox-fe/apps/omnichannel/components/molecules/settings/add-ons/instagram/InstagramPlatformContent.tsx` | Supply reconnect handler (reuse `onConnect`/OAuth popup) into the table columns |
| `omnichannel-satuinbox-fe/apps/omnichannel/hooks/instagram/use-instagram-oauth.ts` | Reuse for reconnect, or add an account-scoped variant if userId-mismatch guardrail requires it |

workPackages.subject: Team filter on Statistic Responsiveness doesn't search backend data
workPackages.description:
The team filter on Statistic → Responsiveness looks like a search box, but typing only filters whatever teams were already loaded locally (first page of 25 non-archived teams) — it never hits the backend, so any team beyond that first page is unreachable no matter what's typed.

Root cause: `apps/omnichannel/components/molecules/statistic/responsiveness/useResponsivenessFilterOptions.ts` called `useGetTeamList({ isArchived: false, search: '' })` with a hardcoded empty search string and never wired `onSearchChange`/`shouldFilterOption` into the returned filter config. The `Combobox` component (wraps `cmdk`) defaults to `shouldFilterOption=true` in that case, which does `cmdk`'s own client-side fuzzy filter over whatever options are already rendered — completely independent of the backend.

The correct, working pattern already exists in the same codebase (and even on the same page, just hidden behind `hideTeamFilter`): `useTeamSearch` debounces input and sends it to the backend, used correctly by `StatisticFilter.tsx`'s `TeamFilterCombobox` (`shouldFilterOption={false}`) across the Conversations/Broadcast/Ticket statistic tabs. The agent filter on this same Responsiveness page was already wired correctly too — only the team filter was the outlier.

Fix: added local debounced search state + `limit: 50` + wired `onSearchChange`/`shouldFilterOption: false` into the team filter config, mirroring the agent filter's existing wiring in the same file. Single file changed (+13/-2 lines).

Branch: `fix/responsiveness-team-filter-search` off `v2.8.0.1` in omnichannel-satuinbox-fe.

Filed retroactively — found and fixed during an unrelated session, no ticket existed at write time.

workPackages.subject: Cloudflare Internal Server - At some time Cloudflare incidental error
workPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report — Intermittent HTTP 500 "Internal Server Error" on Conversation Page (Cloudflare Layer) ## Summary On **14 August 2026**, an intermittent HTTP 500 Internal Server Error was observed while accessing the SatuInbox conversation page at `v2.satuinbox.com/id/conversation/all`. The first observed failure occurred at approximately **11:09:59 WIB**, and the application returned to normal operation at approximately **11:18:30 WIB**, giving an observed incident window of approximately **8 minutes 31 seconds**. During the incident the page displayed a Cloudflare error page — "Internal server error (Error code 500)" — with the Cloudflare status indicators showing **Browser: Working, Cloudflare: Error, Host (v2.satuinbox.com): Working**. This indicates the failure was surfaced at the Cloudflare proxy layer rather than a confirmed browser-side or origin-host outage. The issue recovered without any client-side configuration change or application intervention. Based on available evidence this is currently classified as an **intermittent infrastructure / proxy-layer error with Cloudflare involvement**, not a conclusively confirmed backend application defect. Further investigation is required to correlate the incident timeframe with Cloudflare logs, origin/server logs, request traces, and deployment or infrastructure events. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce > _Note: the failure was intermittent and not reproducible on demand. The following steps document the observed trigger and verification actions._ 1. Open `https://v2.satuinbox.com/id/conversation/all` in the browser on 14 Aug 2026 at ~11:09:59 WIB. 2. Observe the Cloudflare error page: "Internal server error (Error code 500)". 3. Verify the Cloudflare status indicators: Browser **Working**, Cloudflare **Error**, Host **Working**. 4. Refresh the page manually (`Cmd + R`) approximately every 10 seconds throughout the affected period. 5. Observe the page recovering on its own and the conversation page loading normally at approximately **11:18:30 WIB** (screenshot at 11:19:30 WIB shows the app restored). ## Actual Result * Page displayed Cloudflare error page **"Internal server error (Error code 500)"** between ~11:09:59 and ~11:18:30 WIB. * Error page text: _"There is an internal server error on Cloudflare's network."_ / _"Please try again in a few minutes."_ * Cloudflare **Ray ID:** `**a2ad1b034988cec7**` (captured at 11:11:08 WIB screenshot; visible in the 11:09:59 capture as well). * Cloudflare status indicators during the failure: **Browser: Working · Cloudflare: Error · Host: Working**. * Page timestamps shown on the error page: **2026-08-14 04:09:41 UTC** (≈ 11:09:41 WIB) and **04:11:08 UTC** (≈ 11:11:08 WIB). * Manual refreshes every ~10 s continued to show the error throughout the window. * The issue recovered without client-side configuration change or application intervention; conversation page loaded normally at ~11:18:30 WIB (verified by 11:19:30 WIB screenshot showing the inbox restored). ## Expected Result * The conversation page (`/id/conversation/all`) should load and display normally at all times. * No HTTP 500 / Cloudflare error page should be served during normal operation. * If a transient infrastructure event occurs, the incident should be traceable to Cloudflare / origin logs and the service should self-recover or be restored without prolonged user-facing failure. ## Impact ## Evidence _Ray ID_ `_a2ad1b034988cec7_` _present in both failure captures — useful for Cloudflare log correlation._ ## Initial Observation * Cloudflare error page 500 appeared on `v2.satuinbox.com/id/conversation/all` at ~11:09:59 WIB and persisted through repeated refreshes until ~11:18:30 WIB. * The Cloudflare diagnostic indicators explicitly reported **Cloudflare: Error** while **Browser: Working** and **Host: Working** — the failure is attributed at the Cloudflare network/proxy layer, not the browser or the origin host status indicator. * The error page text states the error is _"on Cloudflare's network"_ (generic Cloudflare 500 message), and includes a Ray ID for traceability. * Recovery was spontaneous; no client-side change or intervention preceded it. * The page recovered to the conversation inbox (screenshot 11:19:30 WIB shows the app fully functional, with the inbox listing visible). ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * **Cloudflare edge / proxy layer** — transient Cloudflare network error (the error page and status indicators point here first). * **Origin (host) upstream** — intermittent upstream failure or timeout that Cloudflare translated to a 500 page; the "Host: Working" indicator is the Cloudflare-side health check and does not rule out per-request origin errors. * **Deployment / infrastructure event** — coincident deploy, config change, or resource event on 2026-08-14 ~11:09–11:18 WIB. * **Application backend** — an intermittent application-level 500 cannot be fully excluded without origin logs. _Hypotheses only — Cloudflare/origin log correlation is required before assigning root cause._ ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. **Correlate the incident window** (2026-08-14 04:09:41 – 04:18:30 UTC) with **Cloudflare logs / analytics** for Ray ID `a2ad1b034988cec7` — determine whether the error originated at the Cloudflare edge or was proxied from origin. 2. **Check origin/server logs** for `v2.satuinbox.com` in the same window for any 5xx, timeout, restart, or resource-exhaustion events. 3. **Check deployment and infrastructure events** (deploys, config changes, DNS, certificate, rate limiting, WAF) around the incident time. 4. **Verify scope**: determine whether the 500 affected only `/id/conversation/all` or was broader (other paths, other users, API calls). 5. If reproducible, capture the exact request (headers, Cloudflare headers, `cf-ray`) and origin response to distinguish edge vs origin failure. ## Additional Notes * **Host**: the incident URL uses `v2.satuinbox.com` (no `dev-` prefix). This differs from the documented QA/dev host (`dev-v2.satuinbox.com`) — treat `v2.satuinbox.com` as reported by the tester; the architecture reference does not document this host. * **Classification**: per the available evidence, this is reported as an **intermittent infrastructure/proxy-layer error with Cloudflare involvement**, not a confirmed application defect. The report is filed per PM suggestion to track and investigate the event. * **UTC ↔ WIB**: error page timestamps are UTC (04:09:41 / 04:11:08 UTC = 11:09:41 / 11:11:08 WIB, UTC+7). Incident window ≈ 11:09:59 → 11:18:30 WIB. * **Related context**: screenshots taken during the window show the tester was also validating Global Search typo behavior (query "abrizal" visible in the 11:19:30 recovery screenshot); unrelated to this incident unless log correlation says otherwise.

melaporkan hasilnya via email. --- ## 📊 System Architecture Diagram ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ AUTOMATED BUG FIX PIPELINE │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ VM Logs │──5m─>│ Bug Detector │─────>│ OpenProject │ │ /var/log/ │ │ (Bash+AI) │ │ (Ticket) │ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ │ │ │ │ v v ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ Code Reader │ │ Email Report │ │ (Git Repo) │ │ (Daily 7pm) │ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ │ │ v ┌──────────────┐ │ AI Fixer │ │ (Claude) │ └──────────────┘ │ │ v ┌──────────────┐ │ Git Push │ │ (Auto PR) │ └──────────────┘ ``` --- ## 🔄 Workflow Diagram ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PHASE 1: DETECTION (Every 5 min) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [Cron Job: */5 * * * *] │ ├─> tail -f /var/log/app/*.log │ grep -E "ERROR|FATAL|Exception" │ ├─> Parse error stack trace │ │ │ ├─> Extract: file, line, function, error message │ └─> Deduplicate (check if already reported) │ └─> If NEW error found: └─> Go to PHASE 2 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PHASE 2: TICKET CREATION (Immediate) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [Create OpenProject Ticket via MCP] │ ├─> Title: "BUG: {error_type} in {file}:{line}" ├─> Description: │ ├─> Error message │ ├─> Stack trace │ ├─> Affected file & line │ ├─> Timestamp & frequency │ └─> Environment info │ ├─> Type: Bug ├─> Priority: Auto-calculate based on: │ ├─> FATAL/ERROR → High │ ├─> WARNING → Normal │ └─> Frequency > 10/min → Urgent │ ├─> Assignee: Auto (or specific team member) └─> Status: New │ └─> Store ticket ID in cache ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PHASE 3: CODE READING (On demand) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [When ticket status → "In Progress"] │ ├─> Read error location from ticket │ │ │ ├─> cd /path/to/repo │ ├─> git pull origin main │ └─> cat {affected_file} │ ├─> Get surrounding context: │ ├─> 50 lines before error │ ├─> 50 lines after error │ └─> Related functions/classes │ └─> Send to AI for analysis ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PHASE 4: AI FIX (Automated) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [AI Agent (Claude via MCP)] │ ├─> Input: │ ├─> Error message + stack trace │ ├─> Affected code (with context) │ ├─> Related files (dependencies) │ └─> Project language/framework │ ├─> AI Analysis: │ ├─> Identify root cause │ ├─> Generate fix │ ├─> Run unit tests (if available) │ └─> Verify fix doesn't break other code │ └─> Output: Fixed code + explanation ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PHASE 5: GIT COMMIT & PUSH │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [Automated Git Workflow] │ ├─> Create feature branch: │ "fix/auto-bug-{ticket_id}-{timestamp}" │ ├─> Apply fix to code │ ├─> Commit: │ ├─> Message: "🤖 Auto-fix: {error_summary}" │ ├─> Body: │ │ ├─> "Fixes #ticket_id" │ │ ├─> AI explanation │ │ └─> Changed files │ └─> Author: "AI Bot " │ ├─> Push to remote │ └─> Create Pull Request (GitLab/GitHub) ├─> Title: "[AUTO-FIX] {error_summary}" ├─> Description: Link to OpenProject ticket ├─> Labels: automated, bug-fix ├─> Reviewers: Auto-assign team lead └─> Comment on OpenProject ticket with PR link ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ PHASE 6: DAILY EMAIL REPORT (7 PM) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ [Cron Job: 0 19 * * *] │ ├─> Query bugs detected in last 24h │ │ │ ├─> Total bugs found: X │ ├─> New tickets created: Y │ ├─> Auto-fixed & PR created: Z │ └─> Failed to fix: W │ ├─> Generate HTML email: │ ├─> Summary dashboard │ ├─> Top 10 critical bugs │ ├─> Fix success rate │ └─> Links to tickets & PRs │ └─> Send via SMTP ├─> To: dev-team@example.com ├─> Subject: "🤖 Daily Bug Report - {date}" └─> Attachments: Full log CSV ``` --- ## 🛠️ Technical Stack ### 1. Bug Detection Layer ```bash #!/bin/bash # /usr/local/bin/bug-detector.sh LOG_DIR="/var/log/app" CACHE_FILE="/tmp/reported_bugs.json" OPENPROJECT_API="https://openproject.example.com/api/v3" detect_bugs() { # Tail logs and parse errors tail -n 1000 $LOG_DIR/*.log | \ grep -E "ERROR|FATAL|Exception" | \ while read -r line; do process_error "$line" done } process_error() { # Extract error details # Check if already reported # If new, create ticket via MCP } ``` ### 2. OpenProject Integration (MCP) ```javascript // Use existing MCP OpenProject server const mcp = require('@modelcontextprotocol/sdk'); async function createBugTicket(errorData) { return await mcp.call('create_work_package', { projectId: 'satuinbox', subject: `BUG: ${errorData.type} in ${errorData.file}`, description: formatBugDescription(errorData), typeId: 7, // Bug type priorityId: calculatePriority(errorData), assigneeId: 4 // Auto-assign }); } ``` ### 3. AI Fixer (Claude MCP) ```javascript const Anthropic = require('@anthropic-ai/sdk'); async function generateFix(bugContext) { const prompt = ` You are a senior developer. workPackages.subject: Broadcast - [Template] - WhatsApp API templates created directly in Meta Business Manager never sync to DB
workPackages.description:
**Description:**
Templates created directly in Meta Business Manager (not via SatuInbox's own template builder) never appear in the local database — regardless of Meta review status (pending, approved, or rejected) and regardless of how many sync cron cycles run.

**Root cause (confirmed via live docker-compose logs):**
`whatsapp-api`'s periodic Meta template sync (`TemplateSyncCronService`, every 15 min) correctly finds connected WABAs and emits a `BROADCAST_TEMPLATE_RECONCILE` event per template (`found=N reconciled=N` in whatsapp-api logs). But `broadcast-service`'s consumer throws on every single new-template insert:
```
ValidationError: BroadcastTemplate validation failed: approval.token: Path `token` is required.
```
`BroadcastTemplateApprovalDefault.token` is `''` (empty string), and Mongoose's default `required` validator for `String` schema paths treats an empty string as "missing" — unlike `Number`/`Date`/`Array` paths, which only fail on `null`/`undefined`. Since Meta-imported templates never go through the internal token-based approval flow (that's exclusively for locally-authored drafts, which always get a real crypto token via `generateApprovalTemplate()` before their first save), requiring `token` on this schema path is incorrect for `source=meta` rows.

The reconcile event is consumed via RabbitMQ with no try/catch, so the failure is silent/fire-and-forget — whatsapp-api's cron log still reports `reconciled=N` because it only counts successful *emits*, not confirmed persists. This affects every tenant, for every brand-new Meta-imported template.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create a template directly in Meta Business Manager (Facebook page's WhatsApp Business Account), not through SatuInbox's template builder
2. Wait for the sync cron to run (`TEMPLATE_SYNC_CRON_ENABLED=true`, 15-min interval) or trigger `POST /broadcast/template/sync`
3. Check broadcast-service logs and the local template list

**Actual:** Template never appears locally; broadcast-service logs `ValidationError: approval.token: Path 'token' is required.` on every reconcile attempt for that template.

**Expected:** Template appears locally with status correctly mapped from Meta (`PENDING`→`REVIEW`, `APPROVED`→`ACTIVE`, `REJECTED`→`REJECTED`, `DISABLED`→`PAUSE`) — status mapping logic already exists and is correct, it just never got a chance to run because the insert always threw first.

**Fix plan:** `.claude/PRPs/plans/whatsapp-meta-template-sync-approval-token-fix.plan.md` (in `omnichannel-satuinbox-be` repo checkout) — relax `approval.token`'s `required: true` → `required: false` in `broadcast-template.schema.ts`, plus regression tests using real Mongoose `validateSync()` (the existing reconcile-service spec mocks the repository and never caught this).

**Related:** #2373 (Broadcast - Improvement template whatsapp api) — that ticket's own QA notes already flag "status template masih stuck d pending", which is this same symptom.

**Env bug found:** Dev (confirmed via docker-compose logs)
**Env Test:** Dev

workPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Improvement Perfomance
workPackages.description: # \[BUG\] Global Search — P95 latency 60x over PRD threshold (60s vs 1.5s) and 97% request failure rate under 50-VU concurrent load ## Environment ## Description The Global Search endpoint fails catastrophically under concurrent load. During a **50 Virtual User spike test (7.5 minutes)**, only **16 of 489 requests (3.3%)** completed successfully. The remaining **473 requests (96.7%)** either returned **HTTP 500 (240 requests)** or **timed out after 60 seconds (233 requests)**. Performance also fails the PRD requirement before concurrency is introduced. At **1 VU (sequential execution)**, the endpoint already records a **P95 latency of 4.55 seconds**, approximately **3× slower** than the required **1.5-second** threshold. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Authenticate as **Admin (**`**aprizaladm01**`**)** using the NextAuth authentication flow: * CSRF * Credentials * Session * JWT 2. Send a GET request to: ```text /api/search?conversationLimit=20&conversationOffset=0&q=tes&ticketLimit=20&ticketOffset=0 ``` 1. Execute **1 Virtual User** sequentially (5 iterations) to establish a baseline. 2. Execute **5 Virtual Users** with simultaneous requests. 3. Execute the following spike profile: ```text 1 minute @ 20 VUs ↓ Ramp to 50 VUs (1 minute) ↓ Sustain 50 VUs (5 minutes) ↓ Cooldown (1 minute) ``` 1. Observe: * Response latency * HTTP status codes * Failure rate ## Actual Result ### Additional Observations * During the 50-VU test, **255 login attempts** were performed. * Only **40 logins (15.7%)** succeeded. * Authentication also degraded significantly under concurrent load. * Fastest search request: * **675 ms** (passes threshold) * Average latency: * **31,174 ms (31.17 s)** * Endpoint occasionally recovers between failures (16 successful responses), but overall availability remains approximately **3%**. ## Expected Result According to **PRD Global Search Suggestion v2.1**: ### NFR §11 (Performance) * P95 latency should remain **below 1.5 seconds** for combined Ticket and Conversation searches using indexed shared-attribute fields. ### Success Metrics §16 * P95 latency **< 1.5 seconds** under expected production usage. ### EH-004 If both domains fail: * Keep the popup open. * Display an error state. * Allow the user to retry. The endpoint should not return HTTP 500. ### EH-007 If one domain times out: * Return partial results from the other domain. * Avoid failing the entire request. ## Impact 1. **Global Search becomes unusable under normal multi-agent load.** More than approximately five concurrent agents already introduce significant failures. 2. **Duplicate ticket handling increases.** Agents cannot discover existing conversations or tickets, directly impacting the PRD objective: > ≥70% of searches return at least one relevant suggestion. 3. **Loss of user trust.** Repeated HTTP 500 responses and 60-second waits discourage agents from using the feature. 4. **High production risk.** If deployed without optimization, typical business-hour concurrency (50+ agents) will likely render the feature unavailable. ## Evidence ### k6 Script ```text performance-testing/global-search/global-search-stress.js ``` ### Raw Result ```text performance-testing/global-search/results/global-search-50vus.json ``` ## Performance Intelligence Report ### Test Profile ### Search Requests ### Latency ### Threshold Validation ## Additional Notes ### Possible Root Causes * Missing database indexes on searchable shared-attribute fields (AWB, Order ID, Tracking Number, etc.). * Database connection pool exhaustion under concurrent search requests. * Thread pool saturation within the search services. * RabbitMQ or inter-service RPC bottlenecks between API Gateway, Conversation Service, and Ticket Service. * Missing circuit breaker or request throttling mechanism, allowing downstream services to fail instead of rejecting excessive traffic. ### Suspected Backend Components * `conversation-service` * `SearchRelatedByAttribute` RPC * `ticket-service` * `SearchRelatedByAttribute` RPC * Database connection pool configuration. * API Gateway timeout configuration (observed timeout ceiling consistently equals 60 seconds). ## Related PRD **PRD Global Search – Global Search Suggestion v2.1** Relevant sections: * **NFR §11** — Performance * **Success Metrics §16** * **EH-004** * **EH-007** ## Recommendation for Engineering 1. Add database indexes for all searchable shared-attribute fields (AWB, Order ID, Tracking Number, etc.) across both Conversation and Ticket collections. 2. Increase database connection pool sizes for: * conversation-service * ticket-service 3. Implement a circuit breaker or rate limiter at the API Gateway to reject excess requests with HTTP 429 or HTTP 503 instead of allowing downstream HTTP 500 failures. 4. Introduce short-lived caching for identical search queries to reduce repeated database lookups. 5. Re-run the k6 stress test after optimization and verify: * P95 latency < 1.5 seconds * HTTP failure rate < 1% * Login success > 98% * Stable operation at 50 concurrent Virtual Users.

workPackages.subject: Global search Atlas $search fails on tenants with over 1,000 conversations/tickets (maxClauseCount overflow)
workPackages.description:
**Bug**: Global Search's Atlas Search path (ticket #2410) throws `MongoServerError: query has expanded into too many sub-queries internally: maxClauseCount is set to 1024` on every request for any tenant with more than ~1,000 in-scope conversations/tickets. The candidate-ID `in()` filter/should clause embedded the full candidate list (up to 5,000 ids) directly into the `$search` compound query; mongot expands `in()` into one Lucene clause per value, exceeding the default `maxClauseCount: 1024`.

Found via a live debugging session (2026-07-24) against the dev DB (logged in as `goddummyprod`, org "SAP") — reproduced on 8/8 calls (4 query terms x conversation/ticket domains), each silently falling back to the slow regex scan (5.5-15s latency) instead of using the Atlas index.

**Fix (implemented)**: commit `ef8e4743` on branch `fix/2228-ticket-relation-label-comma-filter`.
- Chunk the candidate-id list into batches under mongot's clause limit (new `ATLAS_SEARCH_IN_CLAUSE_MAX_SIZE = 900` constant + `chunkIds` helper in `libs/common`), run one `$search` call per chunk in parallel, and union the results.
- Defensively cap + log a warning on the smaller message/reply-match id-in `should` clause carrying the same overflow risk.
- Mirrored identically in `conversation-search.repository.ts` (conversation-service) and `ticket-search.repository.ts` (ticket-service).
- New unit tests added in both repositories' spec files plus `libs/common`'s `atlas-search-query.utils.spec.ts`.

**Status**: Code complete; lint, unit tests, and build all green. Live re-validation against the dev DB (confirming the latency drop and no more maxClauseCount fallback) is still pending -- no dev DB/services were reachable in the implementation session.

workPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Relation label name has no limit char and UI error on detail ticket/conversation in section relation label
workPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary This report covers two related issues in the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal concerning relation label name length: **Issue 1 — Modal UI Breaks with Long Text**: When a relation label name exceeds the available column width in the modal, the modal becomes horizontally scrollable instead of handling the overflow gracefully. The text pushes the layout beyond the viewport, forcing users to scroll sideways to see the full content. This error was appear on Domain Ticket and Conversation, also this causing the bug ui error on conversation detail section relation label also in ticket detail **Issue 2 — No Maximum Character Limit**: There is no maximum character limit enforced on the relation label name field. Users can input arbitrarily long text, which the system accepts without validation. The Product Manager has confirmed that a 50-character maximum limit should be enforced, with a toast warning: "Maksimal 50 karakter." Both issues stem from the same gap: the relation label name field lacks length constraints, and the UI is not designed to handle long values gracefully. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce ### Issue 1 — Modal UI Breaks with Long Text 1. Open the Global Search popup and select one or more search results. 2. Click **"Tandai Relasi"** to open the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal. 3. Select a **Tipe atribut** from the dropdown. 4. In the **Nilai** field, enter a relation label value exceeding the column width (for example, 60+ characters or more). 5. Optionally apply the label so it becomes a visible badge. 6. Observe the modal layout. ### Issue 2 — No Maximum Character Limit 1. Open the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal as described above. 2. In the **Nilai** field, enter a string longer than 50 characters. 3. Click **Terapkan** (if the button is enabled). 4. Observe whether the input is accepted or rejected. ## Actual Result ### Issue 1 * The relation label name overflows the column or input field. * The modal becomes horizontally scrollable — a scrollbar appears and the layout shifts. * Content is pushed beyond the visible area, requiring sideways scrolling to view. * The modal does not truncate or wrap the long text. ### Issue 2 * The **Nilai** field accepts input of any length without restriction. * No character counter or limit indicator is displayed. * No validation warning or toast appears when exceeding 50 characters. * The system saves the full long value without enforcement. ## Expected Result ### Issue 1 * The modal should handle long relation label names without breaking the layout. * Text should either wrap to the next line or be truncated with an ellipsis. * Full text should remain accessible on hover or via tooltip. * The modal should not become horizontally scrollable regardless of input length. ### Issue 2 * The **Nilai** field should enforce a maximum of 50 characters per the PM's ruling. * A character counter (for example, "12/50") should be displayed near the input. * When the user tries to type beyond 50 characters, input should be blocked. * **If the user pastes text exceeding 50 characters, a toast warning should appear: "Maksimal 50 karakter."** * The **Terapkan** button should be disabled or blocked if the value exceeds the limit. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The "Beri Tag Relasi" modal does not handle text overflow — long values push the layout horizontally. * No maxlength attribute or JavaScript validation is present on the Nilai input field. * No character counter or visual feedback indicates remaining character budget. * The PRD (§10 Field & Validation) does not define a character limit for `relationAttributeValueDisplay` or `relationLabelDisplay`. * The only truncation guidance is EC-003: "Shared attribute display value is long (e.g. 50+ chars) → UI truncates display." This addresses display only, not input validation. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Beri Tag Relasi modal (CSS overflow handling) * Frontend — Nilai input field (missing maxlength attribute and validation) * Frontend — Relation label badge/chip component (overflow rendering) The root cause is twofold: 1. The PRD omitted a maximum character length for relation label values (§10 has no limit defined, unlike the Auto Tag PRD which caps keywords at 50 chars and rule names at 50 chars). 2. The modal's CSS layout does not constrain content width or apply `overflow: hidden` with `text-overflow: ellipsis`, allowing long text to expand the container. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Add `maxlength="50"` to the **Nilai** input field to prevent input beyond the limit. 2. Add a character counter below the input (for example, "24/50") that updates as the user types. 3. Block the **Terapkan** button or show inline validation when the value exceeds 50 characters. 4. Display a toast warning "Maksimal 50 karakter" when the user attempts to exceed the limit (via paste). 5. Fix the modal's CSS to handle overflow: constrain the column width and apply text truncation (`text-overflow: ellipsis`, `overflow: hidden`, `white-space: nowrap`) for long displayed values. Keep the full value accessible on hover via `title` attribute or tooltip. 6. Also apply the 50-character limit and truncation behavior to the relation label badge/chip component used in search result rows and detail pages. 7. Update the PRD §10 Field & Validation to document the 50-character maximum for `relationAttributeValueDisplay`. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: EC-003 — "Shared attribute display value is long (e.g. 50+ chars) → UI truncates display safely but keeps full value accessible on hover/detail." * **PM Confirmation**: The Product Manager confirmed a 50-character maximum limit should be enforced and the issues should be treated as low priority. * **PRD Gap**: §10 Field & Validation does not define a character limit for any relation label field. The Auto Tag PRD defines explicit limits (max 50 chars for keywords, max 50 chars for rule names) — this PRD should be updated to match that standard. * **Related Bug Reports**: * `beri-tag-relasi-modal-value-prefilled-without-attribute.md` — the same modal has pre-fill inconsistency issues. * `tag-relasi-edited-value-not-synced-to-modal.md` — the same modal has value sync issues. * **Priority**: Low — per PM confirmation.
