workPackages.description: # UI/UX Polish Collection > This document collects minor UI, UX, interaction, and visual polish observations found during exploratory testing. > > These observations are **not critical functional bugs**, but addressing them can improve consistency, usability, and the overall product experience. > > See the available ui/ux polish to fix on **Summary** Section > **Status information:** > \- Open (Not yet Fixed ⚠️) > \- Fixed(Already test and fixed) > \- New (New Bug/Error that needed to fix) # Overview # Observation 001 (Fixed✅) ## Title Dropdown field shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the **"Tipe atribut"** dropdown field inside the Relation Label modal, the mouse cursor remains the default arrow cursor. Since this component is clickable and opens a dropdown menu, the interaction feedback does not clearly communicate that the field is interactive. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer (`cursor: pointer`) when hovering over the dropdown field to indicate that the component is clickable. ### Notes This is a common UI convention — dropdown triggers should use a pointer cursor to signal interactivity. # Observation 002 (Fixed✅) ## Title Primary action button shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the **"Tandai Relasi"** button in the bottom action bar, the mouse cursor remains the default cursor. As this is a primary clickable action button, the default cursor does not clearly indicate that the component is interactive. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over the button to provide clear interaction feedback consistent with standard button behavior. ### Notes This affects all users and reduces the perceived responsiveness of the interface. # Observation 003 (Fixed✅) ## Title Secondary action button shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the **"Batal"** button in the bottom action bar, the mouse cursor remains the default cursor. The button is clickable and dismisses the action bar. A pointer cursor would provide consistent interaction feedback across all clickable action buttons. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over the button, matching the interaction behavior of other clickable elements. ### Notes Consistent cursor behavior across all buttons in the action bar improves the overall interaction model. # Observation 004 (Fixed✅) ## Title Dropdown menu options show default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the options inside the **"Tipe atribut"** dropdown menu (e.g., AWB, Order ID, Tracking, Invoice, Custom), the cursor remains the default cursor. Since each option is selectable, the cursor should provide consistent interactivity feedback throughout the dropdown menu. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over each dropdown option to indicate that the item is selectable. ### Notes This is consistent with standard dropdown menu behavior across most web applications. # Observation 005 (Fixed✅) ## Title Modal close button shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the modal close (**×**) button, the cursor remains the default cursor. The close icon is clickable and dismisses the modal. Using a pointer cursor would align with common UI interaction patterns and provide clearer visual feedback. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over the close button to indicate that the icon is clickable. ### Notes Modal close buttons universally use a pointer cursor across most modern web applications. # Observation 006 (Fixed✅) ## workPackages.subject: Release notes 2.8.0
workPackages.description:
**\# Apa yang Baru di SatuInbox v2.8.0**

  
  

**\## ✨ Fitur Baru**

  
  

\- **\*\*Related Conversations\*\*** — Percakapan yang berhubungan sekarang dikelompokkan otomatis di inbox, jadi konteks pelanggan lebih mudah dilihat.

\- **\*\*Related Tickets & Merge Suggestion\*\*** — Sistem sekarang menyarankan tiket yang mirip/berkaitan, dan bisa digabung supaya tim gak kerja dobel.

\- **\*\*Round Robin lebih pintar\*\*** — Pembagian percakapan ke agent sekarang pakai aturan batch, jadi gak ada lagi penumpukan (bottleneck) di satu agent.

\- **\*\*Sinkron kontak dengan Lincah\*\*** — Kontak SatuInbox otomatis nyambung dengan kontak Lincah.

\- **\*\*Unlink Relation Label\*\*** — Sekarang bisa "Hapus Relasi" (satu-satu atau sekaligus banyak) dengan konfirmasi, fitur yang sebelumnya belum ada.

\- **\*\*Auto-assign conversation ke team\*\*** — Percakapan yang belum ada pemiliknya otomatis masuk ke team begitu channel-nya ditambahkan ke team itu — gak perlu sync manual lagi.

\- **\*\*Validasi nomor WhatsApp via API\*\*** — Nomor WhatsApp bisa divalidasi lewat API terbuka (dipakai untuk integrasi Salfok).

\- **\*\*Fuzzy search di Global Search\*\*** — Pencarian sekarang lebih toleran typo, sama seperti pencarian di daftar percakapan.

\- **\*\*Widget chat baru untuk Lincah\*\*** — Perusahaan Lincah sekarang punya widget live chat sendiri.

  
  

**\## 🐞 Perbaikan Bug**

  
  

\- **\*\*Global Search jauh lebih cepat\*\*** — sebelumnya bisa gagal/lemot parah kalau banyak orang search bersamaan, sekarang sudah dibenahi.

\- **\*\*Global Search di tenant besar (>1000 percakapan/tiket)\*\*** — sebelumnya error, sekarang jalan normal.

\- Klik hasil Global Search gak lagi salah pencet checkbox, dan tombol "Hapus Relasi" yang sempat hilang sudah balik.

\- Gak bisa lagi pilih hasil Conversation dan Ticket bersamaan di Global Search (dulu bikin bingung).

\- Label relasi yang diedit sekarang benar-benar tersimpan dan muncul di modal.

\- Berbagai polesan kecil UI di Global Search (kursor, hover, pesan notifikasi lebih jelas).

\- Widget chat gak lagi kadang "skip" pesan pas server baru restart/rilis.

\- Badge label relasi di tiket sekarang muncul dengan benar di hasil pencarian.

\- Nama label relasi sekarang dibatasi 50 karakter, dan tampilan gak lagi berantakan untuk nama panjang.

\- Label yang sudah dihapus gak lagi nongol lagi di hasil pencarian lama.

\- Copy-paste di form pembuatan tiket sekarang berfungsi normal.

\- Template WhatsApp yang dibuat langsung di Meta Business Manager sekarang otomatis kesinkron ke sistem.

\- Modal "Lepas Label Relasi" gak lagi berantakan untuk nama label panjang.

\- Label relasi dengan nama 40+ karakter sekarang bisa dihapus (sebelumnya error).

\- Preview pesan di daftar percakapan sekarang terpotong rapi (…) alih-alih bisa di-scroll.

  
  

**\## ⏳ Belum Rilis (masih dalam proses, tidak masuk versi ini)**

  
  

\- Reconnect channel Instagram yang expired (masih testing)

\- Broadcast template WhatsApp dengan media (gagal test, perlu perbaikan)

workPackages.subject: Global Search — add fuzzy/typo-tolerant matching (gap vs conversation-list search)
workPackages.description:
## Summary

Global search's Atlas-backed relevance scoring is a strict exact/prefix/partial `$switch` ladder (`SCORE_EXACT`/`SCORE_PREFIX`/`SCORE_PARTIAL` in `conversation-search.repository.ts`; `SCORE.EXACT`/`NORMALIZED_EXACT`/`PREFIX`/`PARTIAL` in `ticket-search.repository.ts`) and deliberately excludes Atlas `fuzzy` matching. The conversation-list (inbox) search already supports typo-tolerant fuzzy matching via `fuzzy: {maxEdits: 1}` on `contactInfo.displayName` (`conversation.repository.ts:528`), so a typo in a contact name gets looser matching in the inbox list but not in global search.

## Why this happens (verified in code, not a bug)

`conversation-search-atlas.pipeline.ts` (and the ticket-service equivalent) explicitly omit `fuzzy` from their Atlas `$search` `should` clauses. The inline comment documents why: any fuzzy-only hit would score 0 in the current exact/prefix/partial ladder and get discarded by the `_scoreField > 0` guard — so naively adding `fuzzy` today would produce matches that are silently dropped, which is worse than the current state. This is an intentional design tradeoff, not a regression.

## Ask

Investigate/propose how to extend global search's relevance ladder with a fuzzy tier (e.g. a new lowest-priority `SCORE_FUZZY` rung below `SCORE_PARTIAL`) so typo-tolerant queries can surface results in global search, without breaking the deterministic exact > prefix > partial ordering that the `matchFields[]` highlight metadata depends on downstream.

## Where to look

*   `apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/conversation-search.repository.ts` — relevance ladder + `buildRelevancePipeline`
    
*   `apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/pipelines/conversation-search-atlas.pipeline.ts` — Atlas `should`\-clause builder (fuzzy-omission comment)
    
*   `apps/ticket-service/src/app/repositories/ticket-search.repository.ts` + its atlas pipeline — same pattern, ticket domain
    
*   `apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/conversation.repository.ts:528` — existing fuzzy usage in list search, as the reference pattern for how fuzzy is wired on the Atlas side
    

## Scope note

This is an improvement/investigation ticket, not a defect against existing behavior — filed as a child of #2410 (Global Search Suggestion - Improvement Perfomance) since it's the same "global search quality" track.

workPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Domain Ticket Relation label badges was not appear on global search result
workPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary After successfully applying a system relation label to a Ticket via the "Beri Tag Relasi" bulk action, the relation label badge does not appear on the Ticket result row in the Global Search popup. The label is correctly displayed on the Ticket Detail page, confirming the label was persisted. However, the Global Search result row for the same ticket shows no relation label badge — even after a hard browser refresh. This only apper on domain ticket, on conversation domain, this bug not appear. This inconsistency means users searching for a related ticket in Global Search cannot visually confirm that a relation label has already been applied to that record. The label is only discoverable by opening the Ticket Detail page, defeating the purpose of surfacing relation context in the search results. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Global Search popup and search for a keyword that returns Ticket results. 2. Select one or more Ticket results via checkbox. 3. Click **"Tandai Relasi"** in the Ticket bulk action bar. 4. In the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal, select a **Tipe atribut** and enter a **Nilai**, then click **Terapkan**. 5. Verify the success toast appears confirming the relation label was applied. 6. Navigate to the Ticket Detail page for the selected ticket and verify the relation label badge is visible — confirm the label was persisted. 7. Return to the Global Search popup and perform the same search again. 8. Perform a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R). 9. Locate the same Ticket result row. 10. Observe whether the relation label badge is displayed. ## Actual Result * The relation label badge is **visible** on the Ticket Detail page, confirming successful persistence. * The relation label badge is **not visible** on the same ticket's result row in the Global Search popup. * The badge remains absent even after a hard browser refresh. * Other result card fields (ticket ID, title, status) appear correctly. ## Expected Result * After a relation label is successfully applied to a Ticket, the label badge should appear on that ticket's result row in the Global Search popup. * The badge should be visible immediately after applying the label, or at minimum after a page refresh. * The relation label displayed in Global Search should match what is shown on the Ticket Detail page. * Conversation result rows should also consistently display their relation label badges (verify this domain for comparison). ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * Relation labels are correctly persisted — they appear on the Ticket Detail page after application. * Global Search result rows do not display the relation label badge for Tickets. * Hard refresh does not resolve the issue, suggesting a backend data fetch or rendering issue rather than a client-side cache problem. * The issue may be specific to the Ticket domain — Conversation result rows should be checked for comparison. * Result card rendering otherwise works correctly (ticket ID, title, status all display). ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend — Global Search API response for Ticket domain * Backend — Relation label inclusion in search index or query * Frontend — Ticket result row component (relation label badge rendering) The Global Search API response for Ticket results may not include relation label data, while the Ticket Detail API does. Alternatively, the search index may not be updated with relation label metadata after a bulk apply, causing the search results to return stale or incomplete data for the Ticket domain. The frontend may also have a rendering condition that only renders the relation label badge for Conversation result rows and omits it for Ticket rows. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Compare the Global Search API response for a Ticket with a relation label against the Ticket Detail API response — verify whether the relation label data is present in the search response. 2. Check whether the search index is updated after a relation label is applied to a Ticket. If the index is not refreshed, the label will never appear in search results. 3. Inspect the Ticket result row component to confirm the relation label badge rendering logic is implemented for the Ticket domain — it may only be wired for Conversation rows. 4. Repeat the same test on the Conversation domain to determine if the issue is domain-specific or global. 5. **Cross-reference with FR-022 \[P0\]: "Relation labels MUST be visible in a dedicated relation-label presentation area."** ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-022 \[P0\] — Relation labels MUST be visible in a dedicated relation-label presentation area and MUST NOT be indistinguishable from manual tags in the UI. * **Related Requirement**: FR-018 \[P0\] — Relation labels MUST support at minimum: attribute key, normalized value, display value, created source, and created timestamp. * **Precondition**: At least one Ticket exists in search results with a relation label successfully applied. * **Verification note**: Test on Conversation domain as well to determine if the issue is domain-specific (Ticket only) or cross-domain.

workPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Error when trying to open into related conversation
workPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary This report covers two related issues found in the Global Search actionable search result rows: **Issue 1 — Accidental Checkbox Selection**: When a user clicks a search result row in the Global Search popup to navigate to a Conversation Room, the click unintentionally triggers the per-row checkbox selection for "Tandai Relasi" instead of opening the target conversation. The user intended only to navigate — not to select the record for bulk action. **Issue 2 — "Hapus Relasi" Feature Not Yet Implemented**: The Figma design for the actionable search result row includes a "Hapus Relasi" (Remove Relation) button that allows users to unlink or delete a previously applied relation label. However, this feature has not been developed yet — neither the frontend button nor the backend deletion system exists in the current implementation. Once a relation label is applied to a record, there is no way for users to remove it. Based on this design [FigmaDesign](https://www.figma.com/design/RAAuLaQKUufWMWWEm0kMb9/-V2--Satuinbox-Web-Specs?node-id=12250-73420&t=dQuIT72klLsuPW1S-0) Both issues affect the same result row component, which is intended to carry navigation, selection, relation label display, and unlink actions. The missing "Hapus Relasi" feature means relation labels, once applied, are permanent — there is no undo or correction path for users. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce ### Issue 1 — Accidental Checkbox Selection 1. Open the Global Search popup by clicking **Cari** in the sidenav or pressing **Ctrl+K / Cmd+K**. 2. Enter a search keyword (for example, `JNE123456789` or `min`). 3. Wait for search results to load — verify Conversation and Ticket sections appear. 4. Click the body area of a Conversation result row with the intent to navigate to the Conversation Room. 5. Observe the result. ### Issue 2 — "Hapus Relasi" Feature Not Yet Implemented 1. Open the Global Search popup and search for a keyword that returns records with existing relation labels. 2. Locate a result row that displays a relation label chip (for example, `AWB • JNE123456789`). 3. Observe that there is no **"Hapus Relasi"** button or any user-facing action to unlink or remove the relation label from the record. ## Actual Result ### Issue 1 * The per-row checkbox for "Tandai Relasi" becomes selected (checked). * The bulk action bar appears showing "Percakapan dipilih: 1". * The user is **not** navigated to the Conversation Room on single click. * The Global Search popup remains open. ### Issue 2 * No "Hapus Relasi" button or unlink action is available on the search result row. * Relation labels, once applied, cannot be removed by the user through any available UI action. * There is no confirmation dialog, deletion endpoint, or unlink workflow implemented. ## Expected Result ### Issue 1 * Clicking the Conversation result row navigates the user to the Conversation Room with the Detail panel visible. * The Global Search popup closes automatically. * The checkbox should only become selected when the user explicitly clicks the checkbox element itself, not the surrounding row area. ### Issue 2 * A "Hapus Relasi" button should be displayed on result rows that carry an existing relation label, following the Figma design. * Clicking "Hapus Relasi" should display a confirmation dialog (for example, "Hapus relasi ini?"). * Upon confirmation, the relation label should be removed from the record. * A backend endpoint should handle the deletion and ensure the label is unlinked from the target record. * A toast notification should confirm successful removal (for example, "Relasi berhasil dihapus"). * If deletion fails, an error toast should be displayed (for example, "Gagal menghapus relasi. Coba lagi."). ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The result row responds to a click by selecting the checkbox, not by navigating. * The checkbox click target appears to cover or overlap the row's main clickable area. * The bulk action bar appears immediately upon accidental selection. * No navigation occurs when clicking the row body. * No "Hapus Relasi" button exists on search result rows — the unlink feature has not been developed. * The Figma design includes this button, but neither the frontend component nor the backend deletion endpoint exists in the current implementation. * Relation labels, once applied, are permanent with no undo or correction path available to users. ## Possible Root Cause Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Search result row component (click event delegation) * Frontend — Checkbox click event propagation * Frontend — "Hapus Relasi" button event handler (missing or not wired) * Backend — Relation label deletion endpoint (may not exist or not integrated) **Issue 1**: The checkbox element's click handler may be capturing click events that should fall through to the row's navigation handler. Alternatively, the checkbox's visible or interactive area may be sized to cover the entire row rather than being constrained to the checkbox icon only. **Issue 2**: The "Hapus Relasi" feature has not been developed. The PRD (§2, §14, §20) lists unlink as out of scope for Phase 1, which may explain why the feature was deprioritized. However, the Figma design includes the button and interaction, indicating the design team intends for this feature to exist. The following components need to be built: * Frontend — "Hapus Relasi" button component on search result rows (with relation label chips) * Frontend — Confirmation modal ("Hapus relasi ini?") * Backend — Relation label deletion endpoint * Backend — Audit log for deletion events ## Recommendation ### Issue 1 — Checkbox vs Navigation 1. Verify the HTML structure of the search result row — ensure the checkbox is an independent click target, not a child element that captures row-level click events. 2. Confirm that `event.stopPropagation()` or equivalent is applied so that clicking the checkbox does not trigger row navigation, and clicking the row body does not trigger checkbox selection. 3. Visually reduce the checkbox's interactive hit area to only the checkbox icon, leaving the remainder of the row for navigation. 4. Review against PRD FR-001: "Clicking a Conversation result MUST open Conversation Room with Detail panel visible by default." ### Issue 2 — "Hapus Relasi" Feature Development 1. Develop the "Hapus Relasi" button component per the Figma design — display it on search result rows that have an existing relation label. 2. Wire the button to a new backend endpoint for relation label deletion (for example, `DELETE /api/relation-label/{id}`). 3. Add a confirmation modal with title "Hapus relasi ini?" and buttons "Batal" / "Hapus." 4. Upon successful deletion, show a success toast: "Relasi berhasil dihapus." 5. Upon failure, show an error toast: "Gagal menghapus relasi. Coba lagi." 6. Ensure the relation label chip is removed from the result row after successful deletion. 7. Log deletion events for audit purposes (who deleted, which label, timestamp). 8. Coordinate with PM to confirm this feature should be included in Phase 1 despite the PRD listing unlink as out of scope — the Figma design indicates it should exist. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-001 \[P0\] — Clicking a Conversation result MUST open Conversation Room with Detail panel visible. * **Related Requirement**: FR-005 \[P0\] — Search results MUST support checkbox selection per result row. * **PRD Out of Scope**: §2, §14, §20 — Unlink, relation graph editing, and automatic cleanup are explicitly listed as out of scope for Phase 1. * **Design-PRD Discrepancy**: The "Hapus Relasi" button exists in the UI design, but the PRD says unlink is out of scope. This should be clarified with the PM — either the button should be removed, or the PRD scope should be updated to include unlink. * **Precondition**: User is authenticated (Admin, Supervisor, or Agent role) and has accessed the Global Search popup with valid search results. * Both issues were discovered during exploratory testing of the actionable search feature before formal test case execution.

workPackages.subject: Hapus Relasi (Unlink Relation Label) — feature not implemented anywhere in the codebase
workPackages.parentName: Global Search Suggestion - Error when trying to open into related conversation
workPackages.description:
## Summary
Split out from Issue 2 of #2607. A `RelationLabel` can be **applied** to a conversation/ticket (bulk, from Global Search) but there is no way to **remove** it afterward — no gRPC RPC, no REST route, no UI affordance exists in either repo. Once applied, a relation label is permanent.

Verified via codebase grep (2026-07-30): no `UnlinkRelationLabel`/`RemoveConversationRelationLabel`/`RemoveTicketRelationLabel` symbols exist anywhere in `omnichannel-satuinbox-be`, and no `unlink`/`Hapus Relasi` component or hook exists anywhere in `omnichannel-satuinbox-fe`.

## Current State
- `POST /search/relation-labels/apply` → `ConversationService.BulkApplyRelationLabel` / `TicketService.BulkApplyRelationLabel` pushes a label onto `conversation.relationLabels[]` / `ticket.relationLabels[]`.
- `RelationLabelChip` only supports `onFilter` — no remove affordance.
- `RelationLabelSection` (conversation/ticket detail) has no unlink wiring.
- Global Search bulk bar only has "Apply relation label" — no "Unlink relation label" action.

## Desired State (per Figma)
- "Hapus Relasi" button on search result rows / relation chips that carry an existing label.
- Confirmation modal ("Hapus relasi ini?" / Batal / Hapus).
- New single-item unlink RPC + gateway route (mirrors existing tag-remove pattern) for conversation and ticket detail.
- New bulk unlink RPC + gateway route (mirrors existing bulk-apply pattern) for the Global Search bulk bar.
- Success/error toasts ("Relasi berhasil dihapus." / "Gagal menghapus relasi. Coba lagi.").

## Implementation Plan
A full implementation plan already exists at `.claude/PRPs/plans/unlink-relation-label.plan.md` (both repos, ~34 files: proto + conversation-service + ticket-service + api-gateway + frontend hooks/components/i18n). Not yet started — no related code exists in either repo's working tree or git history.

## Out of Scope (per plan)
- `RelationLabel` document deletion/reference-counting in company-service.
- Multi-select inside the related-items panel (bulk unlink lives in Global Search only).
- Automated FE tests (no FE test runner configured in this codebase).

## Related
- Parent: #2607 (bundles this as "Issue 2")
- Related PRD: #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search"
- PRD explicitly lists unlink as out of scope for Phase 1 (§2, §14, §20) — Figma design includes the button regardless; flagged as a design/PRD discrepancy in #2607, needs PM confirmation on scope.

workPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Can't delete the relation label with 40+ relation label char
workPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary When a user attempts to release ("Lepas Label Relasi") a relation label whose name contains 40 or more characters, the action fails with an error — even though the label name is still within the allowed 50-character maximum. The relation label cannot be unlinked from the record, and an error is returned instead of a successful release. This is a functional blocker, not a layout issue: unlike the previously reported overflow problem, here the release action itself fails. Users who applied a long relation label (40–50 characters) are unable to remove or correct it, which is especially problematic because the "Hapus/Lepas Relasi" feature is the only correction path for misapplied labels. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Apply a relation label with a name of 40 or more characters (for example, a 42-character value) to a Conversation or Ticket via the "Beri Tag Relasi" flow. 2. Verify the label was applied successfully. 3. Open the Global Search popup and search for the keyword matching that record. 4. Locate the result row with the long relation label badge. 5. Click the **"Lepas Label Relasi"** action. 6. Complete the confirmation flow (if the modal appears). 7. Observe the result. ## Actual Result * Clicking "Lepas Label Relasi" on a relation label with 40+ characters results in an **error**. * The relation label is **not released** — it remains applied to the record. * An error message or failed state is displayed (no successful release toast). * The failure occurs even though the label name is below the 50-character maximum limit (40–49 characters fails). * The behavior appears on relation labels within the valid length range, suggesting a bug in the release logic rather than a validation rejection. ## Expected Result * "Lepas Label Relasi" should successfully release any relation label whose name is within the allowed character limit (up to 50 characters). * The label should be removed from the record after confirmation. * A success toast should confirm the release (for example, "Relasi berhasil dilepas"). * Labels between 40–50 characters should behave identically to shorter labels — the release action must not fail based on label name length. * If a genuine validation limit exists, it should be enforced consistently with a clear message — but 40+ chars is below the documented 50-char maximum, so this should succeed. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The release action fails for relation labels with 40+ characters. * Labels under 40 characters release successfully (to be confirmed with exact threshold). * The label name is within the valid range (below 50 chars) — so this is not a validation rejection. * The error appears to come from the release operation itself, not from UI validation. * The exact character threshold (40 vs 41 vs 45) should be confirmed during investigation. * The issue may share a root cause with the related overflow bug — the release logic or endpoint may not handle long label values correctly. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend — Relation label release/delete endpoint * Backend — Relation label key generation or lookup for long values * Frontend — Release action request payload for long label names The release operation may use the relation label key (for example, `rel..`) to identify the label to release. For long label values, the generated key or the request payload may exceed an internal limit — for example, a database column length, an API request size constraint, or a backend validation that rejects keys above a certain length — causing the release to fail even though the label name itself is within the user-facing 50-char limit. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Reproduce with labels of varying lengths to determine the exact failing threshold (40, 45, 49 characters). 2. Inspect the release request payload — verify the relation label key/value is transmitted correctly for long names. 3. Check the backend release endpoint for any length-based validation or column-length limits that may reject long relation label keys. 4. Verify the fix ensures labels up to the 50-character maximum can be released without error. 5. Test the release action on both Conversation and Ticket domains, and with labels at exactly 40, 45, 49, and 50 characters. 6. Coordinate with the overflow fix (related issue) to ensure the release modal also handles long labels without layout breakage. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-021 \[P0\] — Applying the same relation label twice MUST NOT create duplicates (label lifecycle management is in scope). * **PM Confirmation**: The 50-character maximum for relation label names has been confirmed by PM (see related report on character limit). Labels within this limit must function correctly. * **Related Bug Reports**: * #2981 the release confirmation modal breaks horizontally for 45+ character labels (UI layout issue). * **Distinction**: This report is a **functional error** (release action fails), NOT the UI overflow issue reported separately. Both affect long relation labels and may share a root cause, but they are distinct symptoms. * **Threshold note**: The exact failing threshold (40 vs 45 characters) should be verified during investigation.

allWorkPackages.subject: Whatsapp API - handle account channel status update
allWorkPackages.description:
# Root cause analysis (code trace, v2.8.2 — no repro environment available)

Two independent defects, both in `apps/whatsapp-api`.

## Defect 1 — account status webhooks are never handled

`WhatsappApiWebhookEventTypeEnum` already declares `ACCOUNT_UPDATE`, `ACCOUNT_BANNED`,
`ACCOUNT_REINSTATED`, `PHONE_NUMBER_QUALITY_UPDATE`, `BUSINESS_STATUS_UPDATE`
(`libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts:583-597`) but **nothing produces or consumes them**.

Evidence:

- `WebhookResolverFactory` registers only three resolvers — incoming message, message
  status, template status (`apps/whatsapp-api/src/app/factories/webhook-resolver.factory.ts:40-44`).
- No resolver's `canResolve()` matches Meta's `account_update` /
  `phone_number_quality_update` / `business_status_update` fields.
  `IncomingMessageResolver` keys off `value.messages`, `MessageStatusResolver` off
  `value.statuses`, `TemplateStatusResolver` off `field === 'message_template_status_update'`.
- Therefore every account webhook falls through to
  `createUnknownEvent()` (`webhook-resolver.factory.ts:63-66`).
- `WebhookEventEmitterService.emit()` looks the type up in
  `WHATSAPP_API_WEBHOOK_TO_EVENT_MAP`, which contains only message + status entries
  (`libs/common/src/lib/maps/whatsapp-api-type.maps.ts:30-42`), gets `null`, and drops the
  event through `handleUnmappedEvent()` — a `warn`/`debug` log line and nothing else
  (`webhook-event-emitter.service.ts:60-65, 87-94`).

Net effect: when Meta bans a WABA, the webhook is persisted in `webhooklogs`, logged as
UNKNOWN, and the `accountchannels` row keeps `connectionStatus: active` forever. There is
no code path from a Meta account webhook to `ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_UPDATED`.

Note the contrast with whatsapp-web (Baileys), which does handle this correctly:
a `forbidden` disconnect maps to `ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_CONNECTION_STATUS_SUSPENDED` and any
other terminal close to `INACTIVE`
(`apps/whatsapp/src/app/services/whatsapp-connection.service.ts:431-437`).

## Defect 2 — account channel is created before OAuth is proven complete

`AccountSetupService.completeEmbeddedSignup()`
(`apps/whatsapp-api/src/app/services/account-setup.service.ts:260-294`) performs no
status check on the OAuth state it loads.

- `resolveOauthState(id, phoneNumberId)` (line 404) only asserts the document exists.
  When `phoneNumberId` is passed it *force-sets* `status = COMPLETED` and saves
  (lines 417-422) — so the state is marked complete before any Meta call succeeds.
- `registerWebhookAndPhoneNumber()` (line 524) is the first thing that validates
  `accessToken` / `whatsappBusinessId` / `selectedPhoneNumberId`, and it throws
  `GrpcNotFoundException` when they are missing.
- If the OAuth callback never ran (user abandoned the Meta dialog, or
  `handleOAuthCallback` failed before `updateOauthStateWithPhoneNumbers`), the state has
  no `accessToken`, so the throw happens — but only *after* `resolveOauthState` already
  flipped the status to COMPLETED and persisted it.
- Conversely, if the caller retries after a partially successful flow, the account
  channel is created with `connectionStatus: ACTIVE` and `accountStatus: USED`
  (lines 272-284) while the OAuth state may still lack a working token.

Cascading effect (inferred from the read paths, not observed in a live DB): inbound
resolution uses
`findCompletedByBusinessIdAndPhoneId(businessId, phoneNumberId)` with
`status: COMPLETED` (`repositories/oauth-state.repository.ts:52-61`), and outbound uses
`findCompletedByAccountChannelId` (line 70). A prematurely-COMPLETED state satisfies both
queries, so the account channel appears connected in the UI while
`IncomingMessageProcessorService.process()` and `CoreService.handleSendMessage()` operate
on an OAuth record with no usable `accessToken` — messages and conversations silently fail
to process, which matches the reported symptom.

# Fix plan

1. **New `AccountStatusResolver`** in `apps/whatsapp-api/src/app/resolvers/` matching
   Meta's `account_update`, `phone_number_quality_update` and `business_status_update`
   fields; register it in `WebhookResolverFactory` and add the corresponding
   `WHATSAPP_API_WEBHOOK_TO_EVENT_MAP` entries plus a new `EventTypeEnum` topic.
2. **Consume the event in whatsapp-api** and emit `ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_UPDATED` with
   `SUSPENDED` for a ban and `ACTIVE` on reinstate, mirroring the whatsapp-web mapping
   above so both channels behave identically. Resolve the target account channel from the
   OAuth state via business id + phone number id.
3. **Guard `completeEmbeddedSignup`**: require `accessToken` and a resolved
   `whatsappBusinessId` before creating the account channel, and stop
   `resolveOauthState` from setting `COMPLETED` as a side effect of reading. Phone
   selection should persist `selectedPhoneNumberId` only; the COMPLETED transition
   belongs to the callback that actually obtained the token.
4. Unit specs for the new resolver, the status mapping, and the guard.

Branch: `fix/2208-wa-api-account-channel-status` (off `origin/v2.8.2`).

allWorkPackages.subject: notification-service crashes on RabbitMQ consumer_timeout (reminder-queue)
allWorkPackages.description:
**Incident (production, 2026-08-20 ~07:18 AM):** notification-service crashed and restarted.

**Symptom:**
```
ERROR [Server] Disconnected from RMQ. Trying to reconnect.
ERROR [Server] err: Error: Channel closed by server: 406 (PRECONDITION-FAILED)
  "PRECONDITION_FAILED - delivery acknowledgement on channel 1 timed out.
   Timeout value used: 1800000 ms."

Error: channel closed
    at ConfirmChannel.<anonymous> (amqplib/lib/channel.js:43:14)
    ...
Node.js v22.19.0   <- process crashed
```

**Root cause (two layers):**
1. `reminder-queue` (subscription reminder/comeback emails) runs with `noAck: false` (`createRabbitMQDelayedQueueMicroservice`, libs/common/src/lib/utils/main.utils.ts). NestJS holds a delivery unacked for the entire handler duration. `SesService`'s `SESv2Client` (apps/notification-service/src/app/services/ses.service.ts) had no request timeout configured (AWS SDK default is 0 = no timeout), so a stalled AWS SES call could hang a handler indefinitely. Once a delivery sat unacked past RabbitMQ's 30-minute `consumer_timeout`, the broker force-closed the channel (406).
2. Nothing in notification-service caught the resulting `unhandledRejection`/`uncaughtException` from amqplib's internal channel-close cleanup, so the whole Node process crashed instead of just failing that one message — taking down the gRPC server and the other RabbitMQ listener (in-app notifications, payment/token alerts, plan-changed emails) with it, since all three run in one process (main.ts `Promise.all`).

**Fix (branch `fix/notification-service-reminder-queue-crash` off v2.8.0.1):**
1. Give `SESv2Client` an explicit `requestHandler` timeout (connection 5s / request 10s) so a single send() can never hang unboundedly — bounds the trigger well under the 30-min broker timeout even across `@Retry()`'s 3 attempts.
2. Add `process.on('uncaughtException'/'unhandledRejection')` handlers to notification-service's main.ts (matching the existing pattern already used in `apps/whatsapp/src/main.ts`) so a future channel-close event logs cleanly and lets NestJS's own RMQ reconnect logic run, instead of crashing the process.

RabbitMQ itself was never at risk — force-closing the channel is expected broker behavior; only the consuming service crashed.

allWorkPackages.subject: Instagram token refresh queue stuck — 540 messages unacked, never processed
allWorkPackages.description:
**Symptom:** `instagram-token-refresh` queue sat at **540 messages** in Unacked state, appearing completely unprocessed. Backlog never drained.

**How the queue works:**
```
scheduleTokenRefreshForAccount()                token-refresh.service.ts:49
  -> emitWithDelay(x-delay = N days)  ------>   x-delayed-message exchange
                                                'instagram-token-refresh-exchange'
                                                  | routingKey 'instagram-token-refresh'
                                                queue 'instagram-token-refresh'
                                                  | noAck: false  (main.utils.ts:283)
  @EventPattern -> handleTokenRefresh()          token-refresh.service.ts:118
     refreshLongLivedToken() -> reschedule next delay
```
Registered in `apps/instagram/src/main.ts:45` via `createRabbitMQDelayedQueueMicroservice`. Instagram long-lived tokens last 60 days; refresh is scheduled 7 days before expiry (`DAYS_BEFORE_REFRESH`), capped at 49 days by the delayed-message plugin's 2^32 ms ceiling.

**Root cause (three bugs):**

**1. Consumer never acks — the actual cause.**
`handleTokenRefresh` (apps/instagram/src/app/services/token-refresh.service.ts:118) had no `RmqContext` parameter and never called `channel.ack()`, while its queue is created with `noAck: false` (libs/common/src/lib/utils/main.utils.ts:283). Every message was delivered, processed, and then left hanging unacked forever — hence 540 in Unacked, nothing removed. Instagram was the **only** delayed consumer in the repo missing this; ticket.controller.ts:398, export-report-job.processor.ts:76, broadcast-reset.processor.ts:100 and contact-sync.processor.ts:48 all ack correctly.

Knock-on effect: after ~30 min RabbitMQ's `consumer_timeout` force-closes the channel and redelivers the whole backlog — so those tokens were likely being refreshed repeatedly in a loop, not never. Same broker behavior as #3328, but here it manifested as a stuck queue rather than a process crash.

**2. Wrong pattern constant in the manual trigger.**
`scheduleTokenRefresh()` (line 96) published with `MessageQueuePatterns.INSTAGRAM_TOKEN_REFRESH` = `'instagram.token.refresh'` while the consumer listens on `MessageQueueName.INSTAGRAM_TOKEN_REFRESH` = `'instagram-token-refresh'` (libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts:872 vs :1004). The routing key matched so messages entered the queue, but no handler matched the packet pattern, so NestJS `nack(false, false)`'d them straight into `instagram-token-refresh.dlq`. Every manually-triggered batch refresh silently dead-lettered. `scheduleTokenRefreshForAccount` (line 67) and app.service.ts:155 already used the correct constant.

**3. Unbounded prefetch on all delayed queues.**
`createRabbitMQDelayedQueueMicroservice` never passed `prefetchCount`, so NestJS fell back to its default of `0` = unlimited. That is why the entire 540-message backlog landed on a single consumer at once instead of being throttled. The non-delayed sibling factory (`createRabbitMQMessageQueueMicroservice`, main.utils.ts:222) has always set it.

**Fix (branch `fix/instagram-token-refresh-queue-stuck-unacked` off v2.8.0.1):**
1. Add `@Ctx() context: RmqContext` to `handleTokenRefresh` and `channel.ack(originalMsg)` in a `finally` block — matching the established pattern in ticket-service / analytics-service / payment-service.
2. Publish the manual trigger with `MessageQueueName.INSTAGRAM_TOKEN_REFRESH` so the packet pattern matches the `@EventPattern`. Drop the now-unused `MessageQueuePatterns` import.
3. Pass `prefetchCount: rabbitMQConfig.prefetchCount` in `createRabbitMQDelayedQueueMicroservice` (env `RABBITMQ_PREFETCH`, default 10).

**Blast radius note for review:** fix 3 touches shared code and therefore affects every delayed queue — ticket, payment, broadcast, analytics, notification, conversation transcript. It is a correctness improvement (unlimited prefetch defeats fair dispatch and inflates unacked counts), but it does change their effective concurrency from unlimited to 10, so it warrants a deliberate ack from reviewers rather than being waved through.

**Recovery for the stuck 540:** deploy, then restart the instagram pod. The unacked messages are requeued by the broker on channel close and the fixed consumer drains them at 10 in flight, ~2s apart per `REFRESH_DELAY_MS`.

**Known remaining gap (deliberately out of scope):** `handleTokenRefresh` swallows all errors and then acks, so a failed refresh is dropped with no retry — the account is never rescheduled and its token quietly expires. Needs a reschedule-on-failure path with backoff; worth a separate ticket.

**Verification:** `npx nx build instagram` passing, `npx eslint` clean on both changed files. Pre-existing `sort-keys` lint errors in `webpack.config.js` / `jest.config.ts` are untouched and unrelated.

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation - Message - WhatsApp group on-demand history sync (fetchMessageHistory) with progress indicator
allWorkPackages.description:
## Masalah

Setelah full sync history (scan QR), pesan di grup WhatsApp tidak selalu 100% masuk ke SatuInbox. Sync awal hanya satu kali dan dibatasi (default 30 hari / 50 pesan per chat, lihat `WHATSAPP_HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_AGE_DAYS` dan `WHATSAPP_HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_CHAT`). Tidak ada cara bagi agent untuk mengambil pesan yang lebih lama setelah itu. Contoh: grup 1000 pesan, setelah scan hanya 100 yang masuk, sisa 900 tidak bisa diambil.

## Perilaku sekarang

- History hanya masuk lewat event Baileys `messaging-history.set` saat sync awal (raw store, drain, queue backfill #2597).
- `fetchMessageHistory` belum dipakai di mana pun di BE.
- Tidak ada tombol atau endpoint untuk sync per conversation.

## Perilaku yang diharapkan

1. **Manual:** di chat room grup WhatsApp Web, agent mana pun yang boleh membuka conversation bisa menekan tombol "Muat pesan lama". BE memanggil `fetchMessageHistory` (maks 50 pesan per request), jangkar bergeser mundur, berulang sampai batas halaman, respons kosong, atau timeout. Klik berikutnya melanjutkan dari pesan tertua di DB.
2. **Rate limit:** satu sesi per grup (lock Redis), jeda 10 detik antar halaman, budget 20 halaman per grup per 24 jam, maks 10 halaman per klik. Respons kosong menandai grup `exhausted` 7 hari.
3. **Auto:** setelah sync awal selesai, BE mengambil pesan lama untuk grup secara terbatas (maks 20 grup, urut dari grup dengan pesan terbaru). Default OFF sampai spike dan soak test di dev selesai.
4. **Progress di FE:** banner di chat room dengan state: meminta, memuat (halaman N dari M), menyimpan (persisted/received), selesai (ada lagi), semua dimuat, batas harian, timeout, dimuat oleh agent lain. Status disimpan di Redis dan tersedia lewat `GET /conversation/:id/history-sync/status`, jadi tetap benar setelah refresh.
5. **Guard backfill:** pesan history tidak boleh menggeser `latestMessage`/`timestamp`, menaikkan `unread`, atau menimpa `lastReEngagementAt` pada conversation yang sudah aktif.

## Di luar lingkup

- Chat direct (1:1) dan channel selain WhatsApp Web (termasuk Meta Cloud API).
- Mengisi lubang di tengah (antara dua pesan yang sudah ada).
- Mengubah request history sync awal Baileys (`requireFullSync`, dll).

## Belum terverifikasi (Task 0 / spike, butuh akun WA test)

- Apakah id yang dikembalikan `fetchMessageHistory` sama dengan `peerDataRequestSessionId` di respons.
- Bentuk `remoteJid` untuk grup dan chat LID.
- Perilaku saat HP utama offline, dan seberapa dalam HP masih menyimpan pesan (request dijawab oleh HP utama, bukan server WhatsApp).

## Rencana

Plan lengkap: `.hermes/PRPs/plans/whatsapp-on-demand-history-sync.plan.md`. Dibagi 3 MR: MR-1 BE (guard backfill, ingest ON_DEMAND, endpoint manual, socket event), MR-2 FE (tombol + banner), MR-3 auto mode.

Terkait: #2597 (history-sync backfill isolation), #3937 (history-sync backfill drops own group messages).

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - No toast message when release relation label on conversation/ticket detail
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary When a user releases ("Lepas Label Relasi") a relation label from a Conversation or Ticket detail, **no toast message is displayed** — the user receives no feedback about whether the release succeeded or failed. After the action completes, the user must visually verify the label was removed by checking the result row or detail page themselves. The Product Manager has confirmed that a toast message **must** appear when a relation label is released, to provide visibility of the action's status. Without it, the user cannot distinguish between: * A successful release (label removed) — no confirmation shown * A failed release (label still applied) — no error shown * A release still in progress — no loading state shown This silent feedback gap leaves users uncertain whether the action actually worked, which is especially critical when the release fails — the user may assume the label was removed when it was not. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Apply a relation label to a Conversation or Ticket (via "Beri Tag Relasi"). 2. Open the Global Search popup and search for the keyword matching that record. 3. Locate the result row displaying the relation label badge. 4. Click the **"Lepas Label Relasi"** action. 5. Also try to release the relation label via conversation/ticket detail (click the x button in relation label) 6. Complete the confirmation flow (if a confirmation modal appears). 7. Observe the screen after the action completes — specifically for any toast or status message. ## Actual Result * After releasing a relation label, **no toast message appears**. * No success confirmation (for example, "Relasi berhasil dilepas") is shown when the release succeeds. * No error message (for example, "Gagal melepas relasi. Coba lagi.") is shown when the release fails. * No loading or in-progress indicator is displayed during the release request. * The user receives zero feedback about the outcome of the action. ## Expected Result * A **success toast** must appear after a successful release, confirming the action, for example: "Relasi berhasil dilepas." * An **error toast** must appear when the release fails, with a retry hint, for example: "Gagal melepas relasi. Coba lagi." * The toast should appear immediately after the action completes and auto-dismiss after a standard duration. * Ideally, a brief loading state should be shown while the release request is in flight. * This behavior must apply consistently on both the Conversation and Ticket domains. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The release action completes without any visible feedback. * No toast, snackbar, banner, or inline message appears after release. * The user must rely on the result row or detail page state to infer whether the release worked. * The missing feedback is especially problematic on failure — a silent failure is indistinguishable from a successful release. * The issue appears on both Conversation and Ticket domains (to be verified). * The PRD (§7 Error Handling) defines toasts for the **apply** flow (for example, EH-005: "Sebagian label berhasil diterapkan") but contains **no** toast requirement for the **release** flow — a documentation gap confirmed by PM. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — "Lepas Label Relasi" action handler (missing toast call after success/failure) * Frontend — Notification/toast utility not wired to the release flow The release action likely completes its API call and updates state, but the success/failure toast invocation is missing from the action handler. The apply flow (Beri Tag Relasi) has toast feedback, but the release flow was implemented without the equivalent notification — likely because the PRD does not document release-flow messaging. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Add a success toast on successful release: "Relasi berhasil dilepas." 2. Add an error toast on failed release: "Gagal melepas relasi. Coba lagi." 3. Wire the toast calls into the release action handler — success path and error path separately. 4. Add a loading/disabled state on the release button while the request is in flight, to prevent double-submission and show progress. 5. Ensure the toast behavior is consistent on both Conversation and Ticket domains. 6. Update the PRD §7 Error Handling to document release-flow messages (EH-007+), so the requirement is traceable. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **PM Confirmation**: Product Manager confirmed that a toast message must appear when releasing a relation label, for visibility of status information. * **PRD Gap**: §7 Error Handling defines messages for apply/bulk actions (EH-001 → EH-006) but has no entry for the release/delete flow — the release feature comes from the Figma design, not the PRD. * **Consistency Reference**: The apply flow already shows toasts (for example, EH-005 "Sebagian label berhasil diterapkan") — the release flow should follow the same pattern. * **Domain**: Expected on both Conversation and Ticket domains — verify during fix.

allWorkPackages.subject: WA Web Multi-Library: whatsmeow Connector Architecture Brief
allWorkPackages.description: ## Background WhatsApp Web integration saat ini hanya pakai **Baileys** (`7.0.0-rc13`). PRD V2 (US-2) sudah mendesain arsitektur multi-library: Baileys (primary), WhatsAppWebJS (backup), "extensible for future". Tapi belum ada adapter layer — Baileys dipanggil langsung dari `whatsapp` service. **whatsmeow** adalah Go library untuk WA Web Multi-Device protocol. Sama-sama speak Noise Protocol + Signal Protocol seperti Baileys, tapi runtime berbeda (Go vs Node.js). ## Mengapa whatsmeow? * **Redundansi runtime:** Kalau Baileys kena breaking change dari WA update, Go ecosystem punya independent fix cycle. * **Performance:** Go lebih efisien untuk high-concurrency session management (ribuan account). * **PRD compliance:** Memenuhi intent US-2 "extensible for future libraries". ## Analisa Arsitektur ### Option A: Separate Go Microservice (Recommended) ```text ┌─────────────────┐ gRPC/RabbitMQ ┌──────────────────┐ │ whatsapp service │ ◄──────────────────► │ whatsapp-mew │ │ (NestJS) │ proto contract │ (Go + whatsmeow) │ │ Baileys │ │ port :50XX │ └──────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ ``` * `whatsapp` service tetap handle Baileys accounts * `whatsapp-mew` = Go microservice baru, handle whatsmeow accounts * Shared proto contract: `ConnectAccount`, `SendMessage`, `DisconnectAccount`, `GetQRCode`, event stream * `channel-service` punya `connectorType` field: `baileys` | `whatsmeow` * Gateway routes tetap sama — routing berdasarkan `connectorType` ### Credential Sharing **TIDAK portable.** Baileys credential (JSON authState) ≠ whatsmeow (SQL rows). Switch connector = **re-scan QR**. Bukan hot-failover, tapi cold-switch. ### Switch Strategy * Default: semua account pakai Baileys (production-proven) * whatsmeow = fallback manual saat Baileys kena breaking change * Bukan auto-rotate — manual switch via admin UI ## Scope Pekerjaan **Total: ~9-12 engineering days** ## Risks 1. **Credential tidak portable** — switch connector = re-qr. Downtime saat switch. 2. **Go runtime di infra** — DevOps perlu build + deploy pipeline untuk Go binary. 3. **Two codebases untuk satu protocol** — maintenance burden ganda saat WA update. 4. **whatsmeow less battle-tested** di SaaS scale dibanding Baileys. ## Rekomendasi **Bangun dulu** `**ConnectorAdapter**` **interface** (1d) — ini cheap dan bikin future whatsmeow integration plug-and-play tanpa refactor besar. Build the interface, not the implementation. **Sisanya (full microservice) build when:** Baileys actually breaks atau WA protocol diverge cukup justify dual-runtime. ## Dependencies * PRD V2 file 1 (US-2): Multi-library connectors * PRD V2 file 3: Bulk Scan QR (connector-aware) * Anti-Ban Guard: `OutboundSendQueue` per connector instance ## Open Questions * [ ] Apakah credential format bisa di-abstract ke unified store? (research spike) * [ ] Apakah whatsmeow support pairing code (bukan cuma QR)? * [ ] Infra readiness: Go build pipeline di GitLab CI?

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation - Message - album duplicated in group connected to account channels of different companies
allWorkPackages.description:
## Problem
Duplicate album messages appear in a WhatsApp group when the same group is connected through account channels that belong to two different companies.

## Current behaviour
Each company gets its own conversation for the group, but the album parent and children carry the same `externalMessageId` / `parentExternalMessageId` in both conversations.
`MessageRepository.populateAlbumMessages` (`apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/message.repository.ts`) matched children by `parentExternalMessageId` only, so every album parent also pulled in the other company's children and the album rendered duplicated images.

## Expected behaviour
An album only contains the children that belong to the same conversation (and therefore the same company) as the parent message.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Connect the same WhatsApp group through account channels in two different companies.
2. Receive an album (multiple images) in the group.
3. Open the group conversation in either company: the album shows duplicated items.

## Proposed fix
Scope the album-children query to the parent's `conversationId` (messages do not store `companyId`; the conversation already belongs to exactly one company).

## Note
`getConversationHistoryMessages` caches results in Redis for one week per conversation; history cached before the fix keeps the duplicates until the entry is cleared or expires.

## Masalah
Saat membuka detail conversation **grup**, FE tetap memanggil `GET /api/conversation-sla-metrics/:conversationId` dan selalu mendapat **404 Not Found**. Grup tidak punya SLA otomatis, jadi dokumen SLA metrics memang tidak ada.

## Kondisi saat ini (hasil baca kode)
- `ConversationAssigneeContent` (`apps/omnichannel/components/molecules/conversations/chat-detail/content/ConversationAsigneeContent.tsx`) memanggil `useGetConversationSLAMetrics` dengan `enabled: Boolean(activeConversation?.id)` saja.
- Tampilan SLA untuk grup sudah disembunyikan (`slaItems: activeConversation?.isGroup ? [] : slaItems`), tapi query tetap jalan sehingga request 404 tetap terkirim.

## Perilaku yang diharapkan
- Untuk conversation grup (`isGroup === true`), FE tidak mengirim request `conversation-sla-metrics`.
- Conversation non-grup tidak berubah: SLA metrics tetap di-fetch dan ditampilkan.

## Steps To Reproduce
1. Buka Inbox, pilih conversation grup.
2. Buka panel detail conversation (bagian Assignee).
3. Lihat tab Network: `GET /api/conversation-sla-metrics/<id>` -> 404.

## Solusi
Tambahkan `&& !activeConversation?.isGroup` pada `enabled` query `useGetConversationSLAMetrics` di komponen tersebut (perubahan FE satu baris).

allWorkPackages.subject: WhatsApp - Inbound media download fails and saves empty message (no reupload/retry/marker)
allWorkPackages.description:
## Masalah

Pesan gambar/media WhatsApp masuk kadang tersimpan kosong: `content: ""` dan tanpa attachment. Agent hanya melihat bubble kosong, tanpa petunjuk bahwa media gagal diunduh.

## Perilaku saat ini (hasil penelusuran kode, belum dari DB)

- `downloadAndUploadMedia` (`apps/whatsapp/src/app/services/whatsapp-message.service.ts`) memanggil `downloadMediaMessage(msg, 'buffer', {})` tanpa argumen ctx. Tanpa `reuploadRequest`, Baileys tidak meminta ulang media ke device pengirim, jadi URL CDN yang sudah kedaluwarsa (404/410) langsung melempar error. Ini umum pada pesan lama / history-sync / device pengirim sempat offline.
- `catch` menelan error dan mengembalikan `null`, `getAttachment` mengembalikan `undefined`, lalu `extractMessageData` tetap mengembalikan pesan dengan `text: ''` dan tanpa attachment. Pesan kosong tersimpan tanpa penanda gagal.
- Tidak ada retry untuk error sementara (timeout, ECONNRESET, upload ke media-service gagal).

## Perilaku yang diharapkan

- Media yang URL-nya kedaluwarsa diunduh lewat reupload request Baileys.
- Error sementara di-retry beberapa kali dengan backoff; error permanen tidak di-retry.
- Jika tetap gagal, pesan tersimpan dengan penanda yang jelas (placeholder teks + `metaData.whatsapp.mediaDownloadFailed`), bukan kosong tanpa jejak, dan kegagalan tercatat di log dengan message id.

## Usulan perbaikan (BE `whatsapp`)

1. Teruskan `sock` ke `downloadAndUploadMedia` dan panggil `downloadMediaMessage(msg, 'buffer', {}, { logger, reuploadRequest: sock.updateMediaMessage })`.
2. Retry maksimal 3 kali dengan backoff pendek, hanya untuk error non-permanen.
3. Fallback placeholder + flag `mediaDownloadFailed` bila tetap gagal.

## Di luar cakupan

- Tombol / job "coba unduh ulang" (butuh menyimpan `mediaKey` + `directPath`), tiket terpisah bila diperlukan.
- Caption album tidak tampil: lihat #4021 (FE).

## Catatan

Akar masalah dari penelusuran kode; belum dikonfirmasi lewat dokumen pesan kosong di Mongo.

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation - Message - album sent as a reply fails proto serialization and loses its reply quote
allWorkPackages.description:
## Problem

Some conversations fail to load messages with:

```
Error serializing response: .conversation.Message.replyFromMessage: object expected in message list
```

## Cause

When a customer sends an album **as a reply** to another message:

1. WhatsApp puts the quote (`stanzaId`) on `albumMessage.contextInfo` and on each image child (`imageMessage.contextInfo`).
2. `getQuotedContext` (whatsapp service) ignored `albumMessage`, so the album parent was stored without `replyFromMessage`, while the image children kept it as a raw ObjectId.
3. `Message.album` is `repeated Message`, and `cleanMessageReplyFrom` only cleaned the top level and was skipped when the parent had no reply, so the children's unpopulated ObjectId reached gRPC serialization and failed.

## Fix

- conversation-service / common: `cleanMessageReplyFrom` also sanitizes every `album` child; message list and history endpoints always run it.
- whatsapp: read `albumMessage.contextInfo` so the album parent gets `replyFromMessage` for new albums.

## Notes

- Albums received before the fix keep no reply on the parent (no backfill).
- Reproduce: customer replies to a message with 2+ images, then open the conversation.

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation - Group - memberContactInfo kosong tidak terisi ulang saat inbound grup (safety net)
allWorkPackages.description:
## Masalah
`memberContactInfo` pada conversation grup WhatsApp Web bisa kosong dan tidak pernah terisi lagi selama conversation OPEN yang sama masih dipakai.

## Kondisi saat ini (hasil baca kode)
- `findOrCreateConversation` (conversation-service) hanya memakai `memberContactIds` / `memberLids` di cabang `createNewConversation`. Kalau `findActiveConversation` menemukan conversation, bagian ini dilewati.
- Update lain hanya lewat event Baileys `group-participants.update` (`handleParticipantsUpdate`) atau refresh manual FE `POST /conversation/:id/group-participants/refresh` (hanya terpicu saat popup mention terbuka dan daftar kosong).
- Akibatnya kalau conversation dibuat saat `memberContactIds` kosong (peserta tanpa phoneNumber / LID belum ter-resolve, gagal ambil group metadata, atau conversation lama), array tetap kosong. Mention picker FE kosong sampai agent memicu refresh.

## Perilaku yang diharapkan
Safety net: pada inbound grup untuk conversation yang sudah ada, jika `memberContactInfo` kosong dan payload inbound membawa `memberContactIds`, isi `memberContactInfo` dari kontak tersebut (termasuk `lid` dan flag admin). Bila sudah terisi, tidak diubah sama sekali.

## Batasan / di luar scope
- Tidak mengubah alur refresh saat conversation sudah punya member.
- Tidak mengubah cache `GROUP_META_DATA` (TTL 1 hari) maupun event participants update.
- Kegagalan backfill tidak boleh menggagalkan proses inbound (best-effort, hanya warning log).

## Implementasi
`ConversationService.backfillEmptyMemberContactInfo`, dipanggil dari `findOrCreateConversation` hanya untuk `isGroup`. Update memakai filter atomik (`memberContactInfo` tidak ada atau `$size: 0`) agar tidak menimpa hasil refresh yang berjalan bersamaan.

## How to test

No migration or config change is needed. Use a WhatsApp Web account channel connected to a group, and a MongoDB shell on the `conversations` collection.

**Scenario A: empty `memberContactInfo` is backfilled on the next inbound**
1. Pick an OPEN group conversation (`isGroup: true`) and note its `_id`.
2. Empty its snapshot: `db.conversations.updateOne({ _id: ObjectId('<id>') }, { $set: { memberContactInfo: [] } })`
3. Send a message in that WhatsApp group from any participant.
4. Read it back: `db.conversations.findOne({ _id: ObjectId('<id>') }, { memberContactInfo: 1 })`
5. Expected: `memberContactInfo` is filled with the group's participants (`id`, `displayName`, `phone`, and `lid` for LID-based participants). Admins have `isAdmin: true`.

**Scenario B: a missing sender is appended when the snapshot is not empty**
1. Pick an OPEN group conversation whose `memberContactInfo` has several members. Choose a participant X who is in the group.
2. Remove X from the snapshot: `db.conversations.updateOne({ _id: ObjectId('<id>') }, { $pull: { memberContactInfo: { id: ObjectId('<X contact id>') } } })`
3. Send a message in the group from X, then read the document back.
4. Expected: X is appended exactly once and the other members are unchanged.
5. Send a second message from X. Expected: still exactly one entry for X (no duplicate).

**Scenario C: sender already in the snapshot**
1. Pick an OPEN group conversation whose snapshot already contains the sender.
2. Note `memberContactInfo`, then send a message from that sender.
3. Expected: `memberContactInfo` is unchanged.

**Scenario D: non-group conversations**
1. Send a message in a normal 1:1 WhatsApp conversation.
2. Expected: no `memberContactInfo` write, and the inbound is processed as before.

**Failure path (optional)**
Make the people-service lookup fail (for example, stop `people-service`) and send a group message into a conversation with an empty snapshot. Expected: the message is still stored, and the conversation-service log shows a `group_member_contact_info_backfill_failed` warning with `conversationId` and `reason`.

**Automated tests**
`npx jest --config apps/conversation-service/jest.config.ts src/app/services/conversation.service.spec.ts -t "group safety net"` runs the 10 new tests; all should pass.

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation - Message - album caption not displayed (stored on child message)
allWorkPackages.description:
## Masalah

Pada pesan album WhatsApp yang dikirim dengan caption, caption tidak tampil di chatroom Omnichannel. Bubble hanya menampilkan gambar/video, teks captionnya hilang.

## Perilaku saat ini (hasil telusur kode)

WhatsApp mengirim album sebagai satu pesan parent `albumMessage` ditambah N pesan child `imageMessage`/`videoMessage`. Caption ada di child, bukan di parent.

1. **WA service.** `getTextMessage` (`apps/whatsapp/src/app/utils/baileys.util.ts:210`) membaca `conversation`, `extendedTextMessage.text`, `imageMessage.caption`, `videoMessage.caption`, dan `documentWithCaptionMessage`. Pesan `albumMessage` tidak punya field caption, jadi parent tersimpan dengan `content: ''`. Child tersimpan dengan `content` = caption dan `parentExternalMessageId` terisi lewat `getParentAlbumId` (`baileys.util.ts:487`).
2. **Conversation service.** `findByConversationId` (`apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/message.repository.ts:76-90`) membuang semua child dari list. `populateAlbumMessages` lalu menempelkan child ke `parent.album` (`message.repository.ts:147-196`).
3. **FE.**
   - `message-renderer/AlbumMessage.tsx` hanya mengambil `album.flatMap(i => i.attachments)`. `content` child dibuang.
   - `MessageContent` di `ConversationChatroomBuble.tsx` merender `message.content` milik parent, yang `''`.

Caption sebenarnya tersimpan di DB (di child), tapi tidak ada yang membacanya.

## Perilaku yang diharapkan

Caption album tampil di bawah grid media pada bubble album, seperti di aplikasi WhatsApp.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Dari HP, kirim album (2+ gambar) dengan caption ke nomor yang terhubung ke Satuinbox.
2. Buka percakapan di Omnichannel.
3. Bubble album tampil tanpa caption.

## Usulan perbaikan

FE: untuk parent bertipe `album` dengan `content` kosong, render `content`/`mentions`/`mentionAll` dari child pertama di `album[]` yang punya `content`. Helper `resolveTextSourceMessage` di `apps/omnichannel/helpers/message-utils.ts`, dipakai oleh `MessageContent`. Tanpa migrasi, data lama ikut terbenahi.

Alternatif yang dipertimbangkan dan tidak dipilih:
- Menyalin caption ke parent di BE saat inbound: child bisa tiba sebelum parent (race), harus mencari parent per conversation (lihat #3998), dan data lama tidak terbenahi.
- Derive di read-time di `populateAlbumMessages`: mengubah `content` parent sehingga ikut mengubah `isEditable` dan preview reply.

## Di luar cakupan

- Widget livechat (`apps/widget/.../WidgetBuble.tsx`) punya pola yang sama dan perlu tiket terpisah.
- Penentuan edit pada bubble album.

## Catatan verifikasi

Temuan di atas berasal dari penelusuran kode saja. Belum diverifikasi terhadap dokumen album sungguhan di Mongo, termasuk child mana yang membawa caption. Asumsi sementara: child pertama yang punya `content`.

allWorkPackages.subject: Bad decrypt config Organization level
allWorkPackages.description:
## Problem

Bad decrypt dapat menyebabkan disconnected WhatsApp Web.

## Solusi Sementara

### 1\. Config Organization Level

Parameter:

*   enable/disable bad decrypt guard
    
*   retry times before logout (3x)
    
*   span time retry after logout (60)
    
*   syncFullHistory boelan
    
*   HISTORY\_SYNC\_MAX\_AGE\_DAYS: 30, // 0 = unlimited
    
*   HISTORY\_SYNC\_MAX\_MESSAGES\_PER\_CHAT: 50, // 0 = unlimited
    

### 2\. Alert Monitoring ke Google Chat

*   kapan bad decrypt di trigger
    
*   dari company mana bad decrypt berasal

---

## Implementation Findings (code trace, 2.8.2.3)

All six parameters requested already exist in code as **hardcoded constants or a
hardcoded socket literal**. None is organization-scoped today, so one tenant's
bad-decrypt tuning is impossible without a redeploy.

| Ticket parameter | Where it lives today | Current default |
|---|---|---|
| enable/disable bad decrypt guard | no switch at all — `baileys.service.ts` `handleDecryptionFailure()` always runs | always on |
| retry times before logout (3x) | `instance.constant.ts` `INSTANCE.DECRYPT_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` | 3 |
| span time retry after logout (60) | `instance.constant.ts` `INSTANCE.DECRYPT_FAILURE_WINDOW_MS` | 60000 ms |
| syncFullHistory boolean | `whatsapp-connection.service.ts` socket config literal | false |
| HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_AGE_DAYS | `instance.constant.ts` (env override `WHATSAPP_HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_AGE_DAYS`) | 30 |
| HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_CHAT | `instance.constant.ts` (env override `WHATSAPP_HISTORY_SYNC_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_CHAT`) | 50 |

### Blocker found

The `whatsapp` app has **no gRPC client to company-service**. Its module wires only
CHANNEL, PEOPLE and MEDIA clients, so `OrganizationServiceClient` is not reachable
from `BaileysDependencies` as written.

### Implementation approach

1. Add six fields to the `Organization` schema as a nested `whatsappConfig`
   sub-document, all optional with no schema-level defaults, so an organization
   that was never configured stores nothing and the resolver falls back.
2. Extend `company.proto` `Organization` + `UpdateOrganizationRequest` with the
   same nested message; regenerate proto types.
3. Register the COMPANIES gRPC client in the whatsapp app module and add a
   cached (`CacheTTLEnum.FIVE_MINUTES`) `getWhatsappConfig(organizationId)`
   resolver on `BaileysDependencies`, mirroring broadcast-service's
   `isSpinTextEnabledForOrganization()` fail-open pattern.
4. Resolve the config once per session at socket init and read it in
   `handleDecryptionFailure()` and `parseHistoryMessages()`; every absent field
   falls back to the existing constant, so behaviour is unchanged for every
   organization until someone sets a value.
5. Expose the fields on the existing `PATCH /organization/:id` gateway route via
   `UpdateOrganizationDto`.

Alert-to-Google-Chat (section 2 of this ticket) is **not** in this change — it is
a separate deliverable and is being tracked apart from the config work.

Findings are code-trace only; no live WhatsApp session was reproduced.

allWorkPackages.subject: History-sync backfill silently drops own group messages
allWorkPackages.description:
## Bug Description

WhatsApp history-sync messages were **silently lost** during backfill. Two independent defects compounded: own group messages could not be attributed, and the resulting failure was recorded as a success.

## Root Cause

**1. Null payloads were laundered into `PROCESSED`.**

`apps/whatsapp/src/app/services/history-sync-drain.service.ts`

When `buildHistorySyncPayload` returned `null`, the drain loop skipped the `if (result)` block but **still pushed the id into `processedIds`**. The document was marked delivered without ever being emitted to a queue — an undelivered doc became indistinguishable from a delivered one, with no `failReason` and no retry.

**2. Own group messages were unattributable.**

`apps/whatsapp/src/app/services/baileys.service.ts` — `getParticipant`

WhatsApp omits `participant` on the session's own outbound group messages; the sender is implied by `fromMe`. History-sync replays them verbatim, so `getParticipant` returned `undefined` and every `fromMe` group message produced a null payload — which defect #1 then silently swallowed.

## Fix

- **`history-sync-drain.service.ts`** — a null payload now calls `markFailed(id, NULL_PAYLOAD_FAIL_REASON)` and `continue`s instead of joining `processedIds`. `markFailed` keeps the doc `PENDING` until `MAX_ATTEMPTS`, then parks it `FAILED` with a reason, so the message is retried and any residual loss is visible.
- **`baileys.service.ts`** — `getParticipant` falls back to the session's own JID from creds when `participant` is absent and `fromMe` is set, normalized via `jidNormalizedUser` to strip the device suffix so it matches `saveParticipants`.
- **`history-sync-filter.util.ts`** — added an `isRealMessage` guard so stub-only events (group-membership changes, ciphertext placeholders) and `protocolMessage`s are never persisted. They can never yield an inbound payload, so storing them only creates backlog rows guaranteed to fail the drain.

No new `SKIPPED` status was introduced — `markFailed`'s retry-then-park semantics already express this correctly.

## Verification

**Red/green.** Reverting the drain-loop change failed 2 of the new tests; restoring it passed them.

**Suite.** 125 passed, 125 total.

**Gates.** `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `nx run whatsapp:build` compiled successfully; lint clean apart from 3 pre-existing `sort-keys` errors in an untouched `webpack.config.js`.

**Live end-to-end**, against the real session and a real group, driving an on-demand backfill of 50 older messages:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| history-sync docs | 25 -> 51 (26 new) |
| drain outcome | 51 `PROCESSED`, 0 failed, 0 `failReason` |
| joined to `satuinbox_conversation.messages` on `rawMessage.key.id` | landed 26, **missing 0** |

Before the fix, the `fromMe` group messages in that set were dropped with no record.

## Risk

Low. No signature or schema changes, no new dependencies, no config. The participant fallback only fires where the result was previously `undefined` (a guaranteed drop), so it can only convert losses into deliveries. Downstream dedupe at `inbound-message.processor.ts:310` makes the added retries safe against duplicate inserts.
