allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Improvement Perfomance
allWorkPackages.description: # \[BUG\] Global Search — P95 latency 60x over PRD threshold (60s vs 1.5s) and 97% request failure rate under 50-VU concurrent load ## Environment ## Description The Global Search endpoint fails catastrophically under concurrent load. During a **50 Virtual User spike test (7.5 minutes)**, only **16 of 489 requests (3.3%)** completed successfully. The remaining **473 requests (96.7%)** either returned **HTTP 500 (240 requests)** or **timed out after 60 seconds (233 requests)**. Performance also fails the PRD requirement before concurrency is introduced. At **1 VU (sequential execution)**, the endpoint already records a **P95 latency of 4.55 seconds**, approximately **3× slower** than the required **1.5-second** threshold. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Authenticate as **Admin (**`**aprizaladm01**`**)** using the NextAuth authentication flow: * CSRF * Credentials * Session * JWT 2. Send a GET request to: ```text /api/search?conversationLimit=20&conversationOffset=0&q=tes&ticketLimit=20&ticketOffset=0 ``` 1. Execute **1 Virtual User** sequentially (5 iterations) to establish a baseline. 2. Execute **5 Virtual Users** with simultaneous requests. 3. Execute the following spike profile: ```text 1 minute @ 20 VUs ↓ Ramp to 50 VUs (1 minute) ↓ Sustain 50 VUs (5 minutes) ↓ Cooldown (1 minute) ``` 1. Observe: * Response latency * HTTP status codes * Failure rate ## Actual Result ### Additional Observations * During the 50-VU test, **255 login attempts** were performed. * Only **40 logins (15.7%)** succeeded. * Authentication also degraded significantly under concurrent load. * Fastest search request: * **675 ms** (passes threshold) * Average latency: * **31,174 ms (31.17 s)** * Endpoint occasionally recovers between failures (16 successful responses), but overall availability remains approximately **3%**. ## Expected Result According to **PRD Global Search Suggestion v2.1**: ### NFR §11 (Performance) * P95 latency should remain **below 1.5 seconds** for combined Ticket and Conversation searches using indexed shared-attribute fields. ### Success Metrics §16 * P95 latency **< 1.5 seconds** under expected production usage. ### EH-004 If both domains fail: * Keep the popup open. * Display an error state. * Allow the user to retry. The endpoint should not return HTTP 500. ### EH-007 If one domain times out: * Return partial results from the other domain. * Avoid failing the entire request. ## Impact 1. **Global Search becomes unusable under normal multi-agent load.** More than approximately five concurrent agents already introduce significant failures. 2. **Duplicate ticket handling increases.** Agents cannot discover existing conversations or tickets, directly impacting the PRD objective: > ≥70% of searches return at least one relevant suggestion. 3. **Loss of user trust.** Repeated HTTP 500 responses and 60-second waits discourage agents from using the feature. 4. **High production risk.** If deployed without optimization, typical business-hour concurrency (50+ agents) will likely render the feature unavailable. ## Evidence ### k6 Script ```text performance-testing/global-search/global-search-stress.js ``` ### Raw Result ```text performance-testing/global-search/results/global-search-50vus.json ``` ## Performance Intelligence Report ### Test Profile ### Search Requests ### Latency ### Threshold Validation ## Additional Notes ### Possible Root Causes * Missing database indexes on searchable shared-attribute fields (AWB, Order ID, Tracking Number, etc.). * Database connection pool exhaustion under concurrent search requests. * Thread pool saturation within the search services. * RabbitMQ or inter-service RPC bottlenecks between API Gateway, Conversation Service, and Ticket Service. * Missing circuit breaker or request throttling mechanism, allowing downstream services to fail instead of rejecting excessive traffic. ### Suspected Backend Components * `conversation-service` * `SearchRelatedByAttribute` RPC * `ticket-service` * `SearchRelatedByAttribute` RPC * Database connection pool configuration. * API Gateway timeout configuration (observed timeout ceiling consistently equals 60 seconds). ## Related PRD **PRD Global Search – Global Search Suggestion v2.1** Relevant sections: * **NFR §11** — Performance * **Success Metrics §16** * **EH-004** * **EH-007** ## Recommendation for Engineering 1. Add database indexes for all searchable shared-attribute fields (AWB, Order ID, Tracking Number, etc.) across both Conversation and Ticket collections. 2. Increase database connection pool sizes for: * conversation-service * ticket-service 3. Implement a circuit breaker or rate limiter at the API Gateway to reject excess requests with HTTP 429 or HTTP 503 instead of allowing downstream HTTP 500 failures. 4. Introduce short-lived caching for identical search queries to reduce repeated database lookups. 5. Re-run the k6 stress test after optimization and verify: * P95 latency < 1.5 seconds * HTTP failure rate < 1% * Login success > 98% * Stable operation at 50 concurrent Virtual Users.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global search Atlas $search fails on tenants with over 1,000 conversations/tickets (maxClauseCount overflow)
allWorkPackages.description:
**Bug**: Global Search's Atlas Search path (ticket #2410) throws `MongoServerError: query has expanded into too many sub-queries internally: maxClauseCount is set to 1024` on every request for any tenant with more than ~1,000 in-scope conversations/tickets. The candidate-ID `in()` filter/should clause embedded the full candidate list (up to 5,000 ids) directly into the `$search` compound query; mongot expands `in()` into one Lucene clause per value, exceeding the default `maxClauseCount: 1024`.

Found via a live debugging session (2026-07-24) against the dev DB (logged in as `goddummyprod`, org "SAP") — reproduced on 8/8 calls (4 query terms x conversation/ticket domains), each silently falling back to the slow regex scan (5.5-15s latency) instead of using the Atlas index.

**Fix (implemented)**: commit `ef8e4743` on branch `fix/2228-ticket-relation-label-comma-filter`.
- Chunk the candidate-id list into batches under mongot's clause limit (new `ATLAS_SEARCH_IN_CLAUSE_MAX_SIZE = 900` constant + `chunkIds` helper in `libs/common`), run one `$search` call per chunk in parallel, and union the results.
- Defensively cap + log a warning on the smaller message/reply-match id-in `should` clause carrying the same overflow risk.
- Mirrored identically in `conversation-search.repository.ts` (conversation-service) and `ticket-search.repository.ts` (ticket-service).
- New unit tests added in both repositories' spec files plus `libs/common`'s `atlas-search-query.utils.spec.ts`.

**Status**: Code complete; lint, unit tests, and build all green. Live re-validation against the dev DB (confirming the latency drop and no more maxClauseCount fallback) is still pending -- no dev DB/services were reachable in the implementation session.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Relation label name has no limit char and UI error on detail ticket/conversation in section relation label
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary This report covers two related issues in the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal concerning relation label name length: **Issue 1 — Modal UI Breaks with Long Text**: When a relation label name exceeds the available column width in the modal, the modal becomes horizontally scrollable instead of handling the overflow gracefully. The text pushes the layout beyond the viewport, forcing users to scroll sideways to see the full content. This error was appear on Domain Ticket and Conversation, also this causing the bug ui error on conversation detail section relation label also in ticket detail **Issue 2 — No Maximum Character Limit**: There is no maximum character limit enforced on the relation label name field. Users can input arbitrarily long text, which the system accepts without validation. The Product Manager has confirmed that a 50-character maximum limit should be enforced, with a toast warning: "Maksimal 50 karakter." Both issues stem from the same gap: the relation label name field lacks length constraints, and the UI is not designed to handle long values gracefully. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce ### Issue 1 — Modal UI Breaks with Long Text 1. Open the Global Search popup and select one or more search results. 2. Click **"Tandai Relasi"** to open the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal. 3. Select a **Tipe atribut** from the dropdown. 4. In the **Nilai** field, enter a relation label value exceeding the column width (for example, 60+ characters or more). 5. Optionally apply the label so it becomes a visible badge. 6. Observe the modal layout. ### Issue 2 — No Maximum Character Limit 1. Open the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal as described above. 2. In the **Nilai** field, enter a string longer than 50 characters. 3. Click **Terapkan** (if the button is enabled). 4. Observe whether the input is accepted or rejected. ## Actual Result ### Issue 1 * The relation label name overflows the column or input field. * The modal becomes horizontally scrollable — a scrollbar appears and the layout shifts. * Content is pushed beyond the visible area, requiring sideways scrolling to view. * The modal does not truncate or wrap the long text. ### Issue 2 * The **Nilai** field accepts input of any length without restriction. * No character counter or limit indicator is displayed. * No validation warning or toast appears when exceeding 50 characters. * The system saves the full long value without enforcement. ## Expected Result ### Issue 1 * The modal should handle long relation label names without breaking the layout. * Text should either wrap to the next line or be truncated with an ellipsis. * Full text should remain accessible on hover or via tooltip. * The modal should not become horizontally scrollable regardless of input length. ### Issue 2 * The **Nilai** field should enforce a maximum of 50 characters per the PM's ruling. * A character counter (for example, "12/50") should be displayed near the input. * When the user tries to type beyond 50 characters, input should be blocked. * **If the user pastes text exceeding 50 characters, a toast warning should appear: "Maksimal 50 karakter."** * The **Terapkan** button should be disabled or blocked if the value exceeds the limit. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The "Beri Tag Relasi" modal does not handle text overflow — long values push the layout horizontally. * No maxlength attribute or JavaScript validation is present on the Nilai input field. * No character counter or visual feedback indicates remaining character budget. * The PRD (§10 Field & Validation) does not define a character limit for `relationAttributeValueDisplay` or `relationLabelDisplay`. * The only truncation guidance is EC-003: "Shared attribute display value is long (e.g. 50+ chars) → UI truncates display." This addresses display only, not input validation. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Beri Tag Relasi modal (CSS overflow handling) * Frontend — Nilai input field (missing maxlength attribute and validation) * Frontend — Relation label badge/chip component (overflow rendering) The root cause is twofold: 1. The PRD omitted a maximum character length for relation label values (§10 has no limit defined, unlike the Auto Tag PRD which caps keywords at 50 chars and rule names at 50 chars). 2. The modal's CSS layout does not constrain content width or apply `overflow: hidden` with `text-overflow: ellipsis`, allowing long text to expand the container. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Add `maxlength="50"` to the **Nilai** input field to prevent input beyond the limit. 2. Add a character counter below the input (for example, "24/50") that updates as the user types. 3. Block the **Terapkan** button or show inline validation when the value exceeds 50 characters. 4. Display a toast warning "Maksimal 50 karakter" when the user attempts to exceed the limit (via paste). 5. Fix the modal's CSS to handle overflow: constrain the column width and apply text truncation (`text-overflow: ellipsis`, `overflow: hidden`, `white-space: nowrap`) for long displayed values. Keep the full value accessible on hover via `title` attribute or tooltip. 6. Also apply the 50-character limit and truncation behavior to the relation label badge/chip component used in search result rows and detail pages. 7. Update the PRD §10 Field & Validation to document the 50-character maximum for `relationAttributeValueDisplay`. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: EC-003 — "Shared attribute display value is long (e.g. 50+ chars) → UI truncates display safely but keeps full value accessible on hover/detail." * **PM Confirmation**: The Product Manager confirmed a 50-character maximum limit should be enforced and the issues should be treated as low priority. * **PRD Gap**: §10 Field & Validation does not define a character limit for any relation label field. The Auto Tag PRD defines explicit limits (max 50 chars for keywords, max 50 chars for rule names) — this PRD should be updated to match that standard. * **Related Bug Reports**: * `beri-tag-relasi-modal-value-prefilled-without-attribute.md` — the same modal has pre-fill inconsistency issues. * `tag-relasi-edited-value-not-synced-to-modal.md` — the same modal has value sync issues. * **Priority**: Low — per PM confirmation.

allWorkPackages.description: # UI/UX Polish Collection > This document collects minor UI, UX, interaction, and visual polish observations found during exploratory testing. > > These observations are **not critical functional bugs**, but addressing them can improve consistency, usability, and the overall product experience. > > See the available ui/ux polish to fix on **Summary** Section > **Status information:** > \- Open (Not yet Fixed ⚠️) > \- Fixed(Already test and fixed) > \- New (New Bug/Error that needed to fix) # Overview # Observation 001 (Fixed✅) ## Title Dropdown field shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the **"Tipe atribut"** dropdown field inside the Relation Label modal, the mouse cursor remains the default arrow cursor. Since this component is clickable and opens a dropdown menu, the interaction feedback does not clearly communicate that the field is interactive. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer (`cursor: pointer`) when hovering over the dropdown field to indicate that the component is clickable. ### Notes This is a common UI convention — dropdown triggers should use a pointer cursor to signal interactivity. # Observation 002 (Fixed✅) ## Title Primary action button shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the **"Tandai Relasi"** button in the bottom action bar, the mouse cursor remains the default cursor. As this is a primary clickable action button, the default cursor does not clearly indicate that the component is interactive. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over the button to provide clear interaction feedback consistent with standard button behavior. ### Notes This affects all users and reduces the perceived responsiveness of the interface. # Observation 003 (Fixed✅) ## Title Secondary action button shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the **"Batal"** button in the bottom action bar, the mouse cursor remains the default cursor. The button is clickable and dismisses the action bar. A pointer cursor would provide consistent interaction feedback across all clickable action buttons. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over the button, matching the interaction behavior of other clickable elements. ### Notes Consistent cursor behavior across all buttons in the action bar improves the overall interaction model. # Observation 004 (Fixed✅) ## Title Dropdown menu options show default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the options inside the **"Tipe atribut"** dropdown menu (e.g., AWB, Order ID, Tracking, Invoice, Custom), the cursor remains the default cursor. Since each option is selectable, the cursor should provide consistent interactivity feedback throughout the dropdown menu. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over each dropdown option to indicate that the item is selectable. ### Notes This is consistent with standard dropdown menu behavior across most web applications. # Observation 005 (Fixed✅) ## Title Modal close button shows default cursor instead of pointer. ### Screenshot ### Observation When hovering over the modal close (**×**) button, the cursor remains the default cursor. The close icon is clickable and dismisses the modal. Using a pointer cursor would align with common UI interaction patterns and provide clearer visual feedback. ### Expected Behavior The cursor should change to a pointer when hovering over the close button to indicate that the icon is clickable. ### Notes Modal close buttons universally use a pointer cursor across most modern web applications. # Observation 006 (Fixed✅) ## allWorkPackages.description:
**\# Apa yang Baru di SatuInbox v2.8.0**

  
  

**\## ✨ Fitur Baru**

  
  

\- **\*\*Related Conversations\*\*** — Percakapan yang berhubungan sekarang dikelompokkan otomatis di inbox, jadi konteks pelanggan lebih mudah dilihat.

\- **\*\*Related Tickets & Merge Suggestion\*\*** — Sistem sekarang menyarankan tiket yang mirip/berkaitan, dan bisa digabung supaya tim gak kerja dobel.

\- **\*\*Round Robin lebih pintar\*\*** — Pembagian percakapan ke agent sekarang pakai aturan batch, jadi gak ada lagi penumpukan (bottleneck) di satu agent.

\- **\*\*Sinkron kontak dengan Lincah\*\*** — Kontak SatuInbox otomatis nyambung dengan kontak Lincah.

\- **\*\*Unlink Relation Label\*\*** — Sekarang bisa "Hapus Relasi" (satu-satu atau sekaligus banyak) dengan konfirmasi, fitur yang sebelumnya belum ada.

\- **\*\*Auto-assign conversation ke team\*\*** — Percakapan yang belum ada pemiliknya otomatis masuk ke team begitu channel-nya ditambahkan ke team itu — gak perlu sync manual lagi.

\- **\*\*Validasi nomor WhatsApp via API\*\*** — Nomor WhatsApp bisa divalidasi lewat API terbuka (dipakai untuk integrasi Salfok).

\- **\*\*Fuzzy search di Global Search\*\*** — Pencarian sekarang lebih toleran typo, sama seperti pencarian di daftar percakapan.

\- **\*\*Widget chat baru untuk Lincah\*\*** — Perusahaan Lincah sekarang punya widget live chat sendiri.

  
  

**\## 🐞 Perbaikan Bug**

  
  

\- **\*\*Global Search jauh lebih cepat\*\*** — sebelumnya bisa gagal/lemot parah kalau banyak orang search bersamaan, sekarang sudah dibenahi.

\- **\*\*Global Search di tenant besar (>1000 percakapan/tiket)\*\*** — sebelumnya error, sekarang jalan normal.

\- Klik hasil Global Search gak lagi salah pencet checkbox, dan tombol "Hapus Relasi" yang sempat hilang sudah balik.

\- Gak bisa lagi pilih hasil Conversation dan Ticket bersamaan di Global Search (dulu bikin bingung).

\- Label relasi yang diedit sekarang benar-benar tersimpan dan muncul di modal.

\- Berbagai polesan kecil UI di Global Search (kursor, hover, pesan notifikasi lebih jelas).

\- Widget chat gak lagi kadang "skip" pesan pas server baru restart/rilis.

\- Badge label relasi di tiket sekarang muncul dengan benar di hasil pencarian.

\- Nama label relasi sekarang dibatasi 50 karakter, dan tampilan gak lagi berantakan untuk nama panjang.

\- Label yang sudah dihapus gak lagi nongol lagi di hasil pencarian lama.

\- Copy-paste di form pembuatan tiket sekarang berfungsi normal.

\- Template WhatsApp yang dibuat langsung di Meta Business Manager sekarang otomatis kesinkron ke sistem.

\- Modal "Lepas Label Relasi" gak lagi berantakan untuk nama label panjang.

\- Label relasi dengan nama 40+ karakter sekarang bisa dihapus (sebelumnya error).

\- Preview pesan di daftar percakapan sekarang terpotong rapi (…) alih-alih bisa di-scroll.

  
  

**\## ⏳ Belum Rilis (masih dalam proses, tidak masuk versi ini)**

  
  

\- Reconnect channel Instagram yang expired (masih testing)

\- Broadcast template WhatsApp dengan media (gagal test, perlu perbaikan)

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search — add fuzzy/typo-tolerant matching (gap vs conversation-list search)
allWorkPackages.description:
## Summary

Global search's Atlas-backed relevance scoring is a strict exact/prefix/partial `$switch` ladder (`SCORE_EXACT`/`SCORE_PREFIX`/`SCORE_PARTIAL` in `conversation-search.repository.ts`; `SCORE.EXACT`/`NORMALIZED_EXACT`/`PREFIX`/`PARTIAL` in `ticket-search.repository.ts`) and deliberately excludes Atlas `fuzzy` matching. The conversation-list (inbox) search already supports typo-tolerant fuzzy matching via `fuzzy: {maxEdits: 1}` on `contactInfo.displayName` (`conversation.repository.ts:528`), so a typo in a contact name gets looser matching in the inbox list but not in global search.

## Why this happens (verified in code, not a bug)

`conversation-search-atlas.pipeline.ts` (and the ticket-service equivalent) explicitly omit `fuzzy` from their Atlas `$search` `should` clauses. The inline comment documents why: any fuzzy-only hit would score 0 in the current exact/prefix/partial ladder and get discarded by the `_scoreField > 0` guard — so naively adding `fuzzy` today would produce matches that are silently dropped, which is worse than the current state. This is an intentional design tradeoff, not a regression.

## Ask

Investigate/propose how to extend global search's relevance ladder with a fuzzy tier (e.g. a new lowest-priority `SCORE_FUZZY` rung below `SCORE_PARTIAL`) so typo-tolerant queries can surface results in global search, without breaking the deterministic exact > prefix > partial ordering that the `matchFields[]` highlight metadata depends on downstream.

## Where to look

*   `apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/conversation-search.repository.ts` — relevance ladder + `buildRelevancePipeline`
    
*   `apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/pipelines/conversation-search-atlas.pipeline.ts` — Atlas `should`\-clause builder (fuzzy-omission comment)
    
*   `apps/ticket-service/src/app/repositories/ticket-search.repository.ts` + its atlas pipeline — same pattern, ticket domain
    
*   `apps/conversation-service/src/app/repositories/conversation.repository.ts:528` — existing fuzzy usage in list search, as the reference pattern for how fuzzy is wired on the Atlas side
    

## Scope note

This is an improvement/investigation ticket, not a defect against existing behavior — filed as a child of #2410 (Global Search Suggestion - Improvement Perfomance) since it's the same "global search quality" track.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Domain Ticket Relation label badges was not appear on global search result
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary After successfully applying a system relation label to a Ticket via the "Beri Tag Relasi" bulk action, the relation label badge does not appear on the Ticket result row in the Global Search popup. The label is correctly displayed on the Ticket Detail page, confirming the label was persisted. However, the Global Search result row for the same ticket shows no relation label badge — even after a hard browser refresh. This only apper on domain ticket, on conversation domain, this bug not appear. This inconsistency means users searching for a related ticket in Global Search cannot visually confirm that a relation label has already been applied to that record. The label is only discoverable by opening the Ticket Detail page, defeating the purpose of surfacing relation context in the search results. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Global Search popup and search for a keyword that returns Ticket results. 2. Select one or more Ticket results via checkbox. 3. Click **"Tandai Relasi"** in the Ticket bulk action bar. 4. In the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal, select a **Tipe atribut** and enter a **Nilai**, then click **Terapkan**. 5. Verify the success toast appears confirming the relation label was applied. 6. Navigate to the Ticket Detail page for the selected ticket and verify the relation label badge is visible — confirm the label was persisted. 7. Return to the Global Search popup and perform the same search again. 8. Perform a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R). 9. Locate the same Ticket result row. 10. Observe whether the relation label badge is displayed. ## Actual Result * The relation label badge is **visible** on the Ticket Detail page, confirming successful persistence. * The relation label badge is **not visible** on the same ticket's result row in the Global Search popup. * The badge remains absent even after a hard browser refresh. * Other result card fields (ticket ID, title, status) appear correctly. ## Expected Result * After a relation label is successfully applied to a Ticket, the label badge should appear on that ticket's result row in the Global Search popup. * The badge should be visible immediately after applying the label, or at minimum after a page refresh. * The relation label displayed in Global Search should match what is shown on the Ticket Detail page. * Conversation result rows should also consistently display their relation label badges (verify this domain for comparison). ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * Relation labels are correctly persisted — they appear on the Ticket Detail page after application. * Global Search result rows do not display the relation label badge for Tickets. * Hard refresh does not resolve the issue, suggesting a backend data fetch or rendering issue rather than a client-side cache problem. * The issue may be specific to the Ticket domain — Conversation result rows should be checked for comparison. * Result card rendering otherwise works correctly (ticket ID, title, status all display). ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend — Global Search API response for Ticket domain * Backend — Relation label inclusion in search index or query * Frontend — Ticket result row component (relation label badge rendering) The Global Search API response for Ticket results may not include relation label data, while the Ticket Detail API does. Alternatively, the search index may not be updated with relation label metadata after a bulk apply, causing the search results to return stale or incomplete data for the Ticket domain. The frontend may also have a rendering condition that only renders the relation label badge for Conversation result rows and omits it for Ticket rows. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Compare the Global Search API response for a Ticket with a relation label against the Ticket Detail API response — verify whether the relation label data is present in the search response. 2. Check whether the search index is updated after a relation label is applied to a Ticket. If the index is not refreshed, the label will never appear in search results. 3. Inspect the Ticket result row component to confirm the relation label badge rendering logic is implemented for the Ticket domain — it may only be wired for Conversation rows. 4. Repeat the same test on the Conversation domain to determine if the issue is domain-specific or global. 5. **Cross-reference with FR-022 \[P0\]: "Relation labels MUST be visible in a dedicated relation-label presentation area."** ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-022 \[P0\] — Relation labels MUST be visible in a dedicated relation-label presentation area and MUST NOT be indistinguishable from manual tags in the UI. * **Related Requirement**: FR-018 \[P0\] — Relation labels MUST support at minimum: attribute key, normalized value, display value, created source, and created timestamp. * **Precondition**: At least one Ticket exists in search results with a relation label successfully applied. * **Verification note**: Test on Conversation domain as well to determine if the issue is domain-specific (Ticket only) or cross-domain.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Error when trying to open into related conversation
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary This report covers two related issues found in the Global Search actionable search result rows: **Issue 1 — Accidental Checkbox Selection**: When a user clicks a search result row in the Global Search popup to navigate to a Conversation Room, the click unintentionally triggers the per-row checkbox selection for "Tandai Relasi" instead of opening the target conversation. The user intended only to navigate — not to select the record for bulk action. **Issue 2 — "Hapus Relasi" Feature Not Yet Implemented**: The Figma design for the actionable search result row includes a "Hapus Relasi" (Remove Relation) button that allows users to unlink or delete a previously applied relation label. However, this feature has not been developed yet — neither the frontend button nor the backend deletion system exists in the current implementation. Once a relation label is applied to a record, there is no way for users to remove it. Based on this design [FigmaDesign](https://www.figma.com/design/RAAuLaQKUufWMWWEm0kMb9/-V2--Satuinbox-Web-Specs?node-id=12250-73420&t=dQuIT72klLsuPW1S-0) Both issues affect the same result row component, which is intended to carry navigation, selection, relation label display, and unlink actions. The missing "Hapus Relasi" feature means relation labels, once applied, are permanent — there is no undo or correction path for users. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce ### Issue 1 — Accidental Checkbox Selection 1. Open the Global Search popup by clicking **Cari** in the sidenav or pressing **Ctrl+K / Cmd+K**. 2. Enter a search keyword (for example, `JNE123456789` or `min`). 3. Wait for search results to load — verify Conversation and Ticket sections appear. 4. Click the body area of a Conversation result row with the intent to navigate to the Conversation Room. 5. Observe the result. ### Issue 2 — "Hapus Relasi" Feature Not Yet Implemented 1. Open the Global Search popup and search for a keyword that returns records with existing relation labels. 2. Locate a result row that displays a relation label chip (for example, `AWB • JNE123456789`). 3. Observe that there is no **"Hapus Relasi"** button or any user-facing action to unlink or remove the relation label from the record. ## Actual Result ### Issue 1 * The per-row checkbox for "Tandai Relasi" becomes selected (checked). * The bulk action bar appears showing "Percakapan dipilih: 1". * The user is **not** navigated to the Conversation Room on single click. * The Global Search popup remains open. ### Issue 2 * No "Hapus Relasi" button or unlink action is available on the search result row. * Relation labels, once applied, cannot be removed by the user through any available UI action. * There is no confirmation dialog, deletion endpoint, or unlink workflow implemented. ## Expected Result ### Issue 1 * Clicking the Conversation result row navigates the user to the Conversation Room with the Detail panel visible. * The Global Search popup closes automatically. * The checkbox should only become selected when the user explicitly clicks the checkbox element itself, not the surrounding row area. ### Issue 2 * A "Hapus Relasi" button should be displayed on result rows that carry an existing relation label, following the Figma design. * Clicking "Hapus Relasi" should display a confirmation dialog (for example, "Hapus relasi ini?"). * Upon confirmation, the relation label should be removed from the record. * A backend endpoint should handle the deletion and ensure the label is unlinked from the target record. * A toast notification should confirm successful removal (for example, "Relasi berhasil dihapus"). * If deletion fails, an error toast should be displayed (for example, "Gagal menghapus relasi. Coba lagi."). ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The result row responds to a click by selecting the checkbox, not by navigating. * The checkbox click target appears to cover or overlap the row's main clickable area. * The bulk action bar appears immediately upon accidental selection. * No navigation occurs when clicking the row body. * No "Hapus Relasi" button exists on search result rows — the unlink feature has not been developed. * The Figma design includes this button, but neither the frontend component nor the backend deletion endpoint exists in the current implementation. * Relation labels, once applied, are permanent with no undo or correction path available to users. ## Possible Root Cause Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Search result row component (click event delegation) * Frontend — Checkbox click event propagation * Frontend — "Hapus Relasi" button event handler (missing or not wired) * Backend — Relation label deletion endpoint (may not exist or not integrated) **Issue 1**: The checkbox element's click handler may be capturing click events that should fall through to the row's navigation handler. Alternatively, the checkbox's visible or interactive area may be sized to cover the entire row rather than being constrained to the checkbox icon only. **Issue 2**: The "Hapus Relasi" feature has not been developed. The PRD (§2, §14, §20) lists unlink as out of scope for Phase 1, which may explain why the feature was deprioritized. However, the Figma design includes the button and interaction, indicating the design team intends for this feature to exist. The following components need to be built: * Frontend — "Hapus Relasi" button component on search result rows (with relation label chips) * Frontend — Confirmation modal ("Hapus relasi ini?") * Backend — Relation label deletion endpoint * Backend — Audit log for deletion events ## Recommendation ### Issue 1 — Checkbox vs Navigation 1. Verify the HTML structure of the search result row — ensure the checkbox is an independent click target, not a child element that captures row-level click events. 2. Confirm that `event.stopPropagation()` or equivalent is applied so that clicking the checkbox does not trigger row navigation, and clicking the row body does not trigger checkbox selection. 3. Visually reduce the checkbox's interactive hit area to only the checkbox icon, leaving the remainder of the row for navigation. 4. Review against PRD FR-001: "Clicking a Conversation result MUST open Conversation Room with Detail panel visible by default." ### Issue 2 — "Hapus Relasi" Feature Development 1. Develop the "Hapus Relasi" button component per the Figma design — display it on search result rows that have an existing relation label. 2. Wire the button to a new backend endpoint for relation label deletion (for example, `DELETE /api/relation-label/{id}`). 3. Add a confirmation modal with title "Hapus relasi ini?" and buttons "Batal" / "Hapus." 4. Upon successful deletion, show a success toast: "Relasi berhasil dihapus." 5. Upon failure, show an error toast: "Gagal menghapus relasi. Coba lagi." 6. Ensure the relation label chip is removed from the result row after successful deletion. 7. Log deletion events for audit purposes (who deleted, which label, timestamp). 8. Coordinate with PM to confirm this feature should be included in Phase 1 despite the PRD listing unlink as out of scope — the Figma design indicates it should exist. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-001 \[P0\] — Clicking a Conversation result MUST open Conversation Room with Detail panel visible. * **Related Requirement**: FR-005 \[P0\] — Search results MUST support checkbox selection per result row. * **PRD Out of Scope**: §2, §14, §20 — Unlink, relation graph editing, and automatic cleanup are explicitly listed as out of scope for Phase 1. * **Design-PRD Discrepancy**: The "Hapus Relasi" button exists in the UI design, but the PRD says unlink is out of scope. This should be clarified with the PM — either the button should be removed, or the PRD scope should be updated to include unlink. * **Precondition**: User is authenticated (Admin, Supervisor, or Agent role) and has accessed the Global Search popup with valid search results. * Both issues were discovered during exploratory testing of the actionable search feature before formal test case execution.

allWorkPackages.subject: Hapus Relasi (Unlink Relation Label) — feature not implemented anywhere in the codebase
allWorkPackages.parentName: Global Search Suggestion - Error when trying to open into related conversation
allWorkPackages.description:
## Summary
Split out from Issue 2 of #2607. A `RelationLabel` can be **applied** to a conversation/ticket (bulk, from Global Search) but there is no way to **remove** it afterward — no gRPC RPC, no REST route, no UI affordance exists in either repo. Once applied, a relation label is permanent.

Verified via codebase grep (2026-07-30): no `UnlinkRelationLabel`/`RemoveConversationRelationLabel`/`RemoveTicketRelationLabel` symbols exist anywhere in `omnichannel-satuinbox-be`, and no `unlink`/`Hapus Relasi` component or hook exists anywhere in `omnichannel-satuinbox-fe`.

## Current State
- `POST /search/relation-labels/apply` → `ConversationService.BulkApplyRelationLabel` / `TicketService.BulkApplyRelationLabel` pushes a label onto `conversation.relationLabels[]` / `ticket.relationLabels[]`.
- `RelationLabelChip` only supports `onFilter` — no remove affordance.
- `RelationLabelSection` (conversation/ticket detail) has no unlink wiring.
- Global Search bulk bar only has "Apply relation label" — no "Unlink relation label" action.

## Desired State (per Figma)
- "Hapus Relasi" button on search result rows / relation chips that carry an existing label.
- Confirmation modal ("Hapus relasi ini?" / Batal / Hapus).
- New single-item unlink RPC + gateway route (mirrors existing tag-remove pattern) for conversation and ticket detail.
- New bulk unlink RPC + gateway route (mirrors existing bulk-apply pattern) for the Global Search bulk bar.
- Success/error toasts ("Relasi berhasil dihapus." / "Gagal menghapus relasi. Coba lagi.").

## Implementation Plan
A full implementation plan already exists at `.claude/PRPs/plans/unlink-relation-label.plan.md` (both repos, ~34 files: proto + conversation-service + ticket-service + api-gateway + frontend hooks/components/i18n). Not yet started — no related code exists in either repo's working tree or git history.

## Out of Scope (per plan)
- `RelationLabel` document deletion/reference-counting in company-service.
- Multi-select inside the related-items panel (bulk unlink lives in Global Search only).
- Automated FE tests (no FE test runner configured in this codebase).

## Related
- Parent: #2607 (bundles this as "Issue 2")
- Related PRD: #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search"
- PRD explicitly lists unlink as out of scope for Phase 1 (§2, §14, §20) — Figma design includes the button regardless; flagged as a design/PRD discrepancy in #2607, needs PM confirmation on scope.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Can't delete the relation label with 40+ relation label char
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary When a user attempts to release ("Lepas Label Relasi") a relation label whose name contains 40 or more characters, the action fails with an error — even though the label name is still within the allowed 50-character maximum. The relation label cannot be unlinked from the record, and an error is returned instead of a successful release. This is a functional blocker, not a layout issue: unlike the previously reported overflow problem, here the release action itself fails. Users who applied a long relation label (40–50 characters) are unable to remove or correct it, which is especially problematic because the "Hapus/Lepas Relasi" feature is the only correction path for misapplied labels. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Apply a relation label with a name of 40 or more characters (for example, a 42-character value) to a Conversation or Ticket via the "Beri Tag Relasi" flow. 2. Verify the label was applied successfully. 3. Open the Global Search popup and search for the keyword matching that record. 4. Locate the result row with the long relation label badge. 5. Click the **"Lepas Label Relasi"** action. 6. Complete the confirmation flow (if the modal appears). 7. Observe the result. ## Actual Result * Clicking "Lepas Label Relasi" on a relation label with 40+ characters results in an **error**. * The relation label is **not released** — it remains applied to the record. * An error message or failed state is displayed (no successful release toast). * The failure occurs even though the label name is below the 50-character maximum limit (40–49 characters fails). * The behavior appears on relation labels within the valid length range, suggesting a bug in the release logic rather than a validation rejection. ## Expected Result * "Lepas Label Relasi" should successfully release any relation label whose name is within the allowed character limit (up to 50 characters). * The label should be removed from the record after confirmation. * A success toast should confirm the release (for example, "Relasi berhasil dilepas"). * Labels between 40–50 characters should behave identically to shorter labels — the release action must not fail based on label name length. * If a genuine validation limit exists, it should be enforced consistently with a clear message — but 40+ chars is below the documented 50-char maximum, so this should succeed. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The release action fails for relation labels with 40+ characters. * Labels under 40 characters release successfully (to be confirmed with exact threshold). * The label name is within the valid range (below 50 chars) — so this is not a validation rejection. * The error appears to come from the release operation itself, not from UI validation. * The exact character threshold (40 vs 41 vs 45) should be confirmed during investigation. * The issue may share a root cause with the related overflow bug — the release logic or endpoint may not handle long label values correctly. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Backend — Relation label release/delete endpoint * Backend — Relation label key generation or lookup for long values * Frontend — Release action request payload for long label names The release operation may use the relation label key (for example, `rel..`) to identify the label to release. For long label values, the generated key or the request payload may exceed an internal limit — for example, a database column length, an API request size constraint, or a backend validation that rejects keys above a certain length — causing the release to fail even though the label name itself is within the user-facing 50-char limit. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Reproduce with labels of varying lengths to determine the exact failing threshold (40, 45, 49 characters). 2. Inspect the release request payload — verify the relation label key/value is transmitted correctly for long names. 3. Check the backend release endpoint for any length-based validation or column-length limits that may reject long relation label keys. 4. Verify the fix ensures labels up to the 50-character maximum can be released without error. 5. Test the release action on both Conversation and Ticket domains, and with labels at exactly 40, 45, 49, and 50 characters. 6. Coordinate with the overflow fix (related issue) to ensure the release modal also handles long labels without layout breakage. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-021 \[P0\] — Applying the same relation label twice MUST NOT create duplicates (label lifecycle management is in scope). * **PM Confirmation**: The 50-character maximum for relation label names has been confirmed by PM (see related report on character limit). Labels within this limit must function correctly. * **Related Bug Reports**: * #2981 the release confirmation modal breaks horizontally for 45+ character labels (UI layout issue). * **Distinction**: This report is a **functional error** (release action fails), NOT the UI overflow issue reported separately. Both affect long relation labels and may share a root cause, but they are distinct symptoms. * **Threshold note**: The exact failing threshold (40 vs 45 characters) should be verified during investigation.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - The label on global search was not sync into current data relation label list
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary When a relation label is deleted from a Conversation Detail page, the Global Search result row for that conversation continues to display the deleted relation label badge. The Global Search data does not synchronize with the updated conversation state, the stale label remains visible in search results until the user performs a full browser refresh. This affects the user's trust in the feature: a user who deletes a relation label and then reopens Global Search will see the label still present, leading them to believe the deletion failed. Only by navigating to the Conversation Detail again (or refreshing the browser) can they confirm the label was actually removed. The discrepancy between Global Search and the detail view creates a confusing, inconsistent experience. This issue was confirmed on the Conversation domain. The Ticket domain should also be verified, as it likely shares the same stale-data behavior. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a Conversation Detail page that has a relation label applied. 2. Delete or unlink the relation label from the conversation. 3. Confirm the label is removed from the Conversation Detail page, then verify the badge is no longer visible. 4. Open the Global Search popup (Ctrl+K / Cmd+K) and search for a keyword that returns the same conversation. 5. Observe the relation label badge on the conversation's search result row. 6. Navigate to another page (for example, Ticket List or Settings), then return to Global Search and repeat the same search. 7. Observe the relation label badge again. 8. Perform a full browser refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) and repeat the search. 9. Observe the relation label badge after refresh. ## Actual Result * The relation label is correctly removed from the Conversation Detail page (deletion succeeds). * The relation label badge **remains visible** on the conversation's result row in Global Search — showing the stale, deleted label. * Navigating to other pages and returning to Global Search does **not** update the badge — the stale label persists. * The stale label only disappears after a **full browser refresh** (hard reload). ## Expected Result * After a relation label is deleted from the Conversation Detail page, the Global Search results should reflect the updated state. * Reopening the Global Search popup and executing the same search should show the conversation **without** the deleted relation label badge. * The data should be consistent between the Conversation Detail view and the Global Search view at all times — without requiring a browser refresh. * If a real-time sync mechanism is not feasible, the Global Search should at minimum re-fetch data from the server when the popup is reopened (not rely on a stale client-side cache). ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * Relation label deletion on Conversation Detail works correctly — the label is removed from the database. * Global Search results appear to use a client-side cache or session-scoped data that is not invalidated when relation labels are modified externally. * Navigating between pages does not trigger a cache invalidation — only a full browser refresh clears the stale data. * The issue is confirmed on the Conversation domain. The Ticket domain is suspected to have the same behavior but has not yet been verified. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Global Search data cache / state management * Frontend — Search result cache invalidation strategy * Backend — Global Search API response (may serve cached results) The Global Search popup likely caches search results in client-side state (for example, React state, SWR cache, or sessionStorage) to enable the "restore last search results" feature (FR-004). However, this cache is not invalidated when relation labels are modified from outside the Global Search context. When the user reopens the popup, the cached results — including stale relation label data — are displayed instead of fresh data from the server. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Implement a cache invalidation strategy for Global Search results whenever a relation label is added, modified, or deleted from any surface (Conversation Detail, Ticket Detail, or bulk action). 2. At minimum, re-fetch search results from the server when the Global Search popup is reopened, rather than serving entirely from a stale cache. 3. Verify the same behavior on the Ticket domain — if the issue exists there as well, apply the same fix. 4. Consider using a shared state or event bus so that relation label mutations trigger a cache clear for all affected search result entries. 5. Test the fix by: * Adding a relation label → verifying it appears in Global Search immediately. * Deleting a relation label → verifying it disappears from Global Search immediately. * Modifying a relation label value → verifying the updated value appears in Global Search. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-022 \[P0\] — Relation labels MUST be visible in a dedicated relation-label presentation area. * **Related Requirement**: FR-004 \[P0\] — Search state MUST be restorable within the same session after navigation. (This feature may be the source of the stale cache — restoring state should not override fresh data.) * **Domain**: Confirmed on Conversation. Ticket domain should be tested by the developer as part of the fix. * **User expectation**: From the user's perspective, any data change should be reflected dynamically across all views without requiring a browser refresh. This is a standard web application UX expectation. * **Related Bug Reports**: * Ticket #2905 — relation label badge not appearing for Ticket domain in search results (may share cache-related root cause).

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Tag relasi edited value not synced to modal
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary The **Tag Relasi** input field in the Global Search bulk action bar accepts user edits, but the modified value is not carried forward when opening the **"Beri Tag Relasi"** modal. Instead, the modal's **Nilai** (Value) field initializes with the original Global Search keyword, discarding the user's edit. This creates a data synchronization gap between two connected UI surfaces. The user edits a value in the action bar, opens the modal expecting to see their edit reflected, and instead finds the stale original keyword — giving the impression their input was ignored. Additionally, the Tag Relasi input presents an editable UI (text cursor, keyboard input accepted), yet behaves as if read-only at the data level. This ambiguity confuses users about whether the field is intended to be editable or display-only. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Global Search popup and enter a search any keyword (for example, `pagi mas`). 2. Wait for search results to load. 3. Select one or more Conversation or Ticket results via checkbox. 4. Observe the **Tag Relasi** input in the bottom action bar — it is pre-filled with the search keyword (`pagi mas`). 5. Edit the Tag Relasi input to a any new value (for example, `ini aku ubah`). 6. Verify the input now displays the edited value (`ini aku ubah`). 7. Click the **"Tandai Relasi"** button. 8. Observe the **Nilai** (Value) field inside the **"Beri Tag Relasi"** modal. ## Actual Result * The **Tag Relasi** input in the action bar reflects the user's edit (`ini aku ubah`). * The **Nilai** field in the modal displays the original search keyword (`pagi mas`), ignoring the edit. * The two values are out of sync — the modal does not use the latest user-modified value. ## Expected Result * Editing the Tag Relasi input and then opening the modal should carry the latest value into the **Nilai** field. * Both UI surfaces should remain synchronized — the modal must reflect whatever the user sees in the action bar before clicking "Tandai Relasi." ## Impact ## Evidence1 ## Initial Observation * The Tag Relasi input in the action bar is visually editable: text cursor appears on hover/focus, keyboard input is accepted, and the displayed value updates. * Despite accepting edits, the edited value is never consumed by downstream UI components. * The modal always initializes with the original search keyword, regardless of edits made in the action bar. * There is no visual indication to the user that their edit will be ignored once the modal opens. * The ambiguity extends to the input's intended design: it looks editable but behaves as read-only at the data propagation level. ## Possible Root Cause Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Global Search bulk action bar component (Tag Relasi input state) * Frontend — Beri Tag Relasi modal initialization logic * Frontend — State management (data flow between action bar and modal) The action bar's Tag Relasi input likely maintains its own local UI state (allowing edits), but the modal's initialization logic reads the value from a separate source — the original Global Search keyword state — rather than from the action bar's current input value. The two components are not connected through a shared state or prop, causing the desynchronization. ## Recommendation 1. Identify the intended UX for the Tag Relasi input: * **If editable**: propagate the latest edited value to the modal's Nilai field and also make the cursor into pointer or hand. * **If read-only**: set the input to `readonly` or `disabled`, remove the text cursor, and apply `cursor: default` or cursor disable styling to prevent user confusion. 2. If editable behavior is intended, wire the modal initialization to read from the action bar's current input value, not the original search keyword. 3. Add a validation check: if the user has modified the Tag Relasi value, use the modified value; otherwise, fall back to the search keyword or leave the field empty. 4. Ensure both the "Tandai Relasi" (action bar) and "Beri Tag Relasi" (modal title) button labels are unified to avoid the copy inconsistency noted in related bug report #4. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-012 \[P0\] — Phase 1 bulk action set MUST support `Beri Tag Relasi Otomatis`. * **Related Requirement**: FR-019 \[P0\] — User-facing relation labels MUST use readable format ` • `. * **Related Bug Report**: `beri-tag-relasi-modal-value-prefilled-without-attribute.md` — the Nilai field is also pre-filled inconsistently when no attribute type is selected. * **Precondition**: User has searched in Global Search, selected one or more results, and the Tag Relasi input is visible in the bottom action bar. * **Copy inconsistency note**: The action bar button says "Tandai Relasi" while the modal title says "Beri Tag Relasi" — these labels should be standardized.

allWorkPackages.subject: Inbox - Conversation chat list preview was not truncated, that was immediately can be scrollable
allWorkPackages.description:
# 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary Message preview text in the conversation list is not consistently truncated with ellipsis (`...`). Long message previews overflow their container and are visibly clipped at the card boundary without any visual indicator that content has been cut off. This affects all conversation list views — **Kotak Pesan Anda**, **Semua**, and other menu tabs. The issue is systemic: the CSS `text-overflow: ellipsis` property is present on the text element, but an intermediate container in the DOM tree lacks a width constraint (`overflow: hidden` on the parent), allowing the text span to expand to its full unconstrained width. Since the span never overflows its own box, the browser never applies the ellipsis — the text instead overflows the ancestor card and is clipped invisibly. This makes the message preview unreadable for long messages and creates an inconsistent, unpolished user experience across the primary agent workspace. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in as an Admin or Agent user (e.g., `aprizaladm01`). 2. Navigate to the **Conversation** module from the sidebar. 3. Observe the conversation list under **Kotak Pesan Anda**. 4. Locate a conversation with a long message preview (e.g., the message begins with read-receipt checkmarks `✓✓` followed by text). 5. Observe whether the message preview text is truncated with an ellipsis (`...`) at the end. 6. Switch to the **Semua** tab and repeat Steps 4–5. 7. Switch to the **Spam** tab and repeat Steps 4–5 for comparison. ## Actual Result * **Kotak Pesan Anda** — conversation with **Paul Green**: the message preview reads `hali ini contoh kalo misalkan mess` — text is abruptly cut off at the word `mess` without ellipsis. The full text (`...messagenya gak di enter dan terus menerus ke kiri`) is not visible, but no `...` indicator informs the user that content is hidden. * **Semua** — conversation with **guest-6VKQAR**: the message preview reads `[dev-inbound-flood] text mes` — cuts off at `mes` without ellipsis. * Same behavior observed on multiple conversation cards with message text longer than one line. * Some shorter messages (e.g., Kaithlyn's `[dev-inbound-flood] text message #3...`) display correctly because the text fits within the available width — no truncation is needed, so the ellipsis is coincidentally not triggered. * **Spam** tab correctly truncates with ellipsis (`halo cek misal ini chat panjang ap...`). ## Expected Result * All message preview text that exceeds the available card width should be truncated with a trailing ellipsis (`...`) to indicate that the message continues. * The truncation behavior should be consistent across all conversation list sub-views: **Kotak Pesan Anda**, **Semua**, **Belum Ditugaskan**, **Spam**, and any other tab. * When the full message text cannot fit in one line, the browser should apply `text-overflow: ellipsis` so the user sees: `hali ini contoh kalo misalkan mess...` ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The message preview `` element has correct CSS for text truncation: `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, `white-space: nowrap`. * An ancestor `
` (class: `w-full text-gray-500 flex items-center gap-1`) has `overflow: visible` and no width constraint — its computed width is `775px` (the full unconstrained text width), far exceeding its parent card width of `218px`. * Because the text span's direct parent has no width constraint (`overflow: visible`), the span expands to its full intrinsic width — the browser never detects overflow, so `text-overflow: ellipsis` never activates. * The text overflows the card boundary and is visually clipped by a higher-level ancestor with `overflow: hidden`, but no ellipsis is rendered because the clip occurs on a different element than where the text-overflow property is set. * The `min-w-0` class is present on an intermediate flex container (Tailwind's recommended pattern), but it is not sufficient because the unconstrained child overrides it with `overflow: visible`. * Presence of inline elements such as read-receipt checkmark icons (`✓✓`) inside the same flex row does not directly cause the bug but can increase the effective content width, making the truncation failure more noticeable. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Conversation List card component (message preview row) * CSS Layout — Flex container overflow chain The message preview row is built as a chain of nested flex containers. The text `` correctly declares `truncate line-clamp-1`, but an intermediate flex `
` (depth 4 in the DOM walk) lacks `overflow: hidden` or `max-width: 100%`. This breaks the CSS truncation contract: for `text-overflow: ellipsis` to work, the element's **direct containing block** must have a constrained width with `overflow: hidden` (or `auto`/`scroll`/`clip`). The current structure allows the child to determine the parent's width, rather than the parent constraining the child. The fix likely involves adding `overflow: hidden` to the intermediate flex container (the one wrapping both the checkmark icon and the text span) so the text span's width is bounded to the available card space. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Inspect the DOM between the message preview `` and the card container — identify the first ancestor that lacks `overflow: hidden`. 2. Add `overflow: hidden` (Tailwind: `overflow-hidden`) to the flex `
` that wraps the checkmark icon + text span together. 3. Verify that the read-receipt checkmark icon and any other inline elements do not push the text span beyond the available width — apply `shrink-0` to icons, `min-w-0` to the text container. 4. After fixing, regression-test all conversation list sub-views: Kotak Pesan Anda, Semua, Belum Ditugaskan, Spam, Berbintang, Folder Sampah, and any Kotak Masuk Tim views. 5. Test with message text of varying lengths — very short (no truncation needed), moderately long (should show ellipsis), and very long single-word strings (e.g., long AWB numbers). ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Conversation module — while the PRD does not explicitly mandate truncation behavior, the broadcast PRD (`PRD broadcast system - Broadcast Draft list.md`) establishes the pattern: _"Names longer than one line truncate with ellipsis; tooltip shows full text"_ — this is the expected UX convention across SatuInbox. * **Precondition**: At least one conversation in the list must have a message preview longer than the available card width (approximately 25–30 characters at the current font size). * **The Spam tab truncates correctly** — its DOM structure may differ; this can serve as a reference implementation for the fix. * The issue was reproduced on the **Kotak Pesan Anda** and **Semua** views. The user reports it also affects all conversation sub-views.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Bug UI on modal "Lepas Label Relasi"
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary When a relation label name contains more than approximately 45 characters, opening the "Lepas Relasi Label" confirmation modal causes the UI to break. The Select component displaying the relation label name expands horizontally beyond the modal's fixed boundary, pushing content outside the visible area and making the modal horizontally scrollable. This layout breakage occurs because the modal's dropdown/select component allows its content width to grow unrestricted based on the selected label text length. Action buttons may also become misaligned or clipped as the modal layout collapses. This issue affects both the **Conversation** and **Ticket** domains. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Ensure a relation label with a name exceeding 45 characters has been applied to a Conversation or Ticket. 2. Open the Global Search popup and search for the keyword matching that record. 3. Locate the result row displaying the long relation label badge. 4. Click the **"Lepas Relasi"** (or equivalent unlink/delete) action associated with that label. 5. Observe the confirmation modal that appears. ## Actual Result * The Select/dropdown component displaying the relation label name expands horizontally beyond the modal container. * The modal content overflows — text and elements are pushed outside the visible boundary. * The modal becomes horizontally scrollable — a scrollbar appears, and the layout shifts. * Action buttons may be partially or fully clipped, requiring the user to scroll sideways to access them. * The issue reproduces on both Conversation and Ticket domains. ## Expected Result * The modal width should remain fixed regardless of the relation label name length. * Long relation label values should not overflow the modal — they should be truncated with an ellipsis (`...`). example: AWB • AWB46KATAGB845G9745G987... then if hovering show this detail AWB • AWB46KATAGB845G9745G987G4587G98475G74H589843JF * The full relation label value should remain accessible via a tooltip on hover. * Action buttons should remain fully visible and aligned at all times. * The dropdown list should be constrained to the modal width — individual items should also truncate with ellipsis. * The modal should never become horizontally scrollable. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * The confirmation modal renders correctly for relation labels under ~45 characters. * At 45+ characters, the Select component begins to overflow the modal container. * The overflow is horizontal only — the modal height remains stable. * The issue occurs on both the Conversation domain and Ticket domain — it is not domain-specific. * This is a CSS/layout issue, not a data or logic issue — the label value is correct, only the rendering breaks. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — "Lepas Relasi Label" confirmation modal component * Frontend — Select/dropdown component CSS The Select component displaying the relation label name likely uses an auto-width or `max-content` sizing behavior, allowing the element to grow to fit its text content. When the text exceeds the modal's available width, the component pushes beyond the container boundary. The modal itself may lack `overflow: hidden` on its content area, allowing the overflow to propagate and create a horizontal scrollbar. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Apply a fixed width (`width: 100%`) to the Select component so it never exceeds the modal's content area. 2. Prevent content-driven expansion using CSS: * `overflow: hidden` * `text-overflow: ellipsis` * `white-space: nowrap` 3. Constrain the dropdown list width to match the Select component width — individual dropdown items should also truncate with ellipsis. 4. Expose the full relation label value via a `title` attribute (tooltip on hover) or a copy-to-clipboard action so users can still read the full text. 5. Verify the fix on both Conversation and Ticket domains. 6. Apply the same truncation/overflow fix to the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal (related issue #7) for consistency across all relation label modals. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: EC-003 — "Shared attribute display value is long (e.g. 50+ chars) → UI truncates display safely but keeps full value accessible on hover/detail." * **Related Bug Reports**: * `beri-tag-relasi-modal-long-text-overflow-no-char-limit.md` — the "Beri Tag Relasi" modal has the same overflow issue plus no character limit. The CSS fix recommended here should be applied to that modal as well. * **Domain**: Confirmed on both Conversation and Ticket domains. * **Trigger threshold**: Approximately 45 characters. * **Priority note**: This is a UI/UX issue — the feature remains functional once buttons are located, but the experience is degraded.

allWorkPackages.subject: Global Search Suggestion - Cross domain selection not disabled
allWorkPackages.description: # 🐞 Bug Report ## Summary In the Global Search popup, users can simultaneously check (select) Conversation results and Ticket results. The Product Manager has confirmed this is incorrect: when a user has already selected a result in one domain, hover and selection on the other domain should be disabled. This violates the expected cross-domain selection guard. Allowing both domains to be selected creates ambiguity, the user may incorrectly assume a single bulk action will apply across both domains, which is explicitly prohibited in Phase 1 (FR-007). The UI must enforce mutual exclusivity at the selection level, not merely display separate bulk action bars after selection. ## Environment ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Global Search popup by clicking **Cari** in the sidenav or pressing **Ctrl+K / Cmd+K**. 2. Enter a search keyword that returns both Conversation and Ticket results (for example, an AWB or Order ID value such as `1234`). 3. Wait for search results to load — verify both the **Percakapan** section and **Tiket** section appear with results. 4. Check the checkbox on a Conversation result — verify it becomes selected and the Conversation bulk action bar appears. 5. Hover over a checkbox on a Ticket result. 6. Click the checkbox on a Ticket result. 7. Observe the result. ## Actual Result * Hover state on the Ticket checkbox remains active (cursor changes, visual hover effect displayed). * The Ticket checkbox can still be clicked and becomes selected. * Both the Conversation bulk action bar **and** the Ticket bulk action bar are displayed simultaneously. * The user can have active selections in both domains at the same time. ## Expected Result * After a Conversation result is selected, hovering over any Ticket result checkbox should be **disabled** — no hover effect, cursor remains default. * Clicking a Ticket checkbox while a Conversation selection is active should have **no effect** — the checkbox must not become selected. * Conversely, after a Ticket result is selected, Conversation checkboxes should be disabled in the same manner. * Only one domain may have active selections at any time. * To switch domains, the user must first deselect all items in the currently active domain. ## Impact ## Evidence ## Initial Observation * Selecting a Conversation result does not disable Ticket result checkboxes. * Selecting a Ticket result does not disable Conversation result checkboxes. * Hover states remain active on the non-selected domain's checkboxes. * Both domain bulk action bars can appear simultaneously. * No visual indicator warns the user that cross-domain selection is not intended. ## Possible Root Cause _(Optional)_ Possible affected areas: * Frontend — Search result selection state management * Frontend — Checkbox component hover/disabled logic The selection state for Conversation and Ticket domains is likely managed independently with no cross-domain exclusion logic. Each domain's checkbox group operates in isolation, unaware of the other domain's selection state. The fix requires adding a mutual exclusion guard: when `selectedConversations.length > 0`, all Ticket checkboxes should render as disabled; when `selectedTickets.length > 0`, all Conversation checkboxes should render as disabled. ## Recommendation _(Optional)_ 1. Add cross-domain mutual exclusion logic to the selection state manager — track which domain currently holds active selections. 2. When one domain has selections (`count > 0`), set the other domain's checkbox `disabled` prop to `true` and suppress hover styling. 3. Ensure deselection of all items in the active domain re-enables the other domain's checkboxes. 4. Confirm the fix with PM against the expected UX: switching domains requires explicit deselection first. 5. Verify the fix does not affect the individual bulk action bars or the per-domain action execution logic. ## Additional Notes * **Related PRD**: Ticket #2228 — "Global Search - improvement autotag after search" (Actionable Shared Attribute Search & System Relation Labels) * **Related Requirement**: FR-006 \[P0\] — Conversation selection state MUST be separate from Ticket selection state. * **Related Requirement**: FR-007 \[P0\] — The system MUST NOT execute one mixed bulk action across Conversation and Ticket results in Phase 1. * **PM Confirmation**: Product Manager confirmed that cross-domain simultaneous selection is incorrect and must be treated as a bug. * **Precondition**: User is authenticated and has performed a search that returns results in both the Conversation and Ticket domains. * This bug was discovered during manual exploratory testing of the per-domain selection behavior.

allWorkPackages.subject: Auto-assign unassigned conversations when a channel is added to a team
allWorkPackages.description:
**Problem:** When an account channel is added to a Team, `conversation-service`'s `TEAM_ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_ADDED` handler only appends the new channel to conversations already on that team. Conversations on that same channel with no team assigned stay orphaned until someone manually calls the `syncTeamConversations` backup RPC.

**Solution:** Extend `updateConversationsWithNewAccountChannels` to also find OPEN, non-group, no-team conversations referencing the newly-added channel(s) and assign them to the team automatically — reusing the existing `assignNoTeamConversationsToTeam` logic from the manual sync path. Conversations already owned by a different team are never touched.

**Scope:** `omnichannel-satuinbox-be`, `conversation-service` only. No proto/schema changes. No people-service changes. Manual `syncTeamConversations` RPC remains as a fallback.

Plan: `.claude/PRPs/plans/team-channel-auto-assign-unassigned-conversations.plan.md`
