## **Description**

There is a state management issue in **Settings → Subscription → Payments → Manage Package** related to **voucher usage**.

When a voucher code has already been **validated or applied**, and the user changes the selected package or plan, the **voucher state is not reset**. The previously validated voucher remains applied even though the package selection has changed.

This can lead to incorrect voucher application or misleading billing calculations.

## **Steps to Reproduce**

1.  Navigate to **Settings → Subscription → Payments → Manage Package**
    
2.  Select a subscription package
    
3.  Enter and **validate a voucher code**
    
4.  Change the selected **package or plan**
    
5.  Observe the voucher input and validation state
    

## **Actual Result**

*   The previously validated voucher **remains applied**
    
*   Voucher input field **does not reset**
    
*   Voucher validation state remains **active**
    
*   User is not required to **revalidate the voucher** for the new plan
    

## **Expected Result**

*   When the user **changes the selected package/plan**:
    
    *   Voucher input should be **reset to empty**
        
    *   Voucher validation state should return to **unvalidated**
        
*   Users must **re-enter and validate the voucher again** for the newly selected plan
    
*   This ensures voucher eligibility is correctly recalculated based on the new plan
    

## **Affected Environment (Bug Found)**

*    [x]  Dev
*    [ ]  Staging
*    [x]  Prod

## **Tested Environment**

*    [ ]  Dev
*    [ ]  Staging
*    [ ]  Prod

## **Additional Notes**

Possible root causes:

*   Voucher validation state stored in component/global state not reset on plan change
    
*   Missing dependency handling between **plan selection and voucher state**
    

Impact:

*   Incorrect voucher application
    
*   Potential billing calculation errors
    
*   User confusion when changing packages

allWorkPackages.subject: SuperAdmin Global Company Access — **Phase 3: Controlled Write Mode + Quick Admin Actions**
allWorkPackages.description:
**\# TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT DOCUMENT (TRD) — Phase 3**

  
  

**\*\*Feature\*\***: SuperAdmin Global Company Access — **\*\*Phase 3: Controlled Write Mode + Quick Admin Actions\*\***

**\*\*Source PRD\*\***: \[\`prd/prd-superadmin-global-access.md\`\](../prd/prd-superadmin-global-access.md) (v1.0) — §5 US-007, §6 FR-023..030, §7 EH-005/006, §8 EC-005, §17 rows 5–6, §19 row 6, §20 Phase 3, §22, §23.

**\*\*Prereq TRDs\*\***: \[\`trd-superadmin-phase-1-...\`\](./trd-superadmin-phase-1-company-list-approval.md) (\`/system\` surface + audit), \[\`trd-superadmin-phase-2-...\`\](./trd-superadmin-phase-2-impersonation-readonly.md) (impersonation + read-only guard).

**\*\*Engineering Lead\*\***: Naftal Yunior

**\*\*Status\*\***: Draft for implementation hand-off

**\*\*Date (Asia/Jakarta)\*\***: 2026-07-01

  
  

> Phase 3 adds an **\*\*opt-in, allowlisted\*\*** write mode on top of Phase-2 impersonation: a SUPER\_ADMIN can explicitly switch a read-only impersonation session into write mode to run a small set of allowlisted quick admin actions (starting with \`change\_permission\`), each fully audited with before/after values. Everything outside the allowlist stays blocked. **\*\*This is the highest-risk phase and is feature-flagged.\*\*** References use \`path:line\`; **\*\*code wins over this file.\*\***

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 1. How this maps to the PRD (Phase 3)**

  
  

| PRD cluster | FRs / US | TRD section | Sub-phase |

|---|---|---|---|

| Explicit read-only→write switch | FR-024/025, US-007.1, §17 rows 5–6 | §6.1, §6.2 | 3a |

| Allowlisted quick actions only | FR-026, EC-005, §19 row 6 | §6.3 | 3a |

| \`change\_permission\` high-risk action | FR-027, US-007.2 | §6.4 | 3a |

| Write-mode audit (before/after) | FR-023, §22, §21 | §6.5 | 3a |

| No unrestricted mutation beyond allowlist | FR-030, US-007.3 | §5 D3, §6.2 | 3a |

| Write-mode UI (toggle + strong warning) | US-007.1, §9 write-mode indicator | §6.6 | 3b |

| Write mode denied when flag off | EH-006 | §6.1, §6.2 | 3a/3b |

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 2. Current-state (verified, Phase-3-relevant)**

  
  

\- Phase 2 delivers: \`impersonation\` claim on \`IJwtPayload\` with \`mode:'read\_only'\\|'write\_mode'\`; \`ImpersonateSession\`/\`EndImpersonation\` RPCs; the gateway \`ReadOnlyImpersonationGuard\` (method-based block under \`read\_only\`); \`superadmin\_audit\_logs\` + read RPC; the \`apps/system\` app + \`ImpersonationBanner\`.

\- **\*\*\`change\_permission\` already has a backend RPC\*\***: \`RoleService.UpdateRolePermissions(UpdateRolePermissionsRequest) returns (Role)\` (\[\`proto/auth.proto\`\](../backend/proto/auth.proto), \`RoleService\`). Role schema \`role.schema.ts\` has \`code\` + \`permission\[\]\` (\[\`apps/auth-service/src/app/schemas/role.schema.ts:14-64\`\](../backend/apps/auth-service/src/app/schemas/role.schema.ts#L14)). So the quick action **\*\*reuses an existing RPC\*\*** (constraint 3) — Phase 3 wraps it with allowlist + write-mode gating + before/after audit; it does not reimplement permission editing.

\- SUPER\_ADMIN perms include \`'\*'\` — so the switched token, in write mode, would technically be all-powerful. Phase 3 must **\*\*not\*\*** rely on the permission set to constrain writes; it constrains via the allowlist guard (D3).

\- No feature-flag primitive is assumed present; Phase 3 introduces a config-driven flag (§6.1).

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 3. Target architecture (Phase 3)**

  
  

\`\`\`

 apps/system (write-mode UI)          api-gateway /system                 auth-service

 ┌───────────────────────┐  enable  ┌──────────────────────────┐  gRPC   ┌───────────────────┐

 │ ⚠ "Mode tulis" toggle │─────────►│ EnableWriteMode          │────────►│ re-issue token     │

 │  (strong warning)     │  {impId} │  @AdminOnly + flag gate  │◄────────│ impersonation.mode │

 └───────────────────────┘          │                          │  token  │  = 'write\_mode'    │

        │ POST quick-actions/:action │                          │         └───────────────────┘

        ▼                            ▼

 ┌──────────────────────┐   QuickActionGuard: allow ONLY when mode==='write\_mode'

 │ change\_permission     │   AND action ∈ ALLOWLIST; everything else still blocked

 │  → RoleService.        │        │  reads before → calls RPC → reads after → emits audit

 │   UpdateRolePermissions│────────┘        (before/after values)

 └──────────────────────┘                       ▼  RabbitMQ

                                        ┌──────────────────┐

                                        │ superadmin audit  │ (before/after, actor, target)

                                        └──────────────────┘

\`\`\`

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 4. Phasing overview (Phase 3 sub-phases)**

  
  

| Sub-phase | Title | Scope | Depends on | Plan file |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| **\*\*3a\*\*** | Write-mode backend + quick actions | feature flag; \`EnableWriteMode\`/\`DisableWriteMode\` (re-issue token mode); allowlist + \`QuickActionGuard\`; \`change\_permission\` quick action wrapping \`UpdateRolePermissions\`; before/after audit | Phase 2a | \`.claude/plans/superadmin-phase-3a-write-mode-backend.md\` |

| **\*\*3b\*\*** | Write-mode frontend | write-mode toggle, strong warning banner/indicator, \`change\_permission\` UI, flag-off/denied states | 3a, Phase 2b | \`.claude/plans/superadmin-phase-3b-write-mode-frontend.md\` |

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 5. Cross-cutting decisions**

  
  

| # | Decision | Rationale / PRD link |

|---|---|---|

| D1 | Write mode is **\*\*opt-in and explicit\*\***: a separate \`EnableWriteMode\` step re-issues the impersonation token with \`impersonation.mode='write\_mode'\`. Read-only is the default and remains so unless this runs. | FR-024/025, §17 rows 5–6. |

| D2 | Write mode is **\*\*feature-flagged\*\*** (\`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_MODE\_ENABLED\`, default \`false\`). Flag off ⇒ \`EnableWriteMode\` refuses (\`write\_mode\_disabled\`, EH-006). | FR-024, §20 rollout (flag per phase). |

| D3 | Mutations are constrained by an **\*\*allowlist guard\*\***, NOT by the token's permission set. Even with \`'\*'\`, only routes in \`SUPERADMIN\_QUICK\_ACTION\_ALLOWLIST\` are permitted under \`write\_mode\`; every other mutating method stays blocked exactly as in read-only. | FR-026/030, EC-005, §23 (no silent unrestricted mutation). |

| D4 | Each quick action captures **\*\*before/after\*\*** state and audits it (\`superadmin\_write\_action\_executed\`), reusing the Phase-1 audit log with populated \`before\`/\`after\`. | FR-023/027, §21, §22. |

| D5 | \`change\_permission\` **\*\*reuses\*\*** \`RoleService.UpdateRolePermissions\` — no new permission-edit logic. The quick-action wrapper adds gating + before/after diff + audit. | constraint 3; §2. |

| D6 | Quick actions define idempotency/safe-retry: the wrapper reads current state first and treats a no-op change as success; a correlation/idempotency key prevents duplicate audits on retry. | §23 retry test, NFR reliability. |

| D7 | Write mode is **\*\*visually distinct\*\*** and requires explicit confirmation in the UI; the banner switches from \`Mode baca saja\` to a strong-warning \`Mode tulis\`. | FR-025, US-007.1, §9. |

| D8 | Disabling write mode (or exiting impersonation) drops back to read-only/normal and re-issues the token accordingly; write rights are removed immediately. | §17 row 6. |

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 6. Detailed design (3a backend)**

  
  

**\### 6.1 Feature flag + mode switch RPCs**

  
  

\- **\*\*Flag\*\***: config key \`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_MODE\_ENABLED\` (default \`false\`) in the api-gateway config factory (and, if needed, auth-service). Read via \`ConfigService.get('superadmin.writeModeEnabled', false)\`.

\- **\*\*RPCs\*\*** — \[\`proto/auth.proto\`\](../backend/proto/auth.proto), \`AuthService\`:

\`\`\`proto

rpc EnableWriteMode(WriteModeRequest) returns (LoginResponse);

rpc DisableWriteMode(WriteModeRequest) returns (LoginResponse);

message WriteModeRequest {

  string impersonationId = 1;

  string actorUserId = 2;

  optional common.MetaData metadata = 3;

}

\`\`\`

\`EnableWriteMode\`: validate the session is an active impersonation owned by \`actorUserId\`, then re-issue tokens with the same \`impersonation\` block but \`mode:'write\_mode'\`; update \`session.metadata.impersonation.mode\` and \`session.accessToken/refreshToken\`. \`DisableWriteMode\`: symmetric, back to \`read\_only\`. Preserve \`impersonationId\` + actor identity (Phase-2 D4/D5).

  
  

**\### 6.2 Gateway — enable/disable + quick-action guard**

  
  

\- \`SystemImpersonationController\` (Phase 2) gains: \`POST /system/impersonation/write-mode/enable\` and \`.../disable\` (\`@AdminOnly()\`). \`enable\` first checks the flag (D2) → if off, \`403 write\_mode\_disabled\` (EH-006). On success emit \`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_MODE\_ENABLED\`/\`\_DISABLED\` audit; return the re-issued token (the FE must swap its session token — same handoff plumbing as Phase 2).

\- **\*\*\`QuickActionGuard\`\*\*** (gateway): for \`POST /system/quick-actions/:action\`, require \`impersonation.mode==='write\_mode'\` **\*\*and\*\*** \`:action ∈ SUPERADMIN\_QUICK\_ACTION\_ALLOWLIST\` (a constant, initially \`\['change\_permission'\]\`). Otherwise \`403 action\_not\_allowed\`. The Phase-2 \`ReadOnlyImpersonationGuard\` must be updated to **\*\*not\*\*** blanket-block the allowlisted quick-action route when \`mode==='write\_mode'\`, while still blocking everything else (D3). Net effect: under \`write\_mode\`, only \`/system/quick-actions/:action\` for allowlisted actions is writable; all other tenant writes remain blocked.

  
  

**\### 6.3 Quick-action controller + allowlist**

  
  

\- New \`SystemQuickActionController\` in \`SystemModule\`: \`POST /system/quick-actions/:action\` with \`@AdminOnly()\` + \`QuickActionGuard\`. Dispatch on \`:action\` to a small handler map keyed by the allowlist. Unknown/blocked action → \`action\_not\_allowed\` (EC-005). DTO validated per action.

\- \`SUPERADMIN\_QUICK\_ACTION\_ALLOWLIST\` constant lives in a shared \`system\` constants file; every entry names the target RPC + the DTO + the before/after reader. Adding a future action is: allowlist entry + handler + DTO + audit reader (PRD §20 "add allowlisted quick actions one by one").

  
  

**\### 6.4 \`change\_permission\` quick action (FR-027)**

  
  

\- DTO \`ChangePermissionDto{ roleId, permissions: string\[\] }\` (validated). Handler:

  1. **\*\*Read before\*\***: \`RoleService.GetRolesById({ roleId })\` → capture \`permission\[\]\` (before).

  2. **\*\*Apply\*\***: \`RoleService.UpdateRolePermissions({ roleId, permissions })\` (existing RPC, D5) in the target tenant context (the switched token carries target \`companyId\`).

  3. **\*\*Read after\*\***: the RPC returns the updated \`Role\`; capture \`permission\[\]\` (after).

  4. **\*\*Audit\*\*** (§6.5) with before/after.

\- Because changing a role's permissions can invalidate active tenant sessions, reuse the existing \`SessionInvalidationReasonEnum.ROLE\_CHANGED\` path if the underlying flow already triggers it (verify; do not add a second invalidation model).

  
  

**\### 6.5 Write-mode audit (before/after)**

  
  

\- New \`EventTypeEnum\`: \`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_MODE\_ENABLED='superadmin.write\_mode.enabled'\`, \`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_MODE\_DISABLED='superadmin.write\_mode.disabled'\`, \`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_ACTION\_EXECUTED='superadmin.write\_action.executed'\`. Add \`@EventPattern\` handlers (extend Phase-1b processor).

\- \`SUPERADMIN\_WRITE\_ACTION\_EXECUTED\` payload populates the \`before\`/\`after\` fields of \`superadmin\_audit\_logs\`: \`{ actorUserId, actorRole, action:'change\_permission', targetType:'role', targetId:roleId, targetCompanyId, before:{permission}, after:{permission}, metadata:{ impersonationId }, correlationId }\`. Surface in the Phase-2 \`GET /system/audit-logs\` read view.

  
  

**\### 6.6 Frontend — write-mode UX (3b)**

  
  

\- **\*\*Toggle\*\***: in the tenant UI banner (impersonation, from Phase 2b), add a \`Mode tulis\` toggle, **\*\*only visible when the flag is on\*\*** (the FE learns flag state from a \`/system\` capability endpoint or the enable call's response). Enabling requires an explicit confirm dialog (D7) → \`POST .../write-mode/enable\` → swap session token → banner switches to the strong-warning write style (\`FR-025\`).

\- **\*\*Quick action UI\*\***: a \`change\_permission\` panel (role picker + permission editor) that calls \`POST /system/quick-actions/change\_permission\`. Success/error toasts; on success, refetch role state.

\- **\*\*Denied/flag-off states\*\***: if the flag is off, the toggle is hidden/disabled and any attempt surfaces \`Mode tulis belum tersedia\` (EH-006). A blocked non-allowlisted write still shows the read-only/blocked message.

\- **\*\*Disable/exit\*\***: disabling write mode or exiting impersonation immediately reverts to read-only/normal (D8) and swaps the token.

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 7. Security, performance, testing**

  
  

\- **\*\*Security\*\***: allowlist guard is the sole authority for what can mutate (D3) — permission \`'\*'\` never widens the surface. Write mode is flag-gated (D2) and fully audited with before/after (D4). Confirm \`change\_permission\` cannot escalate the SUPER\_ADMIN's own or cross-tenant roles beyond the target tenant (the switched token scopes to the target company).

\- **\*\*Idempotency/concurrency\*\*** (§23): no-op permission change → success + audited as no-op; retries deduped by correlation/idempotency key (D6).

\- **\*\*Testing\*\***:

  - auth-service: enable/disable re-issues token with correct \`mode\`; flag off → refused; actor/target preserved.

  - api-gateway: \`QuickActionGuard\` allows only allowlisted action under \`write\_mode\`, blocks otherwise (EC-005); non-allowlisted → \`action\_not\_allowed\`; other tenant writes still blocked under write\_mode; flag-off enable → \`write\_mode\_disabled\`.

  - quick action: change\_permission reads before, applies, reads after, audits before/after; no-op safe; retry deduped.

  - audit-service: write-action log carries before/after; enable/disable logged.

  - frontend: toggle gated by flag; confirm dialog; strong-warning banner; change\_permission panel; denied states.

\- Backend Jest co-located AAA, ≥80% new units; FE \`check-types\`/\`lint\`.

  
  

**\---**

  
  

**\## 8. Open questions**

  
  

\- How the FE discovers the write-mode flag state (dedicated capability endpoint vs enable-call response) — recommend a small \`GET /system/capabilities\` returning \`{ writeModeEnabled }\`.

\- Confirm the initial allowlist beyond \`change\_permission\` (PRD §16 open question: final quick-action allowlist).

\- Whether \`change\_permission\` should require a second confirmation / reason field for the audit (recommend a \`reason\` in the DTO for FR-027 governance).

\- ~~~~Token swap on enable/disable~~~~ **\*\*LOCKED\*\***: happens inside the already-authenticated omnichannel impersonation session via next-auth \`update()\` with the re-issued token — the Phase-2 \`handoffCode\` mechanism is only for the initial system→omnichannel entry, not for mode changes.

\- Rollback: flag off mid-session should force any active write-mode session back to read-only on next refresh (recommend enforcing in the refresh path).

allWorkPackages.subject: SuperAdmin Global Company Access — **Phase 2: Tenant Impersonation (Read-Only) + Audit**
allWorkPackages.description:
# TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT DOCUMENT (TRD) — Phase 2

**Feature**: SuperAdmin Global Company Access — **Phase 2: Tenant Impersonation (Read-Only) + Audit**
**Source PRD**: [`prd/prd-superadmin-global-access.md`](../prd/prd-superadmin-global-access.md) (v1.0) — §5 US-005/006, §6 FR-015..022, §7 EH-004/005, §17 rows 3–4, §19 rows 4–5, §20 Phase 2, §22.
**Prereq TRD**: [`trd-superadmin-phase-1-company-list-approval.md`](./trd-superadmin-phase-1-company-list-approval.md) (gateway `/system` surface + audit foundation).
**Engineering Lead**: Naftal Yunior
**Status**: Draft for implementation hand-off
**Date (Asia/Jakarta)**: 2026-07-01

> Phase 2 lets a SUPER_ADMIN switch into a target tenant's context in **read-only** mode via a purpose-issued "switched session" token that preserves the real actor identity, and makes every enter/exit auditable. It **must not** remove tenant scoping from downstream services — the switched token carries the *target* `companyId`/`organizationId`, so existing single-tenant services behave exactly as they do for a normal tenant user; read-only-ness is enforced at the gateway. References use `path:line`; **code wins over this file.**

---

## 1. How this maps to the PRD (Phase 2)

| PRD cluster | FRs / US | TRD section | Sub-phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Impersonation / switch context | FR-015..017, US-005.1, §17 rows 3–4, §19 rows 4–5 | §6.1, §6.2 | 2a |
| Preserve single-tenant runtime | FR-016/029 | §5 D2, §6.1 | 2a |
| Actor metadata in session | FR-017 | §6.1.2 | 2a |
| Read-only enforcement (backend) | FR-018/019, EH-005, EC-003, §23 | §6.3 | 2a |
| Read-only + banner (frontend) | FR-020, US-005.2/005.3 | §6.5 | 2b |
| Invalid target handling | EH-004, EC-002 | §6.2 | 2a |
| Impersonation audit start/end + read view | FR-022, §22 | §6.4 | 2a |

---

## 2. Current-state (verified, Phase-2-relevant)

- **JWT claims** `IJwtPayload` ([`libs/common/src/lib/interfaces/index.ts:195-210`](../backend/libs/common/src/lib/interfaces/index.ts#L195)): `{ companyId?, organizationId?, username?, email?, exp?, iat?, role?:{name?,code?,permission?:string[]}, sub /*userId*/, sessionId, type:'access'|'refresh' }`. Downstream tenant scoping is derived from `companyId`/`organizationId` in this token (propagated via `@RequestContext().tenant`).
- **Token signing** `JwtTokenService.generateAccessToken()` ([`apps/auth-service/src/app/services/jwt-token.service.ts:136-145`](../backend/apps/auth-service/src/app/services/jwt-token.service.ts#L136)); role built by `toTokenRole()` (~`:110-128`). Secrets/expiry from `jwt.access.*` (`JWT_ACCESS_SECRET`, default `15m`); issuer `satuinbox-app`, audience `satuinbox-users`.
- **Login/refresh** `Login`/`RefreshToken` RPCs ([`proto/auth.proto:12-14`](../backend/proto/auth.proto#L12)) → `LoginResponse{ accessToken, refreshToken, sessionId, onboardingStatus, user, role, teams }`. Controller `app.controller.ts` (~`:115-199`).
- **Session schema** ([`apps/auth-service/src/app/schemas/session.schema.ts`](../backend/apps/auth-service/src/app/schemas/session.schema.ts)): `sessionId` (unique), `userId`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `companyId`, `organizationId`, `isActive`, `onboardingStatus`, `expiresAt` (TTL ~30d), `invalidatedAt`/`invalidationReason`, **`metadata` (generic Object, ~`:132`)**. `metadata` is the natural home for impersonation actor data.
- **RBAC**: `RoleTypeEnum.SUPER_ADMIN` ([`enums/index.ts:14-22`](../backend/libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts#L14)); SUPER_ADMIN perms `['*', VIEW_FULL_EMAIL, VIEW_FULL_PHONE]` ([`default-permission.constant.ts:249-253`](../backend/libs/common/src/lib/constants/default-permission.constant.ts#L249)). `SessionInvalidationReasonEnum` ([`enums/index.ts:1524-1529`](../backend/libs/common/src/lib/enums/index.ts#L1524)).
- **One organization per company** (company-service, Phase-1 TRD §2.3) — needed for target selection (EC-002).
- **No impersonation of any kind exists** — greenfield (grep for `impersonat`/`actAs`/`onBehalf`/`switch` in auth-service: none).
- **Gateway audit foundation** (from Phase 1b): `superadmin_audit_logs` schema + `@EventPattern` processor + `EventTypeEnum.SUPERADMIN_*` + emit-from-gateway pattern. Phase 2 extends it (§6.4).

---

## 3. Target architecture (Phase 2)

```
 apps/system                    api-gateway /system                    auth-service
 ┌────────────┐  POST start   ┌────────────────────────┐  gRPC       ┌────────────────────┐
 │ "Masuk     │──────────────►│ SystemImpersonation     │────────────►│ ImpersonateSession  │
 │  sebagai   │  {companyId,  │  Controller  @AdminOnly  │ Start/End   │  • validate target  │
 │  tenant"   │   orgId}      │  → switched token        │◄────────────│  • issue token w/    │
 └────────────┘               └───────────┬─────────────┘  token       │    target tenant +   │
        │ switched token (banner claims)  │                            │    impersonation meta│
        ▼                                 │ emit audit (RabbitMQ)      └────────────────────┘
 ┌─────────────────────────────┐         ▼
 │ tenant UI (omnichannel) with │   ┌──────────────────┐   ReadOnlyGuard on api-gateway blocks
 │ ImpersonationBanner + RO mode│   │ audit-service     │   mutating methods when the token's
 └─────────────────────────────┘   │ impersonation log │   impersonation.mode === 'read_only'
                                    └──────────────────┘
```

Downstream services (conversation/ticket/etc.) receive the switched token with the **target** `companyId`/`organizationId` and behave normally — they never learn it is an impersonation (FR-016/029). Read-only is a **gateway concern**.

---

## 4. Phasing overview (Phase 2 sub-phases)

| Sub-phase | Title | Scope | Depends on | Plan file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **2a** | Impersonation backend + read-only guard + audit | `IJwtPayload` extension; `ImpersonateSession`/`EndImpersonation` RPCs; gateway start/end controller; `ReadOnlyGuard`; impersonation audit events + read RPC/endpoint | Phase 1a/1b | `.claude/plans/superadmin-phase-2a-impersonation-backend.md` |
| **2b** | Impersonation frontend | Impersonation entry (row action + org confirm), switched-session handoff, global `ImpersonationBanner`, FE read-only affordances, end-impersonation | 2a | `.claude/plans/superadmin-phase-2b-impersonation-frontend.md` |

---

## 5. Cross-cutting decisions

| # | Decision | Rationale / PRD link |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | The switched token is a **normal-shaped access token** whose `companyId`/`organizationId` are the **target tenant's**, so all downstream tenant-scoped services work unchanged. | FR-016/029; §2 (scoping derives from token tenant). |
| D2 | Add an `impersonation` claim block to `IJwtPayload` (optional, backward-compatible): `{ actorUserId, actorRole, actorCompanyId?, actorOrganizationId?, mode:'read_only'\|'write_mode', impersonationId }`. Absent ⇒ a normal session (no behavior change). | FR-017; §2 claims. |
| D3 | **Read-only is enforced at the api-gateway** via a global `ReadOnlyImpersonationGuard`: when `impersonation.mode==='read_only'`, block any state-changing HTTP method (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) except the explicit exit route. Downstream guards are defense-in-depth but the gateway is authoritative. | FR-018/019, EH-005, EC-003, §23 (backend MUST enforce, not FE only). |
| D4 | The impersonation actor identity lives in **both** the token claim (D2) *and* the auth-service `session.metadata` (§2), so exit/refresh can restore the actor and audits can be reconstructed. | FR-017, §21 (preserve actor+target). |
| D5 | **Refresh preserves impersonation**: `RefreshToken` for an impersonation session re-issues a token carrying the same `impersonation` block + target tenant; it never silently upgrades mode. | §23 multi-tab, FR-025 (Phase 3 opt-in only). |
| D6 | Exit impersonation = end the switched session and return to the SUPER_ADMIN's normal context. The system app keeps the SUPER_ADMIN's own session; the switched token is a **separate** session, so exiting never disturbs the admin's platform session. | FR-017, §17 row 4, §28 non-side-effects. |
| D7 | Target validation: company must exist and `organizationId` must belong to it; if a company had multiple orgs, require explicit selection (EC-002) — with one-org-per-company today, default to the sole org but still pass it explicitly. Invalid ⇒ `invalid_target` (EH-004). | EH-004, EC-002. |
| D8 | Impersonation start/end audits reuse the Phase-1 `superadmin_audit_logs` schema + emit pattern; add `SUPERADMIN_IMPERSONATION_STARTED/ENDED` events with actor + target + mode. Add a **read** RPC/endpoint now (the superadmin audit view). | FR-022, §22, §21. |
| D9 | **Cross-app handoff (LOCKED)** — one-time handoff code + next-auth impersonation provider. `start` issues the switched tokens **server-side**, stores them in Redis (via `@omnichannel-satuinbox-be/cache`) keyed by a single-use `handoffCode` (~60s TTL), and returns `{ handoffCode, target }` — **never raw tokens** to the browser. The system app redirects the browser to omnichannel `/{locale}/impersonation/handoff?code=…`; that route calls `signIn('impersonation', { code })`, whose Credentials path POSTs the code to `POST /system/impersonation/exchange`, which validates + **consumes** it and returns the switched tokens + `impersonation` claim → next-auth builds the impersonation session. No raw token ever transits the URL. | US-005.2, §9 banner. Chosen over tokens-in-URL (leak), shared-domain cookie (fragile/CSRF), password re-auth (no password). |

---

## 6. Detailed design

### 6.1 auth-service — switched session (2a)

**6.1.1 Claims.** Extend `IJwtPayload` ([`interfaces/index.ts:195`](../backend/libs/common/src/lib/interfaces/index.ts#L195)) with optional `impersonation?: { actorUserId: string; actorRole: string; actorCompanyId?: string; actorOrganizationId?: string; mode: 'read_only' | 'write_mode'; impersonationId: string }`. Optional ⇒ every existing token stays valid (D2). Update `toTokenRole`/token-builder path to pass it through when present.

**6.1.2 RPCs** — [`proto/auth.proto`](../backend/proto/auth.proto), `AuthService`:
```proto
rpc ImpersonateSession(ImpersonateSessionRequest) returns (LoginResponse);
rpc EndImpersonation(EndImpersonationRequest) returns (common.Success);

message ImpersonateSessionRequest {
  string actorUserId = 1;          // real SUPER_ADMIN (from gateway RequestContext)
  string actorRole = 2;
  string targetCompanyId = 3;
  string targetOrganizationId = 4;
  string mode = 5;                 // 'read_only' (Phase 2 always read_only)
  optional common.MetaData metadata = 6;
}
message EndImpersonationRequest {
  string impersonationId = 1;
  string actorUserId = 2;
  optional common.MetaData metadata = 3;
}
```
`ImpersonateSession` service method: validate the actor is SUPER_ADMIN (defense-in-depth; gateway already gates), validate target company/org (D7 — call company-service `GetCompany`/org lookup over gRPC, no cross-DB read), create a **new session** (`session.schema`) with `userId = actorUserId`, `companyId/organizationId = target`, `metadata = { impersonation:{ actorUserId, actorRole, actorCompanyId, actorOrganizationId, mode, impersonationId } }`, `isActive:true`, issue access+refresh tokens carrying the `impersonation` claim + target tenant, return `LoginResponse`. `impersonationId` = a generated id (pass a UUID in from the gateway or via metadata — scripts can't `Math.random`, but service runtime can use `crypto.randomUUID()`). `EndImpersonation`: mark that session `isActive:false`, `invalidatedAt`, `invalidationReason = 'IMPERSONATION_ENDED'` (add to `SessionInvalidationReasonEnum`). Refresh path (D5): detect `impersonation` in the session/metadata and preserve it.

**6.1.3 No change to normal login.** `Login` is untouched; a normal user never gets an `impersonation` claim.

### 6.2 Gateway — start/end impersonation (2a)

New `SystemImpersonationController` in `SystemModule` (`@AdminOnly()`, `@ApiBearerAuth()`, appears on `/system/docs`):
- `POST /system/impersonation/start` — body `StartImpersonationDto{ companyId, organizationId? }` (validated). Resolve actor from `@RequestContext().user` (D7); if `organizationId` omitted and the company has exactly one org, resolve it; if multiple, require it (EC-002 → 400). Call `ImpersonateSession({ actorUserId, actorRole:'SUPER_ADMIN', targetCompanyId, targetOrganizationId, mode:'read_only', metadata })`. On success: store the returned switched tokens server-side in Redis keyed by a single-use `handoffCode` (~60s TTL), emit `SUPERADMIN_IMPERSONATION_STARTED` audit (§6.4), and return `{ handoffCode, target:{ companyId, organizationId, companyName }, mode:'read_only' }` — **never the raw tokens** (D9). Invalid target ⇒ `invalid_target` → mapped to a clear 4xx (EH-004).
- `POST /system/impersonation/exchange` — body `{ handoffCode }`. Validate + **consume** (single-use) the code from Redis; return `{ accessToken, refreshToken, impersonationId, user, role, target, mode }` for next-auth to build the impersonation session. Expired/used/invalid ⇒ 4xx. Called by omnichannel's next-auth impersonation Credentials provider (D9). `@Public()` at the JWT layer (the code *is* the credential) but rate-limited.
- `POST /system/impersonation/end` — body `{ impersonationId }`. Call `EndImpersonation`; emit `SUPERADMIN_IMPERSONATION_ENDED`; return success. This route is on the **exit allowlist** of the ReadOnlyGuard (D3).

### 6.3 Gateway — read-only enforcement (2a)

`ReadOnlyImpersonationGuard` (global, registered app-wide in api-gateway):
- Read the validated JWT (already on `request.user`); if `impersonation?.mode === 'read_only'`:
  - Allow `GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` and the exact exit route (`POST /system/impersonation/end`).
  - Block any other method → throw `ForbiddenException` with code/message `Mode baca saja aktif. Aksi ini tidak diizinkan.` (EH-005) and emit `superadmin_readonly_block_total{actorId, route, method}` (PRD §22).
- Register **after** `JwtAuthGuard` so `request.user` is populated. Non-impersonation requests pass through untouched (zero effect on normal tenants — FR-028/029).
- This is method-based (not per-route allowlist) so *newly added* tenant write endpoints are automatically covered — no maintenance risk of a "hidden write path" (§23, PRD risk "Read-only enforcement coverage"). Document that any GET-with-side-effects endpoint (there should be none) would be a gap.

### 6.4 Impersonation audit + read view (2a)

- New `EventTypeEnum`: `SUPERADMIN_IMPERSONATION_STARTED = 'superadmin.impersonation.started'`, `SUPERADMIN_IMPERSONATION_ENDED = 'superadmin.impersonation.ended'`. Add matching `@EventPattern` handlers to the `superadmin-audit-log.processor.ts` (Phase 1b) → same `superadmin_audit_logs` collection. Payload: `{ actorUserId, actorRole, action, targetType:'tenant', targetCompanyId, targetOrganizationId, metadata:{ impersonationId, mode }, correlationId, ipAddress, userAgent }`.
- **Read API** (new, for the superadmin audit/impersonation view — FR-022 traceability): add `QuerySuperadminAuditLogs` RPC to `audit.proto` (`{ pagination, action?, actorUserId?, targetCompanyId?, dateFrom?, dateTo? } → { items[], pagination }`) implemented in audit-service, fronted by a gateway `GET /system/audit-logs` on `SystemModule` (`@AdminOnly()`). This is the first audit-service read path (§2 — none exists today).

### 6.5 Frontend — impersonation UX (2b)

- **Entry**: in the Phase-1 company list/detail, add `Masuk sebagai tenant ini` action (row + detail drawer). If the company has multiple orgs, show an org selector (EC-002); else confirm with the single org. Calls `POST /system/impersonation/start`.
- **Cross-app handoff (D9, LOCKED)**: on `start` success the system app receives only a single-use `handoffCode` + target; it redirects the browser to omnichannel `/{locale}/impersonation/handoff?code=<handoffCode>`. That route calls next-auth `signIn('impersonation', { code })`; the omnichannel **impersonation Credentials provider** POSTs the code to `POST /system/impersonation/exchange`, receives the switched tokens + `impersonation` claim, and next-auth builds the impersonation session (separate from the admin's platform session, D6). No raw token transits the URL.
- **Banner (FR-020, US-005.2)**: a global `ImpersonationBanner` in `omnichannel` (rendered in the app shell when `session.user.impersonation` is present) stating `Mode baca saja` + target company/org + an `Exit`/`Keluar` button → `POST /system/impersonation/end` → destroy the impersonation session → return to the system app.
- **FE read-only affordances**: hide/disable obvious write controls when `impersonation.mode==='read_only'` (UX only; the gateway is the real guard, D3). A blocked write (if attempted) surfaces the EH-005 toast from the 403 body.
- next-auth `next-auth.d.ts` (omnichannel): augment session/JWT with the optional `impersonation` block so the banner + guards can read it.

---

## 7. Security, performance, testing

- **Security**: switched token uses the same signing/secrets (no new trust root). Actor identity is immutable in the claim + session metadata (D4); it cannot be stripped by refresh (D5). Read-only enforced server-side, method-based (D3). Impersonation start/end fully audited (§6.4).
- **Performance**: impersonation start is a single gRPC round-trip + token issue; banner reads from the session (no extra call). Audit is async (RabbitMQ).
- **Testing**:
  - auth-service: token carries `impersonation` claim + target tenant; invalid target → error (EH-004); refresh preserves claim (D5); end marks session inactive.
  - api-gateway: `ReadOnlyImpersonationGuard` blocks POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE under read_only, allows GET + exit route, no-ops for normal tokens; start/end controllers; audit emitted; read-logs endpoint scoping.
  - audit-service: impersonation start/end persisted; query RPC filters + paginates.
  - frontend: banner renders under impersonation session; exit flow; write controls disabled; blocked-write toast.
- Backend Jest co-located AAA; ≥80% new units. `npx nx test auth-service|api-gateway|audit-service`; FE `npm run check-types`/`lint`.

---

## 8. Open questions

- ~~Cross-app handoff mechanism (D9)~~ **LOCKED**: one-time `handoffCode` (server-side tokens in Redis, single-use ~60s) + omnichannel next-auth impersonation Credentials provider + `POST /system/impersonation/exchange` (see D9 / §6.2 / §6.5).
- Default-org rule when a company has multiple orgs (EC-002) — assumed explicit selection required.
- Whether FE read-only should also visually lock the tenant UI globally (overlay) vs per-control disabling (assumed per-control + gateway guard).
- Session TTL for impersonation sessions (reuse 30d default vs a shorter, e.g. 1–2h, impersonation-specific TTL — recommend shorter for safety).
- Whether `EndImpersonation` should also be callable implicitly on token expiry (natural session TTL) — yes, via existing TTL; explicit end still audited.

allWorkPackages.subject: Edit Member and Align User Identity Model (Display Name, Username, Email, Login Behavior)
allWorkPackages.description: PRD: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1H3r4OCqQUd9cmSZtkEVHqjcMFtXlF4xGeH6\_Z4eE0/edit?tab=t.gzhfpkdgeg06](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1H3r4OCqQUd9cmSZtkEVHqjcMFtXlF4xGeH6_Z4eE0/edit?tab=t.gzhfpkdgeg06) Goals: * Adding display name (Alias) * Change all in apps show regarding user using Fullname * Change for public such as in widget using display name (Alias) QA inputs : # Gambaran Perubahan Perubahan utama menyentuh: * **Login identifier (username/email)** * **Display name (alias baru)** * **Struktur data user di People Service** * **Relasi member & team** * **Integrasi ke Conversation & Auth** Artinya ini bukan sekadar UI change — tapi menyentuh **core identity system**. # 1\. People Service (User, Member, Team) ### Impact: **5 (Critical)** ## Kenapa tinggi: Ini adalah **source of truth** untuk semua identity. ### Area terdampak: * **User** * tambah field: `alias / displayName` * perubahan logic: * validation (required, trimming, length) * optional email * **Username** * harus unique per **universal** * **Schema & DB** * migration diperlukan * **Search logic** * sekarang multi-field: * displayName * username * email ### Risiko: * ❗ Breaking change di API response * ❗ Query jadi lebih kompleks (multi-index) * ❗ Data inconsistency kalau migration gagal ### Edge Risk: * User tanpa email * Username conflict saat migration * Data lama tidak punya alias # 2\. Auth Service ### Impact: **5 (Critical)** ## Kenapa tinggi: Auth sangat sensitif karena: * semua login bergantung ke sini * perubahan identifier (email/username) ### Area terdampak: * Login logic: * support **email OR username** * Validation: * user lookup jadi multi-field * Password validation tetap, tapi entry point berubah ### Risiko: * ❗ Login failure massal jika mapping salah * ❗ Ambiguity: * username mirip email * ❗ Security risk: * brute force surface lebih luas ### Edge Risk: * Case sensitivity * Multiple identifier match (harus deterministic) * Rate limiting harus tetap jalan # 3\. Conversation Service ### Impact: **4 (High)** ## Kenapa: Tidak mengubah logic utama, tapi **display & reference user berubah** ### Area terdampak: * Menampilkan: * displayName (alias baru) * bukan fullname lama * Data dependency: * ambil data dari People Service ### Risiko: * ❗ Cache inconsistency (nama lama vs baru) * ❗ Historical conversation: * pakai nama lama atau update? ### Edge Case: * User rename saat conversation ongoing * Reopen chat → nama berubah * Multiple agent dalam 1 room # 4\. Member & Team Relation ### Impact: **3 (Medium)** ## Kenapa: Relasi tidak berubah struktur, tapi: * bergantung ke user identity ### Area terdampak: * Member: * tetap pakai `userId` * Team: * tetap pakai `memberId` ### Risiko: * ⚠️ Minimal, karena tidak ubah relasi * ⚠️ Tapi impact dari user update bisa propagate ### Edge Case: * User dihapus / berubah → relasi tetap valid? * Display name berubah → team UI ikut berubah # 5\. Company & Organization Layer (Multi-Tenant) ### Impact: **4 (High)** ## Kenapa: Semua logic username harus: * scoped ke tenant ### Area terdampak: * Unique constraint: * username harus unik **per tenant** * Query: * semua search & login harus include: * `companyId` * `organizationId` ### Risiko: * ❗ Cross-tenant data leakage * ❗ Username conflict antar tenant ### Edge Case: * User pindah organization * Username sama di tenant berbeda # Ringkasan Impact # Risiko Utama (Yang Harus Kamu Antisipasi) ## 1\. Data Migration * fullname → alias/displayName * missing email * duplicate username ## 2\. Login Breaking * user tidak bisa login setelah deploy * ambiguity identifier ## 3\. Cross-Service Sync * conversation pakai data lama * cache tidak ke-refresh ## 4\. Query Performance * search multi-field: * perlu index: * username * email * displayName

allWorkPackages.description:
PRD: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1H3r4OCqQUd9cmSZtkEVHqjcMFtXlF4xGeH6\_Z4eE0/edit?tab=t.d12hw3cwhjmz](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1H3r4OCqQUd9cmSZtkEVHqjcMFtXlF4xGeH6_Z4eE0/edit?tab=t.d12hw3cwhjmz) Design: [https://www.figma.com/design/RAAuLaQKUufWMWWEm0kMb9/-V2--Satuinbox-Web-Specs?node-id=988-70441&t=2GSfLgxEqR90Q4WY-4](https://www.figma.com/design/RAAuLaQKUufWMWWEm0kMb9/-V2--Satuinbox-Web-Specs?node-id=988-70441&t=2GSfLgxEqR90Q4WY-4)
**Task Description** Implement WhatsApp Web account connection with queue-based onboarding and configurable chat import modes. Users must be able to connect accounts through a queue flow, set an import mode per account, and manage the mode again later through edit mode after the account is connected.
--- ## 🎯 ANALISA IMPACT BY QA ### Overview Impact Fitur ini memperkenalkan **Queue Connect Flow** dan **Import Modes** yang akan mengubah cara pengguna connect WhatsApp Web accounts. Dari perspektif QA, ini adalah **HIGH RISK** feature karena: 1. Mengubah core flow connect yang sudah ada 2. Memperkenalkan state management yang kompleks (queue states) 3. Impact ke data existing (conversation import logic) --- ### 📊 Services Impact Mapping ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ EXISTING SERVICES & IMPACT LEVEL │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ 🔴 HIGH IMPACT │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ 1. CHANNEL SERVICE (Account Channel) │ │ │ │ • New fields: import_mode, import_mode_config, queue_state │ │ │ │ • New endpoints: queue management, import mode CRUD │ │ │ │ • Business logic: queue session, mode validation │ │ │ │ ⚠️ TEST FOCUS: Data migration existing accounts │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ 2. WHATSAPP SERVICE (WhatsApp Connector) │ │ │ │ • QR generation per queue item (not just per account) │ │ │ │ • Queue context awareness for QR sessions │ │ │ │ • Public link generation (10-min expiry) │ │ │ │ • Post-connect callback untuk trigger selection screen │ │ │ │ ⚠️ TEST FOCUS: QR expiration, concurrent queue access │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ 🟡 MEDIUM IMPACT │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ 3. CONVERSATION SERVICE │ │ │ │ • Import filtering logic based on import_mode │ │ │ │ • Full Import: allow all chats │ │ │ │ • Whitelist: only allow selected targets │ │ │ │ • Exclude: allow all except selected │ │ │ │ • Ignored event counter (tidak store message content) │ │ │ │ ⚠️ TEST FOCUS: Import timing (60s P95), deduplication │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ 4. PEOPLE SERVICE (Client Contact) │ │ │ │ • Target normalization (phone number, group identifier) │ │ │ │ • Contact matching untuk whitelist/exclude selection │ │ │ │ • Search by number, name, conversation title │ │ │ │ ⚠️ TEST FOCUS: Contact deduplication, search accuracy │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ 🟢 LOW IMPACT │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ 5. COMPANY SERVICE (Client Data) │ │ │ │ • Audit log storage untuk connect, mode change events │ │ │ │ • Minimal impact - mostly read-only untuk audit queries │ │ │ │ ⚠️ TEST FOCUS: Audit log completeness, data retention │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ### 🎯 Critical Test Scenarios by Service #### **CHANNEL SERVICE** (Account Channel) ``` Priority: P0 Test Scenarios: ✅ TC-CH-001: Create queue session with multiple not-connected accounts ✅ TC-CH-002: Navigate queue (Previous, Next, Skip) ✅ TC-CH-003: Queue search by account name ✅ TC-CH-004: Queue search by WhatsApp number ✅ TC-CH-005: Save import mode (Full/Whitelist/Exclude) ✅ TC-CH-006: Edit import mode after connection ✅ TC-CH-007: Concurrent queue access (race condition) ✅ TC-CH-008: Queue session persistence after popup close Data Migration Tests: ✅ TC-CH-100: Existing accounts without import_mode → "Belum diatur" ✅ TC-CH-101: Old connected accounts → backward compatibility ``` #### **WHATSAPP SERVICE** (WhatsApp Connector) ``` Priority: P0 Test Scenarios: ✅ TC-WA-001: QR generation per queue item ✅ TC-WA-002: QR auto-refresh on expiry ✅ TC-WA-003: Public link generation (10-min expiry) ✅ TC-WA-004: Public link access after expiry → regenerate ✅ TC-WA-005: Post-connect trigger for restricted modes ✅ TC-WA-006: Account already connected by other user ✅ TC-WA-007: QR scan while queue item skipped ✅ TC-WA-008: Success state → Next queue item Performance Tests: ✅ TC-WA-100: QR load under 2 seconds (P95) ``` #### **CONVERSATION SERVICE** (Chat/Thread) ``` Priority: P0 Test Scenarios: ✅ TC-CV-001: Full Import → All chats imported ✅ TC-CV-002: Whitelist Only → Only selected imported ✅ TC-CV-003: Exclude Conversations → All except selected imported ✅ TC-CV-004: Whitelist → Non-selected chat ignored ✅ TC-CV-005: Exclude → Excluded chat ignored ✅ TC-CV-006: Mode change → Future events only affected ✅ TC-CV-007: History import within 60s (P95) ✅ TC-CV-008: Deduplication by event_id ✅ TC-CV-009: Ignored counter increment ✅ TC-CV-010: Message content NOT stored for ignored Group Chat Tests: ✅ TC-CV-100: Group chat in Whitelist → imported ✅ TC-CV-101: Group chat in Exclude → ignored ``` #### **PEOPLE SERVICE** (Client Contact) ``` Priority: P1 Test Scenarios: ✅ TC-PL-001: Target normalization (phone number) ✅ TC-PL-002: Group identifier normalization ✅ TC-PL-003: Duplicate target prevention ✅ TC-PL-004: Search by number ✅ TC-PL-005: Search by contact name ✅ TC-PL-006: Search by conversation title ✅ TC-PL-007: Search by visible text ✅ TC-PL-008: Max 5,000 targets validation ✅ TC-PL-009: Min 1 target validation (restricted modes) ``` #### **COMPANY SERVICE** (Client Data) ``` Priority: P1 Test Scenarios: ✅ TC-CY-001: Audit log on connect success ✅ TC-CY-002: Audit log on connect failure ✅ TC-CY-003: Audit log on skip ✅ TC-CY-004: Audit log on public link generation ✅ TC-CY-005: Audit log on mode update ✅ TC-CY-006: Audit log on whitelist save ✅ TC-CY-007: Audit log on exclude save ✅ TC-CY-008: Target masking in logs ✅ TC-CY-009: Encryption at rest for targets ``` --- ### ⚠️ Risk Areas for QA ``` HIGH RISK: 1. Data Migration • Existing accounts tanpa import_mode • Backward compatibility dengan old connect flow • Migration script testing required 2. Concurrent Access • Two users accessing same queue item • QR scan race condition • Mode change during import 3. Performance • 60s P95 for history import • 5,000 targets per account limit • Queue search response time MEDIUM RISK: 4. State Management • Queue session persistence • Popup close → reopen behavior • Skip → Revisit flow 5. Import Logic • Mode change tidak retroactive • Ignored counter accuracy • Deduplication logic ``` --- ### 📝 Test Data Requirements ``` Test Accounts Needed: • 50+ not-connected WhatsApp accounts untuk queue testing • 10+ already-connected accounts untuk negative testing • Accounts dengan berbagai status: pending, skipped, connected, failed Test Conversations Needed: • Personal chats (direct messages) • Group chats (various sizes) • Mixed content types (text, media, documents) • 5,000+ targets untuk boundary testing Configuration Data: • Import modes: Full Import, Whitelist Only, Exclude Conversations • Queue session dengan berbagai state combinations • Audit log baseline untuk comparison ``` --- ### 🔗 Related Work Packages to Test Together ``` Related WP dari Relations: • #431 - RBAC Sales (relates to) • #504 - Modul Sales - Web (relates to) • #487 - Contacts Module (relates to) Integration Testing Required: • RBAC permissions untuk queue actions • Sales module integration dengan WhatsApp connect • Contact module integration untuk target selection ``` --- ### ✅ Definition of Ready for QA ``` Before testing can begin: ☐ PRD reviewed and approved ☐ Figma designs finalized ☐ API specifications documented ☐ Test environment provisioned ☐ Test data prepared ☐ Migration scripts tested (if applicable) ☐ Related WP tested and stable ``` ### ✅ Definition of Done for QA ``` Before sign-off: ☐ All P0 test cases executed and passed ☐ All P1 test cases executed (80%+ pass rate) ☐ Regression testing completed ☐ Performance benchmarks met (QR < 2s, Import < 60s) ☐ Security testing passed (encryption, audit logs) ☐ Data migration validated (if applicable) ☐ Documentation updated ☐ Sign-off from stakeholders ``` --- **Analyst:** QA Team **Date:** 2026-05-04 **Version:** 1.0

allWorkPackages.subject: Broadcast Message View Session-scoped Access Control
allWorkPackages.description:
Contoh user tersebut hanya punya akses di team inbox A saja maka hanya bisa lihat spesifik broadcast inbox a saja.

PRD: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1H3r4OCqQUd9cmSZtkEVHqjcMFtXlF4xGeH6\_Z4eE0/edit?tab=t.crw8p2ejed1d](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i1H3r4OCqQUd9cmSZtkEVHqjcMFtXlF4xGeH6_Z4eE0/edit?tab=t.crw8p2ejed1d) 

### **Minimum requirement (server-side enforced)**

**Define:** `**userAccessSession**`

*   Computed saat login / token issued:
    
    *   `role` (Admin/Supervisor/Agent)
        
    *   `allowedTeamInboxIds: string[] | "*"`
        
    *   (optional) `allowedSenderAccountIds: string[]` kalau aksesnya by account bukan by team inbox
        

### **Validation rules**

1.  **List rows filtering (hard security)**
    
    *   API MUST filter out rows yang user tidak punya aksesnya.
        
    *   Rule:
        
        *   If `allowedTeamInboxIds == "*"`, user can view all (including `null` rows).
            
        *   Else:
            
            *   user can view rows where `teamInboxIdAtSendTime in allowedTeamInboxIds`
                
            *   rows `teamInboxIdAtSendTime = null`:
                
                *   **Option A (safer default):** hidden (karena unassigned → raw number exposure risk)
                    
                *   **Option B (if needed ops):** visible only if user has a specific permission flag `canViewUnassignedBroadcasts = true`
                    
2.  **Detail panel access**
    
    *   `GET /broadcast/history/{id}` MUST re-check permission using the same session rules.
        
    *   If not allowed → return `403` (or `404` to avoid enumeration; pilih salah satu dan konsisten).
        
3.  **Filter options scoping (UX + security)**
    
    *   Team Inbox dropdown hanya menampilkan team inbox yang ada di `allowedTeamInboxIds` (kecuali `"*"`).
        
    *   If user manually inject `teamInboxId` query param yang bukan miliknya:
        
        *   API returns empty list (or 403). Minimum: empty list is fine, but 403 is clearer for debugging.

allWorkPackages.subject: Improve WA API Account Status if Disabled
allWorkPackages.description:
Handle WA API/ Instagram API dan Messenger API (META API) saat kondisi Account status disabled dan suspend. Memberikan notice kepada user.

## 1) Tujuan & Prinsip

*   **Prevent silent failure**: kalau channel “mati”, user harus tahu + sistem stop action yang pasti gagal.
    
*   **Single source of truth**: simpan `connection_status` per channel account.
    
*   **Detect via 2 jalur**:
    
    1.  **Real-time signals** (webhook/event) — terutama WhatsApp punya `account_update` webhook.
        
    2.  **Runtime errors** dari API calls (send/reply/fetch) — map ke kategori status.
        

## 2) Status Model (minimal)

**Entity:** `channel_connection`

*   `id`
    
*   `tenant_id`
    
*   `channel_type`: `WHATSAPP_CLOUD | INSTAGRAM | MESSENGER`
    
*   `provider`: `META`
    
*   `connection_status`: `ACTIVE | DEGRADED | RESTRICTED | DISABLED`
    
*   `status_reason_code`: string (provider code/subcode)
    
*   `status_reason_category`:
    
    *   `POLICY_ENFORCEMENT` (restricted/disabled karena policy)
        
    *   `TOKEN_INVALID` (expired/invalid)
        
    *   `PERMISSION_REVOKED` (missing permission/advanced access)
        
    *   `ASSET_DISABLED` (Page/IG Professional account unpublished/disabled)
        
    *   `UNKNOWN`
        
*   `status_message` (safe text)
    
*   `last_success_at`, `last_error_at`
    
*   `last_error_fingerprint` (hash: endpoint+code+subcode)
    
*   `next_healthcheck_at`
    

> Pattern internal Satuinbox: error handling harus **log + show banner/inline + optionally block action** (lihat EH patterns).
> 
> PRD

## 3) Detection Rules (by channel)

### A) WhatsApp Cloud API

**Signal 1**

*   Subscribe `account_update` untuk policy/spam enforcement & status changes.   
    **Handling:**
    
*   On event receive:
    
    *   set `connection_status = RESTRICTED` atau `DISABLED` sesuai payload
        
    *   store `restriction_type`, `expires_at` jika ada
        
    *   trigger in-app notice + notify Admin
        

**Signal 2 — API error 403/4xx saat send**

*   Banyak provider implementasi melihat “restricted/disabled” muncul sebagai **403 Forbidden** dengan integrity/policy error. (Contoh referensi partner docs: WABA restricted/disabled)   
    **Handling:**
    
*   Map ke `POLICY_ENFORCEMENT`, set `RESTRICTED/DISABLED` (bergantung message).
    
*   Stop retry agresif (lihat Retry section).
    

> Catatan: Meta punya halaman error codes WhatsApp, tapi akses fetch sering rate-limited di sini; implementasi sebaiknya **tidak hardcode** 1–2 code saja—buat mapping configurable.

### B) Messenger API (Facebook Page messaging)

**Primary signal — Graph/Messenger error codes**

*   Messenger punya daftar error codes (umum: permission/token).
    
*   Graph API guidance: handle error token invalid/expired, permission errors.
    

**Minimal mapping yang wajib:**

*   `code=190` (Access Token invalid/expired) ⇒ `TOKEN_INVALID` ⇒ `DISABLED` sampai reconnect.
    
*   `code=10 / 200–299` (permission) ⇒ `PERMISSION_REVOKED` ⇒ `DISABLED` (but may recover after app review/role fix).
    
*   `code=368` (temporarily blocked / abusive) ⇒ `POLICY_ENFORCEMENT` ⇒ `RESTRICTED` (set cooldown).
    

### C) Instagram Messaging API (IG Professional messaging via Meta)

*   Instagram messaging docs ada requirement & endpoint untuk send/reply.   
    **Deteksi utamanya tetap dari Graph error codes** (token/perms/policy) sama seperti Messenger:
    
*   `190` token invalid ⇒ `TOKEN_INVALID`
    
*   permission error ⇒ `PERMISSION_REVOKED`
    
*   `368` temporary block ⇒ `RESTRICTED`
    

## 4) Runtime Handling (behavior saat status RESTRICTED/DISABLED)

### A) Saat user melakukan action (send/reply/assign template/broadcast)

*   Jika `connection_status in (RESTRICTED, DISABLED)`:
    
    *   **Block** action yang pasti gagal
        
    *   tampilkan **blocking inline error** + CTA “Reconnect / Fix”
        
    *   action yang aman: view history/inbox tetap jalan
        

(Sejalan dengan pola “block send + keep config” di error handling internal).

PRD

### B) Saat sistem auto-send (automation/broadcast)

*   Stop job untuk channel tersebut:
    
    *   mark item: `FAILED_PROVIDER_DISABLED` (bukan retry loop)
        
    *   surface summary di campaign/job detail
        

### C) Inbound messages

*   Jika connection disabled, inbound umumnya juga berhenti.
    
*   UI harus show banner: “Channel disconnected” + last seen inbound time.
    

## 5) Notice / UX Requirements (minimal)

**Placement**

*   Channel settings page (Account detail): status chip + reason + last\_error\_at
    
*   Inbox top banner untuk Admin/Supervisor (optional untuk Agent)
    
*   Conversation composer: disable send button + tooltip [Design](https://www.figma.com/design/RAAuLaQKUufWMWWEm0kMb9/-V2--Satuinbox-Web-Specs?node-id=1485-75865&t=on8e6DovB4Fv6BmF-11)
    

**Copy (ID)**

*   `POLICY_ENFORCEMENT`:
    
    *   “Channel dinonaktifkan/dibatasi oleh Meta karena kebijakan. Silakan lakukan review di Meta Business Manager atau hubungi provider.”
        
*   `TOKEN_INVALID`:
    
    *   “Koneksi kedaluwarsa. Silakan reconnect.”
        
*   `PERMISSION_REVOKED`:
    
    *   “Izin aplikasi tidak mencukupi. Periksa permissions & akses aplikasi di Meta D
        
        PRD
        
        ion\*\*
        
*   In-app notif untuk Admin + (optional) email ops.
    

## 6) Retry & Health Check Policy (anti over-engineering)

**Retry rules**

*   `TOKEN_INVALID / PERMISSION_REVOKED / POLICY_ENFORCEMENT`:
    
    *   **No immediate retry loop** (will spam & rate limit). Set `connection_status` + stop.
        
*   `Transient` (5xx, timeouts, “service unavailable”):
    
    *   exponential backoff retry (max N=3) lalu set `DEGRADED`.
        

**Health check**

*   Cron ringan per connection (mis. tiap 30–60 menit):
    
    *   call cheap endpoint (me/accounts / debug\_token / status endpoint)
        
    *   jika sukses ⇒ clear `DEGRADED` dan update `last_success_at`
        
    *   jika fail dengan kategori above ⇒ flip status
        

(Sejalan prinsip “log + retry limited + do not block UX” untuk internal failures).

PRD

## 7) Observability & Audit (wajib minimal)

*   Log event:
    
    *   `tenant_id, channel_connection_id, endpoint, http_status, code, subcode, request_id, timestamp`
        
*   Dedup:
    
    *   jika `last_error_fingerprint` sama dalam window (mis. 10 menit), jangan spam notif.
        
*   Audit status changes:
    
    *   record old/new + source (`WEBHOOK | API_ERROR | HEALTHCHECK | MANUAL`)  
        (Internal precedent: audit logging untuk state changes).
        
        PRD
        

## 8) Edge Cases yang sering kejadian

*   Token valid tapi **asset disabled** (Page unpublished / IG disconnected) ⇒ tetap treat as `ASSET_DISABLED`.
    
*   Partial outage Meta: jangan flip ke DISABLED; gunakan `DEGRADED` dengan retry.
    
*   Multiple connections (1 tenant punya banyak WA numbers / Pages): status per connection, bukan global.

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation Room - timestamp - message timestamp
allWorkPackages.description:
**Jamdev :**

**Description :**

### Message Timestamp & Date Indicator Behavior

1.  **Message Bubble Timestamp**
    
    *   Each message bubble must display the **time the message was created**.
        
    *   Time format should be consistent across the application (e.g. `HH:mm`).
        
2.  **Sticky Date Indicator (Per Room)**
    
    *   A **date indicator** must be displayed at the **top of the conversation room** whenever the room is opened.
        
    *   This indicator shows the **current message date context** (e.g. _Today_, _Yesterday_, or a full date).
        
    *   The indicator must **remain sticky** at the top while the user scrolls within the conversation.
        
3.  **Dynamic Date Update on Scroll**
    
    *   As the user scrolls through the conversation:
        
        *   When the viewport reaches messages from a **different date**, the date indicator must **update dynamically** to reflect that date.
            
        *   The indicator must always represent the **date of the messages currently in view**.
            
4.  **Date Separator Between Messages**
    
    *   A **date separator** must appear **between messages that belong to different dates**.
        
    *   The separator visually divides message groups by day (e.g. _Jan 20, 2026_).
        
    *   Messages within the same day **must not** display repeated date separators.
        
5.  **Intraday Message Grouping**
    
    *   Within the same day:
        
        *   Messages are grouped continuously.
            
        *   Only individual message timestamps are shown.
            
        *   No additional date separators are displayed.
            

### Summary Behavior Flow

*   **Bubble** → shows time only
    
*   **Separator** → appears when date changes
    
*   **Sticky indicator** → reflects currently visible message date
    
*   **Per room** → indicator resets when opening a different room
    

This specification ensures clarity, consistency, and predictable UX behavior for message timelines.

Kalau mau nonaktif, user tinggal delete rule. ## 2) Create / Edit Rule (form) ### Field definitions (urutannya dibuat gampang dipahami) ## Match style (bahasa manusia) ## Rules behavior (simple + predictable) * **Auto-add tag** saat ada message baru sesuai **Source** & **Scan content**. * **No duplicate**: kalau tag sudah ada di scope target → **skip** (tidak apply ulang). * **Tag Scope = Ticket**: * Kalau ticket sudah ada → apply ke ticket. * Kalau ticket belum ada → apply ke conversation dulu; **saat ticket dibuat dari conversation → copy tags** (biar tidak hilang). ## Validasi kecil biar gak bikin ribet * **Scan content** tidak muncul kalau **Source = Customer only**. * **Tags to apply** filter berdasarkan **Tag Scope**: * Scope `Ticket` → hanya tag yang usable untuk Ticket/All * Scope `Conversation` → hanya tag yang usable untuk Conversation/All

QA NOTES :
# 🔥 1. Core Domain Impact (Paling Besar) ## A. Ticket Service **Kena langsung karena trigger utama** ### Dampak: * Event baru: `TICKET_RESOLVED` * Harus emit event yang **reliable & idempotent** * Tambahan dependency: * ticket\_type * custom fields * resolved\_at timestamp (harus akurat) ### Risiko: * Double trigger saat reopen → resolve lagi 👉 mitigasi: idempotency key (`tenant_id + automation_id + ticket_id`) ## B. Conversation Service **Paralel dengan ticket** ### Dampak: * Event baru: `CONVERSATION_CLOSED` * Data tambahan: * custom attributes (`ca.*`) * conversation\_id mapping ke channel ### Risiko: * Reopen → close lagi (sama seperti ticket) # 🧠 2. Automation Engine (NEW SERVICE / EXTENSION) Ini **jantung fitur**. ### Komponen baru: * Automation config storage * Scheduler (delay) * Executor (send engine) * Idempotency guard ### Dampak teknis: * Harus support: * delay (0–10080 menit) * retry policy (1m, 5m, 15m) * skip logic (channel, invalid recipient, dll) ### Risiko: * Race condition: * CSAT submit vs send time * Config berubah setelah scheduling 👉 PRD sudah handle: > “use latest config at send time” → ini penting banget # 📡 3. Notification / Messaging Service ## A. Email Gateway ### Dampak: * Template rendering * Subject fallback logic * Email validation ## B. WhatsApp (Official + Web) ### Dampak besar: * Cost awareness (UX + backend flag) * Template constraint (WA Official) * Message logging ke conversation ### Risiko: * WA template reject * Cost spike (spam automation) # 🧩 4. Data Layer Impact ## A. New Tables / Collections Minimal: ### Automation Config, notification config, CSAT
## B. Idempotency Store Critical untuk: * duplicate prevention * retry safety # 🔗 5. Tokenization & Security Layer ## Dampak besar (sering underrated) ### CSAT & Survey Token * Opaque token (bukan ID) * Payload besar (PII + metadata) ### Harus ada: * encryption / signing * expiration handling * tenant isolation ### Risiko: * token leak → data exposure * replay attack # 📊 6. Analytics & Observability ## Event tracking baru: * scheduled * sent * skipped (+ reason) * failed * link opened * survey submitted ### Dampak: * Logging pipeline harus siap high volume * QA harus test: * skip reason coverage (target 100%) # 🧪 7. QA / Testing Impact (Paling Kompleks) ## A. State Explosion Kombinasi utama: Automation: \- enabled / disabled Entity: \- ticket / conversation Channel: \- included / excluded Recipient: \- valid / invalid / missing Delay: \- 0 / N CSAT: \- enabled / submitted / not submitted Post-survey: \- enabled / submitted / not submitted
👉 Ini jadi **matrix test besar banget** ## B. Critical Test Area ### 1\. Idempotency * double resolve → 1 notif * retry → no duplicate ### 2\. Scheduling Accuracy * delay = 0 * delay = N * config change after schedule ### 3\. Rendering * missing variable * invalid variable * cf hidden vs shown ### 4\. Skip Logic * invalid phone/email * missing mapping * excluded channel # 🧱 8. UI / Frontend Impact ## Wizard Complexity (deceptively simple) ### Dampak: * dynamic form: * ticket vs conversation * cf vs ca * conditional validation * variable picker logic ### Risiko: * invalid config lolos ke backend * UX confusion (non-technical admin target!) # 🔄 9. Cross-Service Contract Impact Ini penting buat regression. ## Affected services: * Ticket Service * Conversation Service * People Service (agent info) * Auth Service (permission) * Notification Service * WhatsApp Integration * Email Service ### Contract baru: * event payload harus lengkap: entity\_id entity\_type channel customer data agent data timestamps
# ⚠️ 10. High-Risk Areas (Prioritas QA & Dev) ## 1\. Idempotency Kalau gagal → spam notif ## 2\. Recipient Mapping Dynamic schema → rawan null / invalid ## 3\. Token Security Leak = critical incident ## 4\. WhatsApp Integration * cost * template compliance ## 5\. Timing Issues * CSAT submit sebelum send * config berubah # 🧭 11. Dampak ke Arsitektur (Summary) Fitur ini bikin sistem berubah dari: > “passive messaging” jadi: > **event-driven automation system** ### Tambahan layer: * Event → Automation → Scheduler → Sender → Tracking # 🧩 12. Quick Impact Map **Paling terdampak:** * Automation Engine (NEW) * Ticket & Conversation lifecycle * Notification pipeline **Medium:** * UI wizard * Data model * Analytics **Critical Risk:** * idempotency * token security * WA cost & delivery # 🚀 Insight (yang biasanya kelewat) 1. Ini bukan cuma notif — ini **foundation automation platform** 2. Future scope (trigger lain) bakal reuse engine ini 3. Kalau salah design sekarang → technical debt besar nanti

allWorkPackages.subject: Conversation : Add attachment on Internal Notes
allWorkPackages.description: ## Minimum Requirements ### 1) Limits & Validation (hard rules) * **Max files per message/reply:** `10` * **Max total size per message/reply:** `20MB` * **Max size per file:** `5MB` * Validation dilakukan **client-side + server-side** * Jika melanggar: * Per-file: show error “File exceeds 5MB” * Total: show error “Total attachments exceed 20MB” * Count: show error “Max 10 attachments” ### 2) Allowed File Types (Docs + Media only) Use MIME allowlist (block everything else). Explicitly **disallow**: executable/script (`.exe .apk .js .sh .bat`), archives (`.zip .rar .7z`) (lean: reduce risk surface). ### 3) UX: Upload in Composer (Conversation + Ticket) * Add **Attach button** (paperclip) in composer. * Multi-select files. * After selecting: * Show **attachment chips/list**: filename + size + type icon * **Per-file progress bar** * Actions per file: **Remove**, **Retry** (if failed) * **Send button disabled** jika ada attachment masih `uploading` atau `failed`. * If user removes failed file → Send allowed (as long as remaining valid). ### 4) Message Rendering (Timeline) For both Conversation timeline & Ticket timeline: * Each attachment bubble shows: * **Filename** * **Size** * **Download** action * Preview rules: * Images: thumbnail preview * PDF: thumbnail/first-page preview (optional MVP: icon only) * Others: icon only ### 5) Download & Access Control (must-have) * Attachment must be **downloadable only** by users who have access to the **same Team Inbox / entity permission** as the conversation/ticket. * No public static URL: * Use **short-TTL signed URL** (or equivalent private download mechanism). * If user loses access (removed from Team Inbox / role change): * Download returns **403/Not allowed** (show friendly error). ### 6) Security & Storage Behavior (no API detail, but required behavior) * Store files in **private object storage**. * Persist metadata minimally: * `entity_type` (conversation/ticket), `entity_id`, `message_id/comment_id` * `uploader_user_id` * `file_name`, `mime_type`, `size_bytes` * `created_at` * Anti-abuse: * Server re-check `mime_type` + actual file signature (basic sniff) to prevent spoofing. * Cleanup: * Orphan uploads (uploaded but never attached to a sent message) auto-delete after X hours (suggest `24h`). ### 7) QA Acceptance Checklist (DoD) * ✅ Upload 1–10 files; each ≤5MB; total ≤20MB → success. * ✅ Any file >5MB → blocked with per-file error. * ✅ Total >20MB → blocked with total error. * ✅ Unsupported type (e.g., `.zip`, `.exe`) → blocked with clear error. * ✅ Partial failure: 1 file fails upload → Send disabled until retry/remove. * ✅ Download works for authorized user; blocked for unauthorized user (403). * ✅ Rendering: image thumbnail displayed; non-image shows icon + name + size.

QA NOTES :
Ini bukan sekadar “fitur mention”, tapi menyentuh banyak layer sistem: **real-time, authorization, notification engine, UX sorting, dan data model**. Kalau dilihat end-to-end, impact-nya cukup luas. # 🔍 1. Impact ke Architecture (Core System) ## 🧠 A. Data Model & Storage Akan ada perubahan signifikan di struktur data: * **Mention Token (structured)** * Tidak bisa hanya plain text `"@nama"` * Harus simpan: * `userId` * `displayName` * `entityId` (conversation/ticket/note) * `sourceType` (message / note / ticket) * **Notification Entity** * Tambahan field: * `sourceId` (conversationId / ticketId) * `sourceType` * `actorId` * `excerpt` (≤140 char) * `dedupeKey` (untuk FR-051, retry 60 detik) * **Mention Indexing** * Untuk fitur **Sort by Mentions** * Kemungkinan perlu: * `lastMentionAt` * `isMentioned` (per user, bukan global) 👉 Impact: **perlu migration + indexing baru (high impact ke DB performance)** ## ⚡ B. Real-time Layer (Socket/Event System) Mention → harus trigger: * Socket event ke: * mentioned users * team inbox (untuk badge) * Event types baru: * `mention.created` * `notification.created` Edge case: * dedupe (FR-051) * multiple mentions dalam 1 note (FR-038) 👉 Impact: * Load ke websocket meningkat * Harus handle **fan-out (1 → banyak user)** ## 🔐 C. Authorization Layer (Critical) Mention tidak bisa asal notify: * Check: * access ke conversation/ticket (FR-048, FR-049) * eligibility (FR-040) * Special flow: * user belum punya akses → prompt assign (FR-042) 👉 Impact: * Mention flow jadi **stateful + conditional** * Bergantung ke: * RBAC * assignment service ⚠️ Ini titik rawan bug: * mention terkirim tapi user tidak bisa buka entity * atau sebaliknya # 🧩 2. Impact ke Feature Behavior ## 💬 A. Conversation Notes (FR-14) * Tambah capability: * create / edit / pin * mention agents * Role restriction: * Supervisor/Admin bisa mention 👉 Impact: * UI editor harus support: * mention picker * token rendering * Backend: * parsing mention sebelum save ## 👥 B. Team Mention (US-8) * `"@TeamInboxName"` → broadcast ke semua member Edge case: * team tidak valid → error * member banyak → performance issue 👉 Impact: * Expand mention jadi **N users** * Risk: * notification spam * socket burst ## 📊 C. Conversation List Sorting (US-15) Sorting baru: * Mentions * Reminder * Longest Waiting 👉 Impact: * Query complexity naik * Harus: * persist di session * combine dengan pagination ⚠️ Potensi issue: * sorting by mention but data async (socket update) * race condition antara: * real-time update vs user sorting ## 🔔 D. Notification System (US-001 + FR-009) Behavior penting: * 1 mention → 1 notification (dedupe) * multiple mention dalam 1 source → tetap 1 * retry → tidak duplicate (60 detik window) 👉 Impact: * Harus ada: * **idempotency mechanism** * kemungkinan pakai: * hash(sourceId + userId) # 🧪 3. Impact ke Testing (High Complexity) Ini fitur dengan **high combinatorial cases**: ## 🎯 A. Dimension yang harus di-cover * Entity type: * conversation * ticket * internal note * User state: * has access / no access * assigned / unassigned * Mention type: * single user * multiple user * team mention * Condition: * retry request * socket delay * permission denied ## 🧨 B. Critical Edge Cases 1. Mention user tanpa akses → tidak boleh notify 2. Mention + assign success → notify 3. Mention + assign gagal → tidak boleh insert token 4. Duplicate mention dalam 1 note → 1 notif 5. Retry API → tidak duplicate notif 6. Sort by mention + real-time update 7. Mention saat agent offline → notif tetap ada 👉 Impact: * Test matrix besar * Cypress: * perlu mock socket + API * race condition testing # ⚙️ 4. Performance & Scalability Impact ## 🚨 High Risk Areas ### 1\. Team Mention * 1 action → N notifications + N socket emit * jika team besar (50–100 agent): * spike event ### 2\. Sorting by Mention * query lebih berat: * join / aggregation per user ### 3\. Notification Deduplication * perlu cache / TTL (60 detik) # 🧱 5. Dependency Impact Fitur ini bergantung ke banyak modul: * RBAC / Permission * Assignment system * Notification service * Socket service * Conversation & Ticket module * UI Editor (mention picker) 👉 Artinya: * perubahan kecil bisa ripple ke banyak tempat # 🧭 6. Risk Summary ## 🔴 High Risk * Authorization inconsistency * Duplicate notification * Socket overload (team mention) * Sorting inconsistency (real-time vs query) ## 🟡 Medium Risk * UX confusion (mention tapi tidak bisa akses) * Assign flow gagal ## 🟢 Low Risk * UI rendering mention # 💡 7. Strategic Insight (Forward-looking) Fitur ini sebenarnya adalah fondasi ke: * **Collaboration layer (Slack-like behavior)** * **Priority routing (mention = urgency signal)** * **Automation trigger (future: mention → workflow)** Kalau didesain rapi: * bisa extend ke: * escalation * SLA priority boost * AI triaging # ✅ Kesimpulan Impact task ini **besar dan lintas sistem**: * **Backend**: data model, notification, auth, dedupe * **Frontend**: editor, sorting, real-time UI * **Infra**: socket scaling * **QA**: combinatorial explosion 👉 Ini bukan “fitur kecil”, tapi **core collaboration capability** yang akan mempengaruhi hampir semua flow conversation & ticketing.

allWorkPackages.subject: Open API broadcast sender can resolve inactive account channel when phone number is duplicated
allWorkPackages.description: ## Summary When sending a broadcast via open API using `sender` as a phone number string, the broadcast service resolves the sender through `getAccountChannelByPhone`. The current lookup only matches by `phoneNumber` and tenant scope, without ensuring the returned `AccountChannel` is active. ## Problem If multiple account channels share the same phone number in the same tenant, MongoDB can return an inactive or suspended channel first. This makes open API broadcast use the wrong sender even though an active channel exists. ## Current behavior * Open API broadcast forwards `sender` as a string number * Broadcast service calls `getAccountChannelByPhone` * Channel service filters by phone regex and tenant scope only * Broadcast service validates platform and phone number, but not `connectionStatus` ## Expected behavior Open API broadcast should only accept an `AccountChannel` with `connectionStatus = active` when resolving sender by phone number. Inactive or suspended channels must not be selected. ## Notes * Bulk broadcast import already checks for active account channels * Team inbox sender resolution already filters active WhatsApp channels * The gap is specific to sender lookup by phone number in the open API broadcast flow ## Suggested fix Apply active-channel validation in the broadcast service sender resolution path and add regression coverage for duplicated phone numbers with inactive channels. ENV test : * dev : [https://qa.satuinbox.dev/s/OCp2PoVr0-tm](https://qa.satuinbox.dev/s/OCp2PoVr0-tm)

allWorkPackages.subject: Account channel event log (REDASH)
allWorkPackages.description: # Product Requirement Document (PRD) **Feature:** Account Channel Event Log for WhatsApp Web **Version:** v1.4 **Scope:** Settings -> Channels -> WhatsApp Web, per-account lifecycle event log ## 1\. Overview Account Channel Event Log provides an immutable lifecycle timeline for WhatsApp Web account channels so Admin and Supervisor can investigate account creation, initialization, restore attempts, QR scan, connection, disconnection, suspension, and per-session active lifetime. ## 2\. Events `CREATED`, `INIT`, `RE_INIT`, `SCAN`, `CONNECTED`, `DISCONNECTED`, `SUSPENDED`. `LIFETIME` is not an event. Phase 1 lifetime is per-session only: start at `CONNECTED`, end at `DISCONNECTED` for the same connection session. Suspend while connected emits `DISCONNECTED(reason=AUTO_SUSPEND)` before `SUSPENDED`. ## 3\. User Stories and Acceptance Criteria ## 4\. Functional Requirements * Record lifecycle events: `CREATED`, `INIT`, `RE_INIT`, `SCAN`, `CONNECTED`, `DISCONNECTED`, `SUSPENDED`. * `SCAN` only when technically confirmed; QR refresh never emits `SCAN`. * `RE_INIT` only for restore attempts using stored credentials without QR/pairing and must not emit `SCAN`. * Every event includes tenant scope, account id, event type, occurrence time, actor, source service, and idempotency key. * `CONNECTED` creates `connectionSessionId`; `DISCONNECTED` reuses it and stores `durationMs` when available. * Admin sees company/org logs; Supervisor is server-side scoped by Team Inbox; Agent denied. * Event write is async and non-blocking. * Duplicate `DISCONNECTED` dedup window default 5s via `ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_DISCONNECT_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS`. * Duplicate `CONNECTED` is skipped before RMQ emit if active session exists. * TTL retention disabled until PM/Legal approval. * Only allowlisted metadata keys are stored. ## 5\. Connection Session Architecture * `connectionSessionId` is generated and owned by `whatsapp-service`. * Active session key: `evt:session:{accountChannelId}` with `{ connectionSessionId, connectedAt }`. * Default active session TTL: 7 days via `ACCOUNT_CHANNEL_ACTIVE_SESSION_TTL_MS`. * `RE_INIT` marks restore attempt and does not create session; session is created only on `CONNECTED`. * Missing session key on disconnect creates orphan `DISCONNECTED` with `metadata.orphan = true`. * Stale session recovery emits orphan `DISCONNECTED`, deletes stale key, then creates new session. * Suspend while connected emits `DISCONNECTED(AUTO_SUSPEND)` then `SUSPENDED`. ## 6\. Idempotency Key Format ## 7\. Open Questions
